guide/src/content/docs/administer/client:
---
title: Clients for other systems
description: Give a system its own identity, grant its access and manage its secrets.
reader: access-admin
---

A **client** is the identity of a system that calls refiroo without a person signing in.
Use one for an unattended import, a data consumer, a monitoring system or another integration.
Its work carries its own name in history. People using the browser sign in as themselves.

You need **Security administration** to manage **Settings › Connections › Clients**.
Use **Search clients** (**Name**) to search the list, which separates **Active** and **Deactivated** clients and shows
when a client last authenticated, or **No token yet** when it has not.

![Clients catalogue with one active client and no selection](/docs/screens/admin-clients.png)

*Above: Stops reader (guide) is the reference instance's client for reading stop data.*

## Identity and access

A client has a stable **Client ID**, a display name and a secret. Select the name where it stands, edit it, then leave the field or press Enter to save.
Escape puts the old name back; an unchanged input saves nothing. The save notice offers **Undo**.
If refused, the input stays open with the reason and **Cancel** and **Save again** beneath it. Its ID stays the same, so the connected system needs no new configuration. **New client** asks for **Name**. **Add client** opens **Copy the client's secret**. Store the ID and secret securely before **I have copied it**; the secret is shown once. A new client starts
with no access. Follow [Create a client](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-client/) to create
it, save its one-time secret and grant what it needs.

![Client detail with ID, secrets and a workspace consumer grant](/docs/screens/admin-client.png)

*Above: Stops reader (guide) has a Consumer API grant in Graubünden. The webhooks section
shows a load error on this capture; it does not show that the client has no webhooks.*

A **Role** grant permits management operations, using the same roles and write restrictions
as people. A **Consumer API** grant permits reading one declared API in one workspace.
Both kinds can be needed. A role alone, even Security administrator, does not grant consumer
data access. Consumer grants must be made separately for each API and workspace.

The **Access** table shows where each grant applies and any write restriction. **Grant**
opens the access dialog. **Remove** takes away that grant; any other applicable grants
continue. If the model removes a granted consumer API, the stale grant no longer permits
access. Replace it with a grant for the intended current API.

Follow [Grant a consumer API to a client](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/) for the grid and its partial-success handling. Give the integration team the ID, secret and agreed access. The
[integration authentication guide](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/) describes how their system signs in
and uses the granted interfaces.

## Secrets and rotation

The full secret is shown only when created. Copy it before closing the dialog; the client
page later identifies it by its last four characters. The **Secrets** table shows **Secret**, **Created**,
**Valid until** and **Last used**. **No end** means no expiry is currently set; **Not yet**
means the secret has not been used.

**Rotate secret…** opens **Rotate the secret of …**. **Rotate secret** makes the replacement with a chosen overlap: **1 hour**, **24 hours**,
**7 days**, or **Stop it now**. During an overlap the system can switch without interruption;
after it, the previous secret no longer works. **End now** in the Secrets table ends a
previous secret's overlap early. Its accessible label, **End the secret ending … now**, identifies the last four characters; it acts immediately. **No valid secret: rotate to make one.** means there is no usable secret left. Use the recorded ending and last-use times to check the handover.
Follow [Rotate a client secret](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-client-secret/).

## Ending access and tracing work

**Deactivate** asks for confirmation. The client cannot authenticate again and its existing
access is refused at the next request. Its grants and name remain for history. It is never
deleted. Use **Restore** from the Deactivated list to reactivate it after reviewing those grants.

**See changes** opens its data changes in workspaces you may read. **Recent activity**
shows security events; **Webhooks it created** lists subscriptions you administer.
A failed section offers **Retry**. Treat a load failure as unavailable information, not an empty list.
See [Who changed what](/docs/administer/audit/) for the distinction between data and security history.

Consumer API grants are for clients only. People use their browser roles to read records;
there is no corresponding grant to a person. In the Grant dialog, choose the consumer APIs
and workspaces in the grid, check the existing grants and confirm the intended additions.
The available APIs come from each workspace's own model.

The client’s header identifies who created it. **Webhooks it created** lists **Webhook**, **Workspace**, **Consumer API** and **State** for someone who also administers those subscriptions; it is not a grant of webhook management. Follow a webhook to its [configuration and deliveries](/docs/administer/webhooks/).

**Recent activity** has **All**, **Signing in**, **Roles and groups** and **Account** filters, grouped by day. It starts with ten entries, then loads twenty more, with **Show fewer** to shorten the list. Its security events contain no secret. Data changes remain in **See changes**, limited to workspaces the viewer may read.

Rotation and ending an old secret stop that secret being used for a new sign-in. They do not themselves cancel access already issued. For immediate refusal of an unsafe client’s requests, **Deactivate** is the relevant action. Check retained grants before **Restore**, which acts immediately. Clients are deactivated and restored rather than deleted.

## Clients for assistants

Create an external assistant's client with **New agent client** under **Settings › Connections › Agent access**. Its grants are restricted to reading and preparing changes through that connection; it cannot approve, publish or write live data. It is distinct from an ordinary integration client. Follow [Manage an assistant's access](/docs/guide/administer/manage-agent-access/).

The built-in assistant instead has a dedicated client for each task, managed by refiroo and omitted from the normal client list. You do not create a secret for that session client. See [AI settings and access](/docs/administer/ai/) for its permissions, costs and retention.

## Plan the next replacement

A newly created secret has **No end** until a later rotation gives it an overlap deadline
or someone ends it. There is no automatic client-secret rotation. Agree who owns the
integration and its next handover. Each rotation shortens all older still-valid secrets
to at most the chosen overlap; it never extends an earlier deadline. Check every running
copy of the receiving integration before ending an older secret.

If a client changed while the page was open, reload its details before repeating a rename,
rotation or deactivation. A successful rotation followed by a lost one-time dialog needs
another rotation, rather than another client identity. Deactivation does not replace a
secret. **Rotate secret…** is available for both Active and Deactivated clients.

For a leaked secret, choose **Deactivate** first and confirm. Select the client in
**Deactivated**, choose **Rotate secret…**, then **Stop it now** and **Rotate secret**.
Save the replacement from its one-time dialog and have the integration owner configure it.
Review retained grants before choosing **Restore**. Rotation does not restore a client:
the new secret takes effect when the client is restored.

The overlap is counted from making the replacement, including time spent deactivated.
It does not start again on **Restore**. With **Stop it now**, older secrets expire immediately;
with a nonzero overlap, an older secret may still work after restoration until its deadline.

![Rotate secret for a deactivated client, with the recovery note and Stop it now selected](/docs/screens/admin-client-inactive-rotate.png)

Moving or restoring these identities is part of the operator's
[instance backup and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/). A client recreated with the
same name has a different ID and secret, and does not inherit the old grants or history.

Deactivation blocks access while the client is inactive. Restoring it can allow previously
issued access again if that access has not expired; deactivation is not permanent
revocation of every earlier sign-in. Coordinate secret replacement and the lifetime of
previously issued access with the integration owner before restoring a compromised client.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/permis:
---
title: Permissions reference
description: Compare every action group, the work it permits and the predefined roles that include it.
reader: access-admin
---

Use this reference when choosing a role or checking why someone cannot complete a task.
Open **Settings › People and access › Roles** with **Security administration** to compare the
matrix or create a custom role. Roles select whole action groups, not individual actions.
[Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) explains where grants apply and
how direct and group access combine. Follow [Create a custom role](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-custom-role/)
to put the groups together.

## Action groups and actions

The action names below are the words used when a permission refusal explains what is
missing. A role can allow an action while another rule still prevents it: for example,
a second-person approval rule, a submitted change set or a write restriction.

| Action group | Actions it allows | Predefined roles holding the group | Where it applies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Browse | Reading the model; Reading the workspace; Reading records; Reading change sets; Reading publications; Exporting records; Using this job. | Reader; Contributor; Data steward; Data owner; Agent | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Edit live | Changing records. | Data steward; Data owner | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Work in change sets | Changing records; Changing change sets; Submitting a change set; Withdrawing a submission; Using this job. | Contributor; Data steward; Data owner; Agent | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Publish | Publishing a change set; Withdrawing a publication. | Data steward; Data owner | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Approve publications | Withdrawing a submission; Deciding on a change set. | Data owner | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Bulk and import | Sending a batch or an import; Using import profiles; Using source files; Using this job. | Data steward; Data owner | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Copy and move | Using model mappings; Moving records; Using this job. | Data owner | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Model authoring | Authoring models; Reading model releases; Using this job. | Model administrator | The whole instance only |
| Install a model | Installing a model release. | Model administrator | The whole instance only |
| Model release | Reading model releases; Installing a model release; Changing the workspace's model; Using this job. | Model administrator | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Workspace administration | Changing the approval policy; Administering workspaces; Creating a workspace from a workbook. | Workspace administrator | The whole instance only |
| Integration administration | Managing consumer subscriptions. | Integration administrator | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Feed | Reading the change feed. | Data owner; Integration administrator | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |
| Operations | Reading the service's operations; Testing the AI provider. | Operator | The whole instance only |
| Security administration | Security administration; Reading agent access; Changing agent access. | Security administrator | The whole instance only |
| Use AI proposals | Ask for AI proposals and summaries; keeping changes also needs their write permissions. | Data steward; Data owner; Model administrator; Workspace administrator; Integration administrator | Selected workspaces or the whole instance |

**Changing records** uses **Edit live** for Live and **Work in change sets** inside a
change set. One does not grant the other. **Withdrawing a submission** additionally
checks that the caller submitted it or can approve it. **Deciding on a change set** means
**Approve and publish** or **Send back**; approval publishes in the same step.
**Changing the approval policy** belongs to **Workspace administration**, not
**Security administration**.

**Creating a workspace from a workbook** also needs either **Install a model** or
**Model release**, together with **Bulk and import**, all granted for the whole instance.

**Reading model releases** is shared by **Model authoring** and **Model release**.
**Installing a model release** is shared by **Install a model** and **Model release**.
Installation alone does not change a workspace. **Changing the workspace's model**
activates a release or migrates that workspace.

**Security administration** includes people, groups, roles, grants, clients, sign-in
providers, second-factor policy, mail and signing keys. **Reading agent access** opens
its settings, assistants, agent clients and calls. **Changing agent access** registers,
blocks and restores the assistants people sign in with. Neither gives workspace data
access by itself.

**Operations**, held by the predefined **Operator** role, also includes **Editing the e-mail template**: changing the template and its logo, and sending a test message.
It includes **Reading the service's operations** and **Testing the AI provider**.
The test sends a real request and can incur a provider charge. **Integration administration**
manages consumer subscriptions and their deliveries; reading data through a consumer API
still requires an explicit client grant. See [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/).

## Using this job

**Using this job** means reading, following, cancelling or confirming a job. The required
group follows the kind of work; it is not a group to tick in a role.

| Kind of work | Group used |
| --- | --- |
| Batch, import, import profile and profile check | Bulk and import |
| Export | Browse |
| Move and inferred model mapping | Copy and move |
| AI record proposals | Work in change sets |
| Assistant task | Bulk and import |
| Workspace migration | Model release |
| Model dry run and model inference | Model authoring |

The requester can still see and cancel their own job after losing the group. Continuing
the work uses current permissions and can fail at the next step. See
[Jobs and limits](/docs/administer/jobs-and-limits/) for visibility and retention.

## What every signed-in person can open

Signing in allows people to inspect their own account and permissions and read general
information about refiroo. Listing workspaces returns only those where they hold a role;
it does not grant Browse. The browser's workspace selector offers readable workspaces.
The Changes page combines only the data and model changes the viewer is allowed to see.
An empty list does not prove that no work took place.

<!-- Inventory actions with no screen label: action:signed-in; action:workspaces.list; action:changes.read. -->
<!-- Predefined role identifiers, not browser labels: role:workspace-admin; role:integration-admin; role:security-admin. -->

## What someone without a group sees

Settings hides pages that need a group the person does not hold anywhere. Without
**Security administration**, for example, People, Groups, Roles, Clients, Agent access,
Sign-in, Signing keys and Mail are absent. Without **Operations**, Deployment, Operations
and AI are absent. Without **Integration administration**, Webhooks is absent. Consumer
APIs needs **Browse** somewhere; its entries still depend on the selected workspace.

In a workspace, the interface hides actions the person cannot perform. A Reader sees
**You can read this workspace** without edit actions. Someone who can propose changes
works through **Propose a change**; that does not give them Live editing or publication.
Narrowed writers see controls on the permitted record types. Other restrictions, such
as a frozen submission or a retired workspace, can also make an action unavailable.

If permissions change while a page is open, a previously visible action can be refused.
Read the action, required group and workspace in the message. Check direct grants,
group memberships and whole-instance grants, then reload after correcting access.
[Account › What you can do](/docs/use/account/#what-you-can-do) shows the person's
combined grants. A hidden control is not a reason to create another identity.

## The assistant ceiling

The predefined **Agent** role contains **Browse** and **Work in change sets**. These
same two groups are the maximum for every external assistant connection, even when its
person holds more. Actual access is the intersection with the person's or client's grants.
An assistant cannot use **Publish**, **Approve publications**, **Edit live**, access
administration or model administration through that connection. It prepares changes in
change sets created by its own person or client. See [Agent access](/docs/administer/agent-access/)
for registration, blocking and ending a connection.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/api-re:
---
title: The API reference and Consumer APIs pages
description: Find the documentation and handover details for integrations without changing the active model.
reader: access-admin
---

Use **Settings › Connections › API reference** to find the interactive reference for refiroo’s interfaces. Use **Consumer APIs** to inspect the read interfaces declared by the active model. These pages are read-only: neither changes a definition nor grants access.

## API reference

**Sources** lists **Management API**, its version and the engine version, followed by the available consumer APIs at their contract versions. Select a source name to open its interactive reference. The **OpenAPI document** column opens or downloads the corresponding document for an integration developer.

The Management API supports the browser and integrations. A consumer API exposes a model-defined selection of data for consuming systems. Its contract version is separate from the engine version and model release version. Use the displayed versions when discussing an integration with its owner.

![API reference Sources table with the management interface and a consumer interface](/docs/screens/admin-api-reference.png)

## Consumer APIs

This Settings page is offered to people with **Browse**. It identifies the active model release and offers **Open the release**. For each available consumer API it shows its name, description, contract version, **Base URL**, **OpenAPI document** and a table of operations. Use the copy controls beside the addresses to hand them to the integration owner; select an operation’s description to open its reference.

These are connection details for the integration team. You do not need to type them into another Settings page. For their meaning and use, see [Consumer APIs](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/).

Definitions change through a model release, not on this page. When **The active release declares no consumer API** appears, **Open model** takes a model administrator to the model. Ask them to declare the required interface if one is needed.

The **Change feed** section states how long change entries are kept. Once an integration falls behind that retention, it needs recovery rather than continuing from an expired position. The operator sets retention; the integration owner handles synchronisation.

![Consumer APIs with an interface’s version, copy controls and operation descriptions](/docs/screens/admin-consumer-apis.png)

## Documentation is separate from access

Being able to open a reference does not authorise reading its data. Consumer API descriptions are publicly readable; data needs an explicit grant to a **client**, for the chosen API in one workspace. A management role never substitutes for that grant, and people do not receive consumer API grants. The list of APIs available to a client is limited to its grants. Follow [Grant a consumer API to a client](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/).

If a page fails to load, use its retry control. A failure to read the definitions does not mean the model declares none. Check the selected workspace and the active release before sending connection details.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/signin:
---
title: Signing keys
description: Understand normal signing-key replacement and emergency retirement.
reader: access-admin
---

Signing keys let the engine sign the proof of access it gives people and clients, so it
can recognise valid access on later requests. They are different from a client's secret
and from the keys used to sign webhook deliveries. You do not copy a signing key to a person or integration.

Open **Settings › People and access › Signing keys** with **Security administration**.
The list shows **Key ID**, **State**, **Created**, **Replaced** and **Retired**.
**No key yet: one is made with the first token.** means the instance has not needed a signing key yet. You do not need to create or delete a row to clear that state. The current key is **Signing**. A replaced key shows **Verifying until** with the end time
while it still accepts access it signed. A retired key no longer does so.

![Signing keys with a current Signing key and a replaced key still verifying](/docs/screens/admin-signing-keys.png)

*Above: the reference instance has a new Signing key and a previous key verifying until
its displayed deadline. The identifiers distinguish keys; they are not values to copy into a system.*

## Normal replacement

By default the engine replaces its signing key after 30 days, when next needed.
The operator can change the interval. Existing access signed with the replaced key remains
valid until it expires. Browser sessions renew and clients move to the new key through
normal sign-in renewal; no administrator handover is needed.

**Start a new key** performs that normal replacement immediately. There is no dialog or
second confirmation. A successful replacement leaves the previous key verifying until its
remaining access expires.

## Suspected disclosure

**Retire the current key now** is the emergency action. It asks for confirmation, then
refuses access signed with that key from the next request and starts a replacement.
People's refiroo sessions renew without signing in again. A client is refused once and must
obtain fresh access using its unchanged secret. The integration must handle that renewal.
Retiring a signing key does not replace client secrets.

If starting or retiring a key fails, read the error and reload the list before assuming
a new key is active. Follow [Rotate signing keys](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-signing-keys/)
for both procedures.

Signing keys are not deleted from this page. Normal replacement preserves verification until existing access expires; emergency retirement refuses it immediately. For webhook delivery keys, follow [Rotate a webhook key](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-webhook-key/); those keys are managed on each webhook, not here.

## Restore or move an installation

Signing keys are held with the instance, shared by its engine processes. They are not
exported or imported from this page. The operator must preserve the database and its
secret storage through the [backup and restore procedure](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/).
Starting a new signing key does not repair an installation that cannot open its saved
secrets. Give the operator that failure message before attempting more replacements.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/sign-i:
---
title: Sign-in and second factors
description: Choose local or provider sign-in, require a second factor and understand browser sessions.
reader: access-admin
---

Open **Settings › People and access › Sign-in** to choose how people prove who they are.
You need **Security administration**. Sign-in establishes identity; [roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/)
decide what that identity may do afterwards.

![Sign-in catalogue with Local accounts on and no providers](/docs/screens/admin-signin.png)

*Above: local accounts are on and no organisation provider is configured in the reference instance.*

## Local accounts

With **Local accounts** on, people can use their refiroo e-mail address and password.
Unless an administrator manages their sign-in, they manage their password, passkeys and
authenticator app on their own [Account](/docs/use/account/) page. For shared, kiosk or training
accounts, see [Sign-in managed by an administrator](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/#sign-in-managed-by-an-administrator). Passwords normally need 15–128 characters. The operator can change the minimum. A password equal to the e-mail address or a common password is refused with a reason.
Repeated failed sign-ins are delayed, rather than permanently locking the account;
the sign-in screen says how long to wait. Slowdown starts after five failed attempts for an account or twenty from an address. Waits double up to fifteen minutes; repeatedly retrying does not bypass them.

**Keeps local sign-in** on a person's page lets them retain this route when local sign-in
is off for everyone else. They use **Sign in with a local administrator account** on the
sign-in page. Keep a working recovery administrator before changing organisation sign-in.
Clients are unaffected by turning local sign-in off.

**Turn off…** is offered only after an enabled provider has successfully signed someone in.
Read and confirm the warning. People without the retained local route then use a provider.
**Turn on** restores local sign-in. The last active person keeping local sign-in cannot be
deactivated or lose it while local sign-in is off.

## The organisation's provider

A provider uses OpenID Connect and brings its own multi-factor sign-in. refiroo still
starts its own session. People are matched by their provider identity, never by e-mail alone.
See [People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/) for linking an existing person
and for provider-controlled membership.

To add a provider in the browser:

1. Choose **New provider**. Enter **Name on the sign-in button**; the button reads
   “Continue with” followed by that name. Enter a **Key**, which cannot change once saved.
2. With your organisation's sign-in administrator, enter **Issuer**, **Client ID** and
   **Client secret** from its application registration. The issuer must match exactly.
   The secret is saved securely and is never shown again. Changing an unused issuer requires the secret again; a secret is not silently carried to a different provider endpoint.
3. Set **Groups claim** only if the provider supplies group memberships. Empty means its
   groups are not used. Ask the sign-in administrator for the correct field name.
4. Leave **Offer it on the sign-in page now** selected to enable it, then choose **Add provider**.
   An enabled provider is checked when saved. If discovery, connection or certificate checks
   fail, read the reason and correct the provider details with the operator.
5. Open the saved provider's page and copy its **Redirect address** under
   **Address to register with the provider**. Have that address registered with the provider.
   Prove a complete sign-in before turning local sign-in off.

![New sign-in provider with identity, registration and groups fields](/docs/screens/admin-signin-provider-new.png)

*Above: the reference instance's New sign-in provider dialog is open and has not been saved.*

Once anyone has used a provider, its issuer cannot change. Add another provider and link
people instead. Disabling a provider ends sessions it started. Removing someone in the
provider alone does not end an already open refiroo session; deactivate leavers in refiroo too.

On the provider page, **Sign people out of … too** also signs the current browser out of
the provider. It is off by default and can sign the person out of other organisation
applications in that browser. It needs provider support and registration of the displayed
**Sign-out address**. **Sign out everywhere** ends refiroo sessions only.

Server address, HTTPS and recovery setup belong with the operator. See the
[Run refiroo sign-in instructions](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/).

## Provider groups and sign-out limits

OpenID Connect works with Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Keycloak, Okta and other compatible providers.
A provider group's membership comes from the person's sign-in. Create expected provider groups
before go-live and grant their roles, or grant them after they first appear. A new provider person
has no direct roles; an e-mail address matching an existing person does not merge them.

For Microsoft Entra ID, group values are object IDs rather than readable names. Ask its
administrator to include groups assigned to the registered application, then give those groups
readable names in refiroo. With more than 200 groups, Entra ID can return a link instead of the
list. refiroo does not follow that link, leaving the person with no provider groups. Reduce the
groups assigned to the registration. Keycloak needs a Group Membership mapper. Google does not
supply groups through this sign-in.

Name and e-mail are refreshed from the provider when the person signs in. Removing a person at
the provider does not recheck an existing refiroo session: deactivate leavers here too.

Turning on provider sign-out affects sessions started afterwards. Older sessions did not retain
the needed provider proof and sign out of refiroo only. An administrator ending someone's sessions,
or **Sign out everywhere**, also ends refiroo sessions only. If the operator changes the public
site address, have both displayed return addresses registered again before testing sign-in.

If **Delete provider** is refused because people have used it, choose **Disable** instead.
The retained provider preserves their identities while its sessions end.

## Second factors and passkeys

Someone whose sign-in is managed by an administrator cannot add or change their own factors.
The following Account controls are for people who manage their own sign-in.

A local password must be set before a person adds an authenticator app or passkey. A provider-only account cannot add local factors. Adding or removing a passkey on Account requires proof with a password, authenticator code or recovery code; knowing an account’s name is insufficient. A person can register up to 25 passkeys.

An authenticator app uses time-based one-time passwords (TOTP), adding a six-digit code after the password. Setup includes confirmation
with a code and ten recovery codes shown once. Each recovery code works once. A phone's
clock must be correct; if valid-looking codes fail, check its automatic time setting.

A WebAuthn passkey uses a fingerprint, face, device PIN or security key. It can sign someone in alone,
or supply the second step after a password. It meets the second-factor requirement.
A passkey belongs to the site's address; a change of host requires people to register new passkeys.

![Local accounts settings with the second-factor requirement](/docs/screens/admin-signin-local.png)

*Above: Local accounts is on in the reference instance; Require a second factor with a password is unchecked.*

**Require a second factor with a password** applies to local password sign-in,
including recovery administrators. Someone who manages their own sign-in and has neither an
authenticator app nor a passkey must set up an app on the sign-in page before a session starts.
An account whose sign-in is managed by an administrator is exempt from this setup: with no
factor, it signs in with the password alone even while the requirement is on. An existing
authenticator app or passkey still applies; switching on administrator management does not
remove it. Provider sign-ins use the
provider's own checks, and clients are not asked for a second factor.
This is the browser's administrative policy control; there are no separate session-duration
or passkey-policy settings here. Follow [Require a second factor](/docs/guide/administer/require-a-second-factor/).

An app code that was already accepted cannot be used again. Authenticator time needs to be within
about a minute of the server; turn on automatic time before replacing an otherwise working app.
Someone who has registered passkeys but no authenticator app has no app recovery codes. They need
another passkey kept elsewhere, or an administrator to remove the lost passkey. While ordinary
local sign-in is off, passkey-only sign-in also requires **Keeps local sign-in**.

## Sessions and help

A session renews while the person works. By default it ends after 12 hours without renewal
or 14 days overall; the operator can change these limits. Once it ends, the person signs in
again and returns to the requested page.

Only the person's own **Account › Where you’re signed in** lists individual sessions.
This section is hidden for a person whose sign-in is managed by an administrator. They can
sign out of their current browser, but need an administrator to end other sessions.
Administrators have **Sign out everywhere** on the person's page, with confirmation.
Deactivation and using a password-reset link also end their sessions. Changing one's own
password keeps the current browser signed in and ends the others.

![Account with sign-in methods and the beginning of the session list](/docs/screens/admin-account-sessions.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's own Account page. The reference account's many sessions include automated
capture sessions; this is not an administrator's list of other people's browsers.*

If someone loses a device, a remaining passkey or recovery code may let them sign in.
Otherwise an administrator can remove the lost authenticator factor or passkey from the
person's page. A password reset does not bypass a second factor. Follow
[Help someone who lost a device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).

When mail is configured, the sign-in page offers a forgotten-password link for local accounts.
A person who manages their own sign-in can request recovery there rather than asking an administrator to make a link. If it
is absent, use the administrator's reset procedure. The account-side password, session, passkey
and recovery-code tasks are on [Your account](/docs/use/account/).

A forgotten-password request replaces only earlier links requested from the sign-in page. It
does not cancel a link made by an administrator. Making a new administrator link replaces all
earlier password links for that person.

Opening a valid link takes the secret part out of the address bar before showing the password
form. You can reload the page in the same browser without losing the link. If the form no longer
opens, reopen the original link while it is valid; an expired, replaced or used link
needs a new one. Keep the original link private rather than sharing the address shown after it opens.

## Help with the sign-in screen

The screen shows the refiroo mark and **Reference data that stays in step.** People enter **E-mail address** and **Password**, then **Sign in**; **Signing in…** means it is waiting for an answer. Provider buttons say **Continue with …**. **Sign in with a passkey** uses a registered passkey and the device’s own confirmation.

The next step depends on the methods available. **Enter your code** asks for an app code. **Confirm it is you** also offers **Use a passkey**. **Use a recovery code instead** opens **Use a recovery code**; **Use the app’s code** returns to the app. **Set up a second factor** shows the setup image and key, followed by **Confirm and continue** and **Keep your recovery codes**. Ask the person to store the codes before continuing. They can start again if the sign-in attempt has expired.

**Your session ended. Sign in again to return to where you were.** calls for a fresh sign-in, not a password reset. **Signing in is not possible right now** with **Try again** can mean a service or connection failure. If the message says this site’s address is not accepted, give the operator the browser address and message so they can correct deployment access. Do not change a person’s password to repair a service failure.

Expired or invalid proof of access is refused before an operation runs. The browser normally renews a session automatically; if it cannot, sign in again. For an external system, have the integration owner follow [Signing in and tokens](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/).

With no mail server, the screen instead says **Forgotten your password? Ask a security administrator for a reset link.** With mail, the person requests a one-time link, enters **New password** and **Type it again**, then chooses **Set password**. **Your password is set. You were signed out everywhere.** leads back to **Sign in**. The request gives the same answer for known, unknown, provider-only and deactivated accounts; mail is sent only for a qualifying local account. An account whose sign-in is managed by an administrator receives no recovery mail; ask an administrator to make a password link instead. An app or recovery code is still required afterwards when configured. See [Mail](/docs/administer/mail/#password-links).

For the administrator’s tasks, follow [Add a sign-in provider](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-sign-in-provider/), [Link a provider sign-in](/docs/guide/administer/link-a-provider-person/) and [Turn off local sign-in](/docs/guide/administer/turn-off-local-sign-in/). On the provider catalogue, **No provider yet: people sign in with a password.** describes an empty list, not a connection failure. Saved provider details include separate Enable, Disable and Delete actions; disabling or deleting one ends the sessions it started.

## Change provider credentials and recover access

If the provider's client secret expires or is replaced there, open the saved provider,
enter its replacement **Client secret** under **Settings** and choose **Save**. A blank
field keeps the saved secret for an unchanged issuer; it does not clear it. Arrange the
handover with the provider administrator and test a new sign-in in a separate browser.
refiroo does not renew that provider credential for you. Existing refiroo sessions are
separate from a new provider sign-in, so an already open page does not prove the new
credential works.

Turning local sign-in off or changing the second-factor requirement changes subsequent
sign-ins; it does not sign out existing sessions. Use **Sign out everywhere** on a person's
page when their existing sessions must end. Turning the requirement off leaves registered
apps, recovery codes and passkeys in place.

The following messages call for different corrections:

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Local sign-in stays on until an enabled sign-in provider has signed someone in, so nobody is locked out | Enable the provider and complete a successful sign-in before trying again. |
| Local sign-in is off and this is the last person who keeps it; turn local sign-in on, or let someone else keep it first | Prepare another recovery account or turn local sign-in on before removing this route. |
| This provider changed while the page was open. It is shown as it is now; try again. | Review the refreshed provider before applying your change. |
| Another sign-in provider has this key | Open the existing provider or choose a distinct key for a different registration. |

A provider's **Disabled** state is reversible with **Enable**. Deleting an unused provider
has no undo: its registration details must be supplied again. Disable a used provider
rather than replacing its issuer. Keep a tested local recovery account while correcting
a failed provider. If none can sign in, the operator uses
[server recovery](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/). Moving or restoring the installation
also needs the operator's [backup and restore procedure](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/);
changing the public address affects registered provider return addresses and passkeys.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/webhoo:
---
title: The Webhooks page
description: Manage webhook delivery, keys, suspended subscriptions and delivery history in Settings.
reader: access-admin
---

Use **Settings › Connections › Webhooks** to send a consumer API’s declared record events or the workspace’s change-set events to another system. You need **Integration administration** in the source workspace. Security administration alone does not grant it. The operator must also enable webhooks in the deployment.

Work with the receiving system’s owner before creating or changing delivery. [Webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) explains the receiving system’s responsibilities. Here you manage the subscription in the browser.

## Sources and configuration

Choose **Events from** in **New webhook**:

- **Consumer API** delivers the selected API’s declared record events from live data in the chosen **Workspace**.
- **Workspace events** delivers the workspace’s change-set steps, independently of a consumer API declaration.

The source and workspace are fixed at creation. Delete the subscription and create another to change them. Consumer APIs and their events are declared by the model; every application can use this capability when its model declares it.

For **Workspace events**, **All events (3)** selects all three choices. **Chosen events** lets you select:

| Event shown | When it is sent |
| --- | --- |
| change-set.submitted | A change set was submitted for approval. |
| change-set.approved | A change set was approved and published. |
| change-set.sent-back | A change set was sent back to its author. |

The **Consumer API** selector, **Filters** and **Content** choices are hidden for workspace events. These notifications describe change-set steps rather than consumer records. **Requests** and **Format** remain available for both sources.

![New webhook with Workspace events selected and all three change-set events](/docs/screens/admin-webhook-workspace-events.png)

**New webhook** is available even when no consumer API declares events. In that case, **Events from** offers **Workspace events** alone. When **Webhooks are off in this deployment** appears, there is no **New webhook** button. **Open Deployment** leads to the deployment information; ask the operator to enable them and restart the service.

The **New webhook** and **Edit webhook** dialogs contain:

| Section | Choices |
| --- | --- |
| Webhook | **Name** identifies the receiver for people. **URL** is its receiving address. Use HTTPS. Private and localhost destinations need the operator to allow them on this instance; plain HTTP is limited to localhost. Link-local destinations are always refused. |
| Source | **Events from**, then **Consumer API** when applicable, and **Workspace**. To change these later, create another webhook. |
| Events | **All events** or **Chosen events**, selected with **Choose events**. The choices describe the record types and changes they watch. |
| Filters | **Add filter** offers the API’s declared filters. Enter a value and press Enter; several values of one filter are alternatives. With no filters, every event of the chosen kinds is delivered. |
| Delivery | **Requests**, **Content** and **Format**, agreed with the receiver’s owner. |

**One event per request** is the default. **Batched** sends waiting events up to **Up to (events)** and the request-size limit, without waiting to fill a batch. The normal maximum is 1,000 events and 1 MiB; an unusually large single record can exceed that size. The form shows the deployment’s event limit.

For consumer API events, **With the object** carries the record as it is when sent. **Notification only** tells the receiver which change happened so it can read what it needs. **Format** selects **RDM JSON** or **CloudEvents 1.0**, as agreed with the receiver. These choices are independent.

For consumer API events, a filter is evaluated when sending, against the record’s current state. A record leaving the filter’s scope is not sent just to tell the receiver it left; deletions are sent. Agree how the receiving system reconciles its copies with its integration owner.

![The New webhook dialog with its source, event and delivery choices](/docs/screens/admin-webhook-new.png)

Follow [Create a webhook](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-webhook/).

## State and delivery position

The catalogue shows **Active**, **Retrying** or **Suspended**. Select a webhook for **Configuration** and **Deliveries**. Configuration shows its destination, source, events, filters, creator, delivery progress, signing-key dates and any failure or suspension findings.

**Suspend** stops delivery immediately, without a confirmation. **Resume…** checks the subscription against the current model and workspace. Choose **The first event not acknowledged** to continue from where it stopped. **Now, with reset** skips waiting changes and starts after the current position; arrange a fresh synchronisation with the receiver’s owner. Reset first, then synchronise from the publication identified by the page so changes do not fall between.

A new webhook starts after the current change position. The browser has no choice of an earlier starting position; an integrator can request one separately. Existing records do not arrive just because a webhook was created.

A failed request blocks later delivery for that subscription. Retries start after about 10 seconds, then 30 seconds, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 minutes, then hourly, for 24 hours; waits vary slightly. The page shows the last error, attempts and next try. After the retry window it becomes Suspended. Editing the receiving URL retries a waiting request at once.

| Suspension shown | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Suspended by a user | Resume when the receiver is ready. |
| The model changed | Edit the subscription to fix the listed missing events, filters or other findings, then resume. |
| The contract version changed | The accepted version stopped being served. Read **Accepted** and **Served now**, have the receiver owner confirm compatibility, then resume to accept the current version. |
| The workspace was retired | Ask a workspace administrator to reactivate it, then resume; otherwise delete the webhook. |
| Delivery failed | Repair the receiver, then resume to retry the unacknowledged request. |
| A filter matches nothing | Correct the filter value, then resume. |
| Events expired | Reset and resume, then have the receiver synchronise again from the named publication. |

A consumer webhook stays on its accepted version while that version remains served by the active model. Its events keep that version’s shape. Stopping that version can suspend it; resuming accepts the current version after its events and filters pass the checks. Workspace events do not depend on consumer contract versions.

Follow [Find out why a webhook paused](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/) for diagnosis.

## Signing keys

Creating a webhook shows **Keep the signing key** once. Store it securely with the receiver’s configuration before **I have stored the key**. It cannot be read back. Each delivery is signed so the receiver can check its origin.

**Rotate key…** replaces that webhook’s key. An overlap of **1 hour**, **24 hours** or **7 days** lets the receiver switch while both keys work. **Stop it now** is for a leaked key: deliveries use the replacement alone and may be refused until the receiver has it. Follow [Rotate a webhook key](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-webhook-key/).

This key is separate from [client secrets](/docs/administer/clients/) and the instance’s [signing keys](/docs/administer/signing-keys/).

## Deliveries

The **Deliveries** tab filters **Status** to **Queued**, **Sending**, **Retrying**, **Succeeded**, **Failed** or **Dropped**. Choose **Refresh** for the current state. Each row identifies the event and record, status, attempts, response and sent time. Open the event to inspect **Attempts** and the saved request and response; select an attempt to inspect its answer. These details can contain record data, so share them only with authorised people.

![Retrying webhook delivery with its attempts and receiver response](/docs/screens/admin-webhook-deliveries.png)

Deliveries are normally kept for seven days; the page states the configured retention. A request still being retried or awaiting resume is kept longer. The list is a delivery log, not permanent data history.

**Resend** asks **Resend a delivered event?** Confirm **Resend event** only with the receiver owner’s agreement, or choose **Don’t resend**. It sends the saved request again and can repeat an action in the receiving system. It is unavailable when the saved request is no longer held. It does not replace repairing and resuming a suspended webhook.

**Delete…** asks **Delete this webhook?** Confirm **Delete webhook** to stop sending and discard its signing key, or choose **Keep the webhook**. A replacement is a new subscription with a new position and key. A workspace with subscriptions cannot be deleted until they are removed.

Edits and actions check that the webhook has not changed meanwhile. If **Not saved** appears, review the current configuration and the explanation before applying the action again.

Webhook subscriptions are installation settings, separate from a model release. Installing or
copying a model does not copy its webhook destinations, keys or delivery positions. Review these
separately when moving an integration to another installation.

## Change a receiver or stop it permanently

Use **Edit…** on the selected webhook to change **Name**, **URL**, chosen events, filters
or delivery choices, then **Save**. A rename preserves a request being retried.
Other configuration edits clear that saved retry and build the next request from the
first event not acknowledged, using the new configuration. The receiver may already have
seen an earlier attempt, so agree the change with its owner. Editing a suspended webhook
does not resume it; use **Resume…** after correcting its findings.

A destination must be an absolute address of at most 2,048 characters, with no user name,
password or fragment. If the form says **The webhook URL must not hold user information:
the request is signed instead**, use the receiver's address without credentials and
configure it to check the webhook signing key. Redirects are not followed; enter the
final destination. The receiving system's owner handles its HTTPS certificate renewal.

Destinations are checked when saved and on every attempt. If an address is refused, read the
reason in **Deliveries** and ask the operator to review the destination. A host name can become
refused if its addresses change. After an upgrade, a private receiver may stop receiving until
the operator allows private destinations; resume a suspended webhook once the cause is fixed.

A webhook's signing key has no scheduled automatic replacement. Rotating again during an
overlap immediately ends the key retained from the earlier rotation: only the current
replacement and the key it just replaced can sign. Arrange each handover before starting
another. Rotation is also possible while suspended; it does not resume delivery.


For temporarily stopping delivery use **Suspend**; for removing the destination use
**Delete…**. Deletion has no undo and a new subscription does not restore the old delivery
position. An installation restore needs its database and secret storage, through the
operator's [backup and restore procedure](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/). Coordinate a
restore with receivers: returning to an older acknowledged position can repeat deliveries.

---
title: Roles and grants
description: Understand every predefined role, combine grants and limit where someone may make changes.
reader: access-admin
---

A **role** is a set of action groups. A **grant** gives that role to a person, group or
client in chosen workspaces or across the whole instance. Manage them under **Settings**
with **Security administration**. A role's name alone does not give it every kind of access:
for example, a Security administrator manages people but needs Browse to read their data.

## The predefined roles

Open **People and access › Roles** to compare roles by action group. The predefined roles cannot
be edited. The following table lists their action groups; the descriptions below explain them.

| Role | Action groups |
| --- | --- |
| Reader | Browse |
| Contributor | Browse; Work in change sets |
| Data steward | Browse; Edit live; Work in change sets; Publish; Bulk and import; Use AI proposals |
| Data owner | Browse; Edit live; Work in change sets; Publish; Approve publications; Bulk and import; Feed; Copy and move; Use AI proposals |
| Model administrator | Model authoring; Install a model; Model release; Use AI proposals |
| Workspace administrator | Workspace administration; Use AI proposals |
| Integration administrator | Integration administration; Feed; Use AI proposals |
| Operator | Operations |
| Security administrator | Security administration |
| Agent | Browse; Work in change sets |

![Roles matrix comparing predefined roles by action group](/docs/screens/admin-roles.png)

*Above: the reference instance shows the predefined roles as columns and action groups as rows.*

| Action group | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| Browse | Read the workspace's model, records, relationships, history, change sets and publications; export to a file. |
| Edit live | Create, change and delete records, field values and relationships in Live. |
| Work in change sets | Create, edit, validate and discard proposals; submit them for publication. It does not permit publishing them. |
| Publish | Publish a change set and withdraw a publication, subject to approval policy. |
| Approve publications | Decide submitted proposals: approve and publish, or send back. |
| Bulk and import | Work with batches, imports, import profiles and source files. |
| Copy and move | Work with model mappings and move records between workspaces. |
| Model authoring | Edit model drafts and read model releases. This responsibility applies across the instance. |
| Install a model | Install a draft as a release without activating it. This responsibility applies across the instance. |
| Model release | Install releases, activate them in a workspace and migrate a workspace. |
| Workspace administration | Create, rename, retire and delete workspaces, set the default and manage approval policies. This responsibility applies across the instance. |
| Integration administration | Manage consumer API subscriptions and deliveries. |
| Feed | Read a workspace's change feed. |
| Operations | Inspect processes, readiness, metrics, backup rehearsals and deployment settings. This responsibility applies across the instance. |
| Security administration | Manage people, groups, roles, grants, clients and signing keys. This responsibility applies across the instance. |
| Use AI proposals | Ask for proposals and summaries where configured. Keeping a proposed change also needs permission to write it. |

Administrative responsibilities do not imply Browse or data editing. Give additional roles
only where the person's task needs them. Roles also do not enable a feature the deployment has disabled.

For the complete list of actions, the roles holding each group and what someone without it sees,
see the [Permissions reference](/docs/administer/permissions-reference/).

## Where a grant applies

**The whole instance** covers every workspace now and later. **Workspaces** limits a grant
to the selected workspaces. The Grant dialog greys out roles held only across the instance
when workspace grants are selected. Choose the whole instance if that is the intended responsibility.

On a person's page, **Roles** lists **Where**, **Role**, **Narrowed to (writes)** and **Through**.
Direct and inherited access are shown separately. On **Settings › Workspaces**, select a
workspace and open **Access** to see the people, groups and clients whose grants apply there.
Use **Search people, groups, clients**, and filter by **Role** or **Kind** (**People**, **Groups**, **Clients**). The colour legend distinguishes Reader, Contributor, Steward, Data owner, Administration and Consumer API. Names and labels identify roles as well as colours.

Each recipient’s plus control, **Add a role for …**, opens the grant dialog for that recipient. A workspace grant’s remove control asks **Remove … from …?** before removing it. Whole-instance grants are labelled and must be removed at their source rather than on the workspace’s Access tab.

![A person's roles showing scope, restrictions and source](/docs/screens/admin-grants-person.png)

*Above: Guide Admin has six roles for every workspace, all granted directly.*

![Workspace Access tab showing people and their grants](/docs/screens/admin-grants-workspace.png)

*Above: Graubünden includes Guide Admin's whole-instance roles, fictional Rita Approver's
workspace Data owner grant and the Stops reader client.*

## How grants combine

Grants add access together. A direct grant and grants through any groups all count; there
is no denying grant that cancels another grant. Removing one leaves the others in effect.
Changes to roles, grants and memberships apply on the next request. A job also uses its
requester's current permissions; taking away required access can stop its next step.

Only **Edit live**, **Work in change sets**, **Publish**, **Bulk and import** and **Copy and move** can be narrowed. A grant can narrow those writes to selected applications or record types. A record matches when either its application or its type is selected; multiple grants add their permitted records together. This affects live edits,
change sets, imports, publication, moves and type changes. An instance grant cannot be narrowed. It never narrows reading:
Browse reads the whole workspace. Keep data that different readers must not see in separate workspaces.
Another applicable grant can still allow wider writes.

The dialog offers narrowing for one role in one workspace. If a later model change removes
the named applications or types, a grant can become stale and cease to allow those writes.
Review and replace stale grants rather than assuming a matching old name still grants access.

Clients need an explicit **Consumer API** grant for each API in each workspace they read.
A management role, even Security administrator, does not substitute for that grant.
See [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/).

## Custom roles

Choose **New role**, enter **Name**, and choose **Start from**: **Nothing** for an empty role
or an existing role to copy its action groups. **Add role** returns to the matrix with
the new role available for editing. Tick its action groups, adjust its name or optional
description and choose **Save**. Creating a copy does not change the source role.

![New role dialog with Name and Start from](/docs/screens/admin-role-new.png)

*Above: the reference dialog starts from Nothing. Action groups are selected in the matrix after creation.*

Editing a custom role changes access for everyone holding it on their next request.
A role still granted cannot be deleted; remove its grants before **Delete role**.
refiroo refuses changes that would leave no active Security administrator.
Follow [Grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) to give or remove access.

A narrowed grant permits a relationship write when either endpoint is within its allowed
records. An import, batch or move refuses individual items outside that scope; publishing a
change set containing an unpermitted type is refused as a whole. Review stale grants after a
model change even when an old type name looks familiar.

In the Grant dialog, roles are ticked as cards for the whole instance or selected workspaces;
consumer APIs use a grid of APIs by workspace for clients only. Existing access is shown and
is not granted again. To check the resulting access as its recipient, open
[Account › What you can do](/docs/use/account/#what-you-can-do).

## What the recipient sees

A Reader sees **You can read this workspace** and no edit actions. A Contributor sees **Propose a change** or **Propose a new …** and works in their own change set; live editing and publishing are refused. A role with only Edit live does not also give Work in change sets. People and clients with the same role have the same management permissions.

A narrowed writer sees edit controls on the permitted types. The interface offers imports, moves, publication and other tasks according to their required groups. A permission change can still refuse an action already open on screen; read the message’s action, required groups and workspace, then review the grants. The server checks every operation as well as the browser.

The workspace selector shows readable workspaces. refiroo opens the default if readable, otherwise the first readable workspace. **There is no workspace you can open yet** offers **People** to a security administrator, otherwise **Settings**, with **Account** to check access. Grant Browse in the intended workspace to provide data access; an administration role alone is insufficient.

For import files, the uploader and people allowed to import in that workspace can see them. Job visibility and cancellation also follow the requester and the kind of work; see [Jobs and limits](/docs/administer/jobs-and-limits/).

## Make and review grants

**Grant access** asks **Who** when opened from a workspace: find a person, group or client by name. **Roles** selects their management access. **Where** chooses **Workspaces** or **The whole instance**, meaning every workspace now and later. **No workspace chosen yet** requires a workspace before granting. A client can instead choose **Consumer APIs**; people and groups cannot.

Each selected role/workspace combination or consumer grid cell is saved separately. If **… could not be granted** appears, successful grants remain and failed choices keep their reasons. **Try again** retries the remaining choices. Closing the dialog does not undo successful grants.

Follow [Create a custom role](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-custom-role/), [Narrow a grant to record types](/docs/guide/administer/narrow-a-grant-to-record-types/), or [Grant a consumer API to a client](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/) for those tasks. Before deleting records, a narrowed writer also needs permission for every type removed by a cascade; an out-of-scope cascade is refused before showing its impact.

## AI permissions and assistants

**Use AI proposals** enables the configured built-in AI features in the granted workspaces. It does not provide Browse, import, model editing or publication rights by itself. The five predefined roles holding it are listed above; combine grants for the person's actual task. **Operations** separately allows inspection of AI settings and the provider test. See [AI settings and access](/docs/administer/ai/) for what is sent, costs and retained information.

The **Agent** role contains Browse and Work in change sets. These groups also limit every external assistant's connection, even when its person holds stronger roles. An assistant cannot approve, publish or write live data, and its preparation is confined to change sets created by its own person or client. A person needs no extra Agent grant to connect an assistant using existing rights. See [Agent access](/docs/administer/agent-access/) for the complete limits and how to stop access.
---
title: Who changed what
description: Trace a person's data changes, security activity and a workspace's history.
reader: access-admin
---

Choose the history view that answers your question. **See changes** traces data and model
work by a person or client. **Recent activity** on their security page traces account and
access events. A workspace's **Activity** shows work in that workspace. There is no separate
instance-wide audit page in Settings.

## Changes by a person or client

Open **Settings › People and access › People** or **Settings › Connections › Clients**, select the identity and choose
**See changes**. You can also follow a person's name from history where it is offered.
The page shows newest first, grouped by day, across the workspaces you may read.

![A person's Changes page with workspace, kind and period filters](/docs/screens/admin-audit-person.png)

*Above: fictional Rita Approver's changes include a publication and the height correction
it applied to Davos Platz in Graubünden.*

Filter by **Workspace**, **What** and **Period**. What offers **Everything**, **Records**,
**Relationships**, **Change sets**, **Publications** and **Model**. Period offers **Any time**,
**Last 24 hours**, **Last 7 days** and **Last 30 days**. **Load more** retrieves older results.

An entry names the action, subject, time and workspace, with the change set or cause where
relevant. Data changes from a job name its requester. Changes applied by a publication
name the publisher. The list summarises which fields changed; open the record's history
to inspect values. Linked titles open their subject where it still exists.

Names reflect the current name of a person or client, including after deactivation.
Removed records are identified as removed. Older entries from before sign-in was recorded
say **Before sign-in** rather than inventing an author; engine work is identified separately.

You need Browse in a data entry's workspace. Model administration entries need Model authoring
across the instance. Security administration alone does not give access to data history.
An empty result can therefore mean no visible changes, not that the person has done nothing.

## Security activity

On the selected person's or client's page, scroll to **Recent activity**. Its filters are
**All**, **Signing in**, **Roles and groups** and **Account**. The list records security
actions involving that identity, the time and who performed the action where known.
It includes successful and failed sign-ins, with the originating address where recorded, and changes to people, groups, roles, grants, clients and keys;
it does not expose passwords, secrets or password links.

![Person detail scrolled to roles, groups and Recent activity filters](/docs/screens/admin-grants-person.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's Recent activity begins below the groups section. All, Signing in,
Roles and groups and Account are separate filters.*

Changing only the setting for [administrator-managed sign-in](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/#sign-in-managed-by-an-administrator)
records **Sign-in managed by an administrator** when it is turned on, or **Sign-in no longer
managed** when it is turned off. Look on that person's **Recent activity** under **Account**
or **All**. If name or e-mail details were saved in the same edit, the entry instead lists
the changed details.

Use **Load more** for older activity and **Show fewer** to shorten the displayed list.
A failed load offers **Retry**; it is not evidence that no activity occurred.

## Workspaces and individual records

For all work in one workspace, use **Settings › Workspaces**, select it and open **Activity**.
For the exact before and after values of a record, open that record's **History**.
See [History](/docs/use/history/) for these views and their filters.

Follow [Find who changed something](/docs/guide/administer/find-who-changed-something/)
for a search across these views.

Recent activity groups events under day headings, starts with ten entries and reads 20 more
at a time. The person's Changes page cannot be exported and shows no field values or
model-to-model mapping operations. Open a record's History for recorded values. A system's work
is marked **client**; a job or publication is named as the cause where applicable.

The whole-instance security event list is available to authorised integrations, but there is no corresponding Settings screen. Ask the integration owner to use the [security model for integrators](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/) when they need that broader list. Do not mistake a person’s Recent activity for an instance-wide log.

A deleted workspace’s retained entries can appear in an instance-wide view without an openable workspace; a workspace-filtered view does not make a removed workspace readable. Clearing a filter widens only within your permissions.

## Security history retention

Security events contain no passwords, secrets, reset links or signing keys. They do not currently
expire automatically. Operators should allow for this history to grow with sign-ins and access
changes; the data-feed retention period does not prune it.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/deploy:
---
title: About, Deployment and Operations
description: Find installed versions, read configuration and give the operator useful service information.
reader: access-admin
---

Use these Settings pages to identify the installation and discuss a problem with its operator. **This instance › About** is available to signed-in people. **This instance › Deployment** and **Operations** need **Operations**, held by the predefined Operator role. Security administrator alone does not provide it.

These pages report information. Deployment settings are changed on the server, and Operations does not restore a backup or restart the service. See [Run refiroo](/docs/run/install-with-compose/) for the operator’s tasks.

## About

**About** opens with **Reference data that stays in step.** Its three points, **Shape it to your domain.**, **Connect, don’t copy.** and **One API for everything.**, describe models, meaningful connections and the API. It links to its documentation, reference, licence and source code. **Engine** identifies the installed engine version, Management API version and supported schema languages. **Active model release** gives the model’s name, key, version, schema language and activation time, with **Open release**.

The engine version identifies the software. The model release identifies the definitions currently used for the selected workspace. They change independently; a consumer API also has its own contract version. When reporting a problem, give the relevant software and model versions rather than just the application’s name.

![About with engine and active model release details](/docs/screens/admin-about.png)

## Deployment

**Deployment** shows **Capability groups** as **On** or **Off**, their limits and the setting responsible. A capability being On does not grant permission to use it. A role also cannot turn on a capability that the operator has disabled.

**Database** shows **Migration revision**, useful to the operator when checking an upgrade. The configuration tables show **Setting**, **Value**, **Default**, **Source** and **What it controls**. **Source** distinguishes **Environment** from **Default**. Secrets show only **Set** or **Not set**; the page does not reveal their values.

Read the explanation next to a setting before asking for a change. Values come from the running service’s environment and change after a restart; there is no Save control here. A warning that cursors do not survive a restart means the operator needs to configure a stable signing key for collection navigation. Give them the warning text rather than repeatedly retrying an old position.

![Deployment showing capability states, limits and setting sources](/docs/screens/run-deployment.png)

## Operations

**Operations** reports the instance’s workspaces, engine processes and the last backup rehearsal. Use **Refresh** to reread it. It also refreshes every 15 seconds while visible. A refresh failure leaves a warning; do not treat old figures as a fresh health check.

**Workspaces** shows the release, schema, state and **Not served by**. A workspace is served when every live engine process can serve its release. If a process cannot do so, ask the operator to investigate the listed process and release before changing access grants.

**Engine processes** shows each process as it last reported. The answering process is current; another process can be one report behind. Use the reported process and thread state with the operator to investigate stalled mail, jobs or delivery. This page is for observation, not process control.

**Last backup rehearsal** records a backup restored into a separate database and checked there. It shows the result and workspace checks. **No backup has been rehearsed** means no rehearsal is recorded, not necessarily that no backup exists. A failed rehearsal needs operator attention. Nothing on this page restores live data.

**For monitoring** provides copy controls for the monitoring addresses. Give these to the operator setting up monitoring; keep monitoring access on the appropriate private network. Recovery and server commands belong in [Run refiroo](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/).

![Operations with workspace readiness, engine processes and backup rehearsal](/docs/screens/run-operations.png)

For an access problem, first check the person’s active state and [roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/). For a service problem, pass the operator the time, selected workspace, visible failure message and versions from About. Never include a password, client secret, signing key or one-time password link.

## Earlier checks and unavailable information

Under **Last backup rehearsal**, **Show earlier rehearsals** expands older recorded
results. **Load more rehearsals** reads more; **Hide earlier rehearsals** folds them
away. Give the operator the failed rehearsal's reason and the affected workspace checks,
rather than assuming a newer backup fixes the cause. **How to rehearse a restore** is
operator guidance; use the [restore runbook](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/) with them.

**Could not refresh** means Operations could not obtain a fresh reading. Check the
reported time before forwarding figures. Use **Refresh** once the connection is restored.
A failure to read Deployment is also different from a capability being Off: retry the
read before asking for a configuration change. None of these pages grants permissions
or modifies records, so there is no removal or undo procedure on them.
guide/src/content/docs/administer/mail.m:
---
title: Mail
description: Set up outgoing mail, understand delivery states and help people receive account links and notices.
reader: access-admin
---

Use **Settings › This instance › Mail** to connect refiroo to your organisation’s mail server. You need **Security administration** for the whole instance. Mail carries password links and, when people choose them, inbox notices and digests. It never sends a password or an authenticator code.

Under **Send mail through**, choose **SMTP server** or **Microsoft 365**. One method is used at a time. Saving one replaces the other method’s saved fields and credentials. There is no automatic fallback to the other method.

Every message includes plain text and an HTML version. The default layout embeds the refiroo mascot and wordmark; an operator can replace the layout and logo under **E-mail template**. If the model gives the product its own name, that name appears in the message.

Without saved mail settings, nothing is sent. Administrators can still copy a new person’s password link and pass it on. Follow [Set up mail](/docs/guide/administer/set-up-mail/) to configure and test SMTP delivery.

## E-mail template

**Settings › This instance › E-mail template** changes the layout around every invitation, password reset, notice, digest and test message. One saved template applies to the whole instance. This page needs the instance-wide **Operations** permission, included in the **Operator** role; Security administration for the Mail page alone does not grant it. Until a template is saved, refiroo uses its own layout.

### Write and preview the layout

1. Open **E-mail template**. In **Markdown**, write the surrounding message. The toolbar offers **Bold**, **Italic**, **Link**, **Heading** and **List**. Use **Insert placeholder…** to insert a value where the caret stands.
2. Keep the message placeholder exactly once. The available placeholders are:

   | Placeholder | What appears in the mail |
   | --- | --- |
   | `{{content}}` | The message's own heading, text and action; required exactly once. |
   | `{{product_name}}` | The product's name. |
   | `{{instance_url}}` | The address of this instance. |
   | `{{recipient_name}}` | The person's name, or “there” when no name is available. |
   | `{{logo}}` | The uploaded logo, or the default mark. |

3. Read **Preview** beside the editor. It updates with sample values after you stop typing. Choose **Light paper**, **Dark paper** and **Plain text** to inspect the alternatives. Preview saves and sends nothing. A refused draft shows **The draft cannot be previewed** and leaves the last good preview visible: correct the error before relying on that preview.
4. Choose **Save**. Unknown placeholders, a missing or repeated message placeholder, or more than 20,000 characters are refused. Raw HTML and Markdown images are not carried into mail. Links may use HTTP, HTTPS or mail addresses; unsafe links are omitted. Use the logo control for your image.

### Add a logo and send a test

1. Under **Logo**, choose **Upload a logo**, or drop the image onto the field. Use PNG, JPEG or SVG without script, up to 512 KB. Uploading saves the logo immediately; **Remove logo** returns to the default mark. The logo is embedded in the mail. Many mail programs do not draw SVG, so use PNG or JPEG when recipients need wider support.
2. Save your Markdown before choosing **Send a test to me**. The test uses the saved template, not unsaved text, and goes to your own account's e-mail address. Mail delivery must be configured and your account must have an address. If **The test could not be sent** appears, read its reason and correct the address or delivery problem before retrying.
3. Check the actual message, including its plain-text version, in the recipient's mail program. The preview is not proof of how every mail program draws the message or that delivery reaches the inbox.
4. To restore the original layout, choose **Reset to default…**, then **Reset to default** in the confirmation. This deletes both the saved Markdown and uploaded logo. Cancel keeps them.

If another operator saves first, your older save is refused. Reload, review their changes and reapply only what is still needed. Template changes are not included in the security audit.

## Mail server

**Server** and **Port** identify the outgoing mail service. **Connection** offers:

| Choice | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| STARTTLS (usually port 587) | The server upgrades the connection to encryption before login. |
| TLS (usually port 465) | The connection is encrypted from the start. |
| None: not encrypted (a relay on a trusted network) | Only for a relay that requires no login. |
