3. Correct a server problem in **Mail server**. Waiting messages retry automatically; a failed password message needs a new link. Do not expect a stopped or failed message to restart.
4. To stop a waiting message, choose its **Stop sending**, check the recipient and confirm **Stop sending**. **Keep trying** leaves it queued. Its text is erased, but its existing link remains valid until used, replaced or expired.

Removing the mail settings stops sending; waiting messages remain until their delivery window ends. Use **Remove settings…**, read the warning and confirm **Remove them** only when that is intended. People choose their own notice mail and digests under **Settings › You › Notification email**; configuring a server does not opt them in.

## Replace credentials or move the site

1. For a replacement mail password, enter it in **Password**, keep the agreed server and
   sender, and choose **Save**. Blank keeps an existing password for the same server; it
   does not replace an expired one.
2. Send a test and check both delivery and the link destination. If the site moved, save
   the new **Application address** before creating any new password links.
3. Check Waiting messages. Existing links keep their old address. Where that address no
   longer works, stop the waiting entry when possible and make a fresh password link;
   do not assume changing the setting rewrites the outbox.

After removing mail settings, recovery means entering and testing them again. Previously
failed messages do not restart when settings return, and the deleted password cannot be
read back from refiroo.

---
title: Manage a group
description: Create a group, add or remove members and grant shared access.
reader: access-admin
---

Use a group when several people need the same roles. You need **Security administration**.
See [People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/) for how local and provider groups differ.

## Create a local group

1. Open **Settings › People and access › Groups**. Use **Search groups** (**Group name**) first to see whether the
   intended group already exists. Choose a result to manage it, or **New group** to create one.
2. Enter **Name** and **Description (optional)**. The description can explain who belongs
   and why. If a **Members** choice is offered, choose **Added here** for membership managed in refiroo.
3. Choose **Add group**. The group opens with its roles and members. **Cancel** closes
   without creating it. If saving fails, read **Not saved**, correct the problem and retry.

![Empty Groups list with search and New group](/docs/screens/admin-groups.png)

*Above: the reference instance has no groups yet.*

![New group dialog with Name and optional Description](/docs/screens/admin-group-new.png)

*Above: no provider supplies groups on the reference instance, so the dialog shows the local fields only.*

## Add people and shared roles

1. On the group's page choose **Add members**. In **Search and tick**, search by name
   or e-mail and tick the intended people. Already-present and deactivated people
   cannot be selected for addition.
2. For a longer list, choose **Paste a list**. Enter **E-mail addresses**,
   one per line or separated by commas or semicolons, up to 500. Choose **Check the list**
   (or **Check … lines** when a count appears). Review the results before adding. Resolve
   unmatched or ambiguous entries rather than choosing someone by guesswork.
3. Review the selected people and choose **Add members**, or the button showing the number
   to add. Check the resulting Members list and success message. A person deactivated while
   the dialog was open can be left out; read the reported count.
4. Choose **Grant** in the group's roles section. Follow
   [Grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) to select roles and workspaces.
   Every member receives that source of access; adding members alone grants nothing if the group has no roles.
5. Open a member's People page to check that the role appears as coming through this group.
   The access applies on their next request; they do not need a new account.

![Local group with two fictional members selected and controls to add or remove members](/docs/screens/admin-group-members.png)

## Change or remove membership

1. Find the group by name and select it. Select its name or description where it stands,
   edit it, then leave the field or press Enter to save. Escape puts the old text back;
   an unchanged input saves nothing. The save notice offers **Undo**. If refused, read the
   reason under the input, then correct it and choose **Save again**, or **Cancel** to abandon
   the edit. This does not change who belongs or the group's grants.
2. To remove a local member, use their row’s **Remove**. For several, tick their rows, or use **Select every member shown**, and
   choose **Remove … from the group**. **Clear** clears the selection without removing anyone. Check the resulting list. Their direct roles and
   roles from other groups remain.
3. To remove the whole group, choose **Delete group** and read the confirmation. Confirm
   **Delete group** only if its memberships and all its grants should be removed.
   The people remain and keep their direct grants.

A change that would leave no active person holding Security administration is refused, including a grant through this group. Removing several members is all-or-nothing: if one removal would lose the last administrator, none of the selected members is removed. Establish another
administrator before removing that membership or deleting that group. If details changed
while you were working, reload and review the current members and grants before retrying.

## Use a provider group

When a configured sign-in provider supplies groups, **New group** offers **From a sign-in provider**.
Choose it, select **Provider** and enter **Claim value** exactly as supplied by the sign-in
administrator. This is the provider's group identifier, which need not be its readable name.
Create the group and grant roles before anyone signs in if access must be ready on their first visit.

A provider group's page shows **Members seen**. Membership is updated at each person's
provider sign-in; people who have not signed in are absent from this list. Make membership
changes in the provider, not with local Add or Remove controls. The group name can be
made readable in refiroo without changing the provider's identifier.

For a provider group, **Members seen** can be empty even when the provider has members who have not signed in yet. Its roles can already be granted. Local group deletion and bulk removal do not change membership at the provider.

---
title: Create a client
description: Give an integration a named client, save its secret and grant the access it needs.
reader: access-admin
---

Use a client for a system that works without a person signing in. You need **Security administration**.
Agree with the integration owner what operations and workspaces it needs first.
See [Clients for other systems](/docs/administer/clients/) for the access and secret rules.

## Create and save the credentials

1. Open **Settings › Connections › Clients**. Search by **Name** to check whether the system
   already has a client. Check **Deactivated** as well before creating a duplicate.
2. Choose **New client**. Enter **Name**, a name people can recognise in access lists and
   history. Choose **Add client**. **Cancel** creates nothing.
3. In **Copy the client's secret**, copy **Client secret** and **Client ID** into the
   integration's agreed secure store. The full secret is shown once; after closing, only
   its last four characters identify it. Choose **I have copied it** after saving both.
4. If creation is refused, read the message and correct the problem. If the client exists
   but its one-time secret was lost, rotate its secret instead of creating it again.

![New client dialog with Name and Create and show its secret](/docs/screens/admin-client-new.png)

*Above: the reference instance's New client dialog is open but has not created another client.*

## Grant access

1. On the new client's page, choose **Grant** in **Access**. A new client has no access.
2. Choose **Roles** under **What** for management operations. Select the least role or roles that cover
   the agreed work and choose where they apply. Narrow writes if appropriate, as described
   in [Grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/).
3. For reading declared consumer APIs, choose **Consumer APIs** under **What**. Tick the
   grid cell for each API and workspace it needs, then choose **Add grant**, or **Add N grants** when several are selected. Row and column
   headings tick the whole line; a ticked grey cell is already granted. A management role
   does not substitute for these consumer grants.
4. Check **Access** on the client page. Confirm the workspace, grant and any write restriction
   before handing the details to the integration owner.

![Client detail showing its ID, secret summary and Consumer API grant](/docs/screens/admin-client.png)

*Above: Stops reader (guide) can read the Stops API in Graubünden. The failed webhooks
section below is a load error, not an empty-list confirmation.*

## Prove the handover

Ask the integration owner to sign the system in using the ID and secret, then exercise the
intended read or write. Send them the [integration authentication reference](/docs/api/)
for the technical sequence. Check the client's last-authentication status and its secret's
**Last used** time afterwards.

A sign-in failure calls for checking the saved ID, secret, expiry and active state.
If sign-in succeeds but an operation is refused, check the role or consumer grant, the
workspace and any write restriction. Expanding access to the whole instance is not needed
merely to correct a missing workspace grant.

---
title: Grant a consumer API to a client
description: Allow a system to read one declared consumer API in selected workspaces.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Security administration** and an existing client. A consumer API grant gives that client access to one API in one workspace. A management role does not open consumer data, and people and groups cannot receive these grants. See [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/).

1. Open **Settings › Connections › Clients**, find the intended system with **Search clients** and select it. Check its **Client ID** and active state; do not grant to a similarly named system by guesswork.
2. Under **Access**, choose **Grant**. In **What**, choose **Consumer APIs**. This is normally the initial choice for a client. **Roles** is the separate choice for management access.
3. In the grid, find the API’s row and the workspace’s column. Tick the intersection. Each tick is a separate grant. A row or column heading selects the whole line; Shift extends a range, so review every selected cell before proceeding.
4. A grey tick means already granted. **not in this model** means the workspace’s model does not declare that API. **unavailable** means the choices could not be read; reopen the dialog after resolving that load failure. It is not proof that the API is absent.
5. Read the sentence describing what the client may read and choose **Add grant**, or **Add N grants** for several. If some grants fail, the successful ones remain; the failed choices stay selected with their reasons. Correct those choices and use **Try again**. Closing does not undo grants already made.
6. Check **Access** for **Consumer API:** followed by the API’s name and the intended workspace. Give the integration owner the agreed access and point them to [The API reference and Consumer APIs pages](/docs/administer/api-reference-and-consumer-api-pages/) for connection details.
7. Ask the integration owner to verify a new request with that client. Its available consumer API list includes only granted APIs. A grant for another workspace does not carry over, and consumer grants cannot be narrowed to selected record types.

![Consumer API grant grid with API rows and workspace columns](/docs/screens/admin-grant-consumer-api.png)

To withdraw access, remove the specific grant from **Access** and confirm the named removal. Other roles and consumer grants remain. If a later model no longer declares the granted API, review that stale grant and replace it with the intended current declaration; a remembered old name is not permission.

---
title: Rotate signing keys
description: Start a normal signing key replacement or retire the current key after suspected disclosure.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Security administration**. Choose the normal or emergency procedure below
according to the reason for replacement. See [Signing keys](/docs/administer/signing-keys/)
for the automatic schedule and how these keys differ from client secrets.

## Start a normal replacement

1. Open **Settings › People and access › Signing keys**. Note the key marked **Signing** and its
   **Created** time. A previously replaced key may still show **Verifying until**.
2. Choose **Start a new key** when ready. **This acts immediately, without a dialog.**
   It is not a preview or the start of a confirmation sequence.
3. Check that a new row is **Signing** and the previous key has a replacement time and a
   verification deadline. Existing access continues until it expires. People and clients
   move to the replacement through normal renewal; no secret handover is needed.

![Signing keys list with current and replaced key states](/docs/screens/admin-signing-keys.png)

*Above: the reference instance shows a new Signing key and a previous key still verifying.*

## Retire the current key after suspected disclosure

1. On the same page, check which key is **Signing**. Choose **Retire the current key now**.
2. Read **Retire the current key now?**. Access signed with that key is refused from the
   next request. People's sessions renew without a fresh sign-in; clients must retry with
   fresh access obtained using their unchanged client secret.
3. Choose **Retire it now** to proceed, or **Cancel** to leave the key in place.
4. Check the list for the retired key's **Retired** time and a new **Signing** key.
   Have affected integration owners check renewal if their systems report a refusal.

![Confirmation for immediate retirement of the current signing key](/docs/screens/admin-signing-keys-retire.png)

*Above: the reference retirement confirmation is open but has not been confirmed.*

If the action reports a failure, read the message and reload the key list to establish the
current state before trying again. A signing-key retirement does not replace a leaked
client secret; use [Rotate a client secret](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-client-secret/)
for that separate credential.

---
title: Manage an assistant's access
description: Connect an assistant, create an agent client, register or block an assistant and review its calls.
reader: access-admin
---

Use **Settings › Connections › Agent access** with **Security administration** across the instance. Read [Agent access](/docs/administer/agent-access/) first for permissions, data sent, call retention and the limits on prepared changes. External assistants may send permitted data to their own provider and incur charges there; refiroo's built-in AI send levels do not control them.

## Connect a person's assistant

1. Open **Settings › Connections › Agent access**. If it says **Agent access is off**, ask the operator to enable it and restart the server. The page cannot switch it on.
2. Under **How to connect**, copy **Address** and give it to the person connecting their MCP assistant. Use the address shown rather than constructing one from the browser's current page.
3. Ask the person to add that address in their assistant. It opens this instance's sign-in page, naming the assistant and where it returns. They should check those details before signing in. The name is what the assistant says about itself.
4. After sign-in, the assistant uses the person's existing grants, limited to reading and preparing changes. It does not need a new Agent role. Under **Assistants people sign in with**, check its **Returns to**, **Signed in now** and **Last used**.

If sign-in cannot register the assistant, use the registration steps below or ask the operator to check the allowed return hosts. If it connects but has no useful tools, review the person's workspace grants. **Browse** allows reads; **Work in change sets** allows preparation. Neither gives publication through the assistant.

A person stops their own connection under **Settings › Account**, in **Where you’re signed in**. The session name includes **(assistant)**. **Sign out** on that session ends its access. For all users of one assistant, block it below.

## Create a client for a system's assistant

1. On **Agent access**, under **Agent clients**, choose **New agent client**. This is different from **New client** on the ordinary Clients page.
2. Enter **Name**, then choose **Add agent client**. The dialog **Copy the client's secret** shows **Client ID** and the secret once. Give these to the responsible integrator through your organisation's secure handover method. Choose **I have copied it** only after keeping what they need; the secret cannot be shown again.
3. Open the new client's name under **Agent clients**. Its normal client detail page opens. In **Access**, use **Grant access** to grant only the required role and workspaces. The **Agent** role gives Browse and Work in change sets; a custom role can provide a smaller set. A consumer API grant alone allows only that API's lookup tool and information about the connection's access.
4. Ask the integrator to configure the system's assistant with this client and the copied connection address. The [integration instructions](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/) explain the connection details.
5. Return to **Agent access**. Check **Access**, **Last used** and **Calls, 30 days** on its row, then inspect **Calls** for the result. A new client has no access until you grant it.

![New agent client dialog with its Name field and creation action](/docs/screens/admin-agent-new-client.png)

For a lost secret, use [Rotate a client secret](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-client-secret/). To stop a system's assistant, open its client and choose **Deactivate**, then confirm. Its next request is refused. Restoring a client does not widen its grants.

## Register an assistant for people

Use this when self-registration is off or its return host is not allowed. Registration does not give the assistant its own workspace access: each person still signs in and works through their own grants.

1. Under **Assistants people sign in with**, choose **New assistant**.
2. Enter **Name**, the name people see on the sign-in page. Under **Return addresses**, enter the exact addresses supplied by the assistant's administrator, one per line. They must use HTTPS, or HTTP loopback addresses on the same computer. Enter at most ten addresses, each at most 2,000 characters, without a fragment.
3. Choose **Add assistant**. The assistant appears in the list and people can sign in with it. If **The assistant was not registered** appears, correct the reported problem and try again.

![Register an assistant dialog showing Name and Return addresses](/docs/screens/admin-agent-register.png)

## Block or restore an assistant

1. Find it under **Assistants people sign in with**. Check the name and **Returns to** so you block the intended one.
2. Choose **Block**. The confirmation names the assistant and how many sessions end. Confirm with **Block**.
3. The row shows **Blocked**. No one can sign in with it, and existing sessions end on their next call.
4. To allow it again, choose **Restore**. People can sign in again; ended sessions stay ended.

![Confirmation to block an assistant with its affected session count](/docs/screens/admin-agent-block.png)

Use client deactivation for a system's assistant, and account sign-out for one person's session. Blocking an assistant registration affects all people signed in through that registration.

## Investigate a call

Read **Calls**, newest first. **Who** is the person or client; **Through** identifies the assistant or says **Its own client**. **Tool** is the operation it asked for and **Arguments** lists names only, never values. **Outcome** says **Answered**, **Refused**, **Limit reached** or **Failed**. Choose **Load more** for older calls.

For **Refused**, inspect the caller's grants and the work it requested. An assistant cannot reach a colleague's change set or approve or publish, even when its person can. A submitted change set is frozen to it; a person must deal with the review. For **Limit reached**, allow the wait requested by the service before another attempt. For **Failed**, ask the integrator for the error returned to the assistant, then involve the operator as needed. The call list shows the outcome, not the failure explanation or the assistant’s conversation.

Calls normally remain for 90 days. The client row's 30-day count is a reporting window. Check actual data changes in [the audit and history](/docs/administer/audit/), and review prepared changes through [the normal approval process](/docs/administer/approval-policies/).

To replace registered return addresses, register a new assistant with the corrected
addresses, have people reconnect and sign in, then block the old registration. There is
no registration edit or delete control. Blocked and administrator registrations are kept;
inactivity cleanup applies only to unblocked self-registrations without an open session.

---
title: Add a person
description: Create a local account, pass on its first-password link and grant access.
reader: access-admin
---

Use this guide for someone who signs in with a refiroo password. You need
**Security administration**. For ordinary password sign-in, local sign-in must be on. Creating an account alone does not give it the retained recovery route when local sign-in is off. For someone using your organisation's
provider, first sign-in creates their person instead; see
[People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/) for that route and linking existing accounts.

## Create the account

1. Open **Settings › People and access › People**. Check the Active list or search by name
   or e-mail to avoid creating another account for the same person. Check **Deactivated**
   too; **Restore** reactivates an existing person with their retained roles and groups.
2. Choose **New person**. Enter **Name**, the display name used in lists and history, up to 200 characters.
3. Enter **E-mail**, the address they sign in with. Another person cannot have the same address.
4. Leave **An administrator manages this person’s sign-in** unticked for someone who manages
   their own password and sign-in methods. Tick it for an account whose sign-in you look after,
   such as a shared reception account or an account on a training machine. Its help text explains
   that they cannot change their password, second factor or passkeys, or sign out other browsers.
   Only someone with **Security administration** can set this option. It is off by default.
   Wrong passwords entered for a shared account's e-mail address slow sign-in for everyone
   using it. See [People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/#sign-in-managed-by-an-administrator)
   for the limits and recovery options.
5. Choose **Create and make a password link**. **Cancel** leaves the person uncreated.
   If a field is refused, correct the named problem and submit again.

## Pass on the password link

1. When **Pass on the password link** opens, copy the link using its copy control.
   Give it to the intended person through your agreed private channel. They choose their own password.
2. Read the expiry shown in the dialog. The link works once and a newer link replaces it.
   Choose **I have copied it** only after saving or passing it on; it is not shown again.
3. With mail configured and an address on the person, creation also queues the link for mail. The dialog reports that outcome. **Mail it to …** is available to make and mail a replacement.
   Mailing makes a replacement link, also shown in the dialog. Use that newest link rather
   than the earlier copy. Check the dialog's sent-to message; do not assume mail was sent.
4. If the person was created but no link dialog appeared, open their page and choose
   **Make a password link** (or **Reset password** once a password is set). Do not create them again. This click makes the link
   immediately, with no confirmation before it.

![One-time password-link dialog with copy control, expiry and acknowledgement](/docs/screens/admin-person-reset-password.png)

*Above: a reset link for fictional Rita Approver, not a newly created person. Creation uses
the same link dialog. Its example address is not one to reuse.*

## Give them access and check the result

1. On their page, inspect **Roles**. A new person has none. Follow
   [Grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) for the intended workspace, or add them
   to a [group](/docs/guide/administer/manage-a-group/) that holds the required roles.
2. Ask them to open the link and set a password. A rejected password gives a reason;
   they must choose another. An expired, replaced or used link needs a new **Reset password** link.
3. Ask them to sign in and check the expected workspace and actions. If the instance requires
   a second factor, someone who manages their own sign-in sets one up before their session starts.
   An administrator-managed account with no factor signs in with the password alone, even
   when the instance requires a second factor. If the workspace is missing,
   review the grant's workspace and whether its role includes Browse.

Creating a person does not send them data or grant access automatically. Keep the e-mail address
correct; use **Edit…** for later name or e-mail corrections.

For delivery problems, check [Mail › Messages](/docs/administer/mail/#messages-and-retries). A queued message can still fail; the one-time dialog is not proof of receipt.

---
title: Find out why a webhook paused
description: Diagnose retrying or suspended delivery and resume from the appropriate position.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Integration administration** in the source workspace. Work with the receiver’s owner: a delivery failure can be a receiver, network, certificate or configuration problem. [The Webhooks page](/docs/administer/webhooks/) lists all suspension reasons.

## Find the cause

1. Open **Settings › Connections › Webhooks** and select the intended receiver. **Retrying** means refiroo is still trying a failed request; **Suspended** means sending has stopped.
2. Read **Configuration**, especially the suspension heading, listed findings, last error, attempt count and next attempt. A failed request prevents later changes passing it. After 24 hours of unsuccessful delivery it is suspended.
3. Open **Deliveries**, filter **Status** if needed and choose **Refresh**. Open the affected event. Inspect **Attempts** and the selected attempt’s answer. An unreachable host, TLS failure, timeout, redirect and receiver error need different repairs. Give the relevant reason to the operator or receiver owner; do not share record content unnecessarily.
4. For **Delivery failed**, fix the receiver or use **Edit…** to correct its URL. Changing a failed destination retries at once. For **The model changed** or **A filter matches nothing**, edit the fields identified in the findings and choose **Save**. If another person changed the webhook, review the reloaded configuration before saving again.
5. For **The contract version changed**, read **Accepted** and **Served now**. The version the receiver accepted is no longer served. Ask its owner to check the current version before resuming: resume accepts that version. A version retained by the active model keeps delivering in its own shape; simply raising the current version does not suspend it. If events or filters no longer exist, fix the findings under **The model changed** first. For **The workspace was retired**, ask a workspace administrator to reactivate it if delivery should continue. Otherwise delete the subscription after agreeing this with its owner.

A workspace-events webhook does not depend on a consumer contract version. For that source,
check the workspace, receiver and selected change-set steps instead. A record edit alone does
not produce a workspace change-set notification.

## Resume without skipping changes

1. Once the cause is fixed, choose **Resume…**. In **Resume this webhook?**, keep **Continue from › The first event not acknowledged**.
2. Choose **Resume**. refiroo checks the subscription against the active model and workspace again. If it refuses, read the findings under **The webhook was not resumed**, correct them and repeat.
3. Check **Deliveries** for a fresh attempt and ask the receiver owner to verify the result. A request can arrive again; the receiver must cope with repeated events.

![Resume dialog for the fictional webhook suspended by an administrator, with continuation choices](/docs/screens/admin-webhook-resume.png)

## Recover after events expired

1. If **Events expired** is shown, record the range lost and the publication named in the details, and arrange a fresh synchronisation with the receiver owner. The publication may be older than the current feed head, so it is not enough on its own. Continuing from the old position is no longer possible.
2. Choose **Resume…**, select **Now, with reset** and read the warning that waiting changes are skipped. A refusal for expired events also selects reset for you; review it before proceeding.
3. Choose **Reset and resume**. Reset moves the subscription to the feed head shown in the refusal message; changes before it are not delivered. Then have the receiver reload from current data taken after the reset (a new publication or a live export), not from the older publication named in the details. Reset comes first so later changes are still delivered during recovery.
4. Verify the refreshed data and subsequent deliveries with the receiver owner. Do not use reset merely to clear an unexplained error.

**Resend** on a saved delivery repeats that request. It does not repair the cause or resume a suspended subscription; use it only for an agreed replay. See [Deliveries](/docs/administer/webhooks/#deliveries).

---
title: Set an approval policy
description: Require reviewed publication in a workspace and decide whether a second person must approve.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Workspace administration** to change the policy. Someone with
**Security administration** grants the approver roles. Read
[Approval policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/) for the effect on publication and Live edits.

## Establish approvers

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**, select the intended workspace and choose **Access**.
   Check who holds a role with **Approve publications** there, directly, through a group
   or across the instance. Data owner is the predefined role with that action group.
2. If approval rights are missing, have the access administrator
   [grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) before requiring approval.
   Data steward can publish but cannot approve someone else's submission.
3. If submitters must never decide their own work, arrange another approver for every
   submitter who is also an approver. One person holding several roles is still one person.

## Save the policy

1. Open the workspace's **Approval** tab. Read the count of people or clients that can approve.
2. Tick **Changes need approval before they are published** to require reviewed publication.
   Leaving it off allows people with Publish to publish directly.
3. To require a different decision maker, also tick
   **The person who submitted a change set cannot approve it**. It is available only with
   the first setting on. Without it, someone permitted to publish and approve their own
   work can publish in one step.
4. Read any warning about missing approvers. The form can still save even if requests
   would have nobody to decide them; correct the grants before relying on the policy.
5. Choose **Save approval policy**. Wait for **Approval policy saved.** The checkboxes
   alone do not save the change.

![Workspace Approval tab showing both policy choices and Save approval policy](/docs/screens/admin-approval.png)

*Above: Graubünden requires approval, allows a submitter with approval rights to decide
their own work, and has two qualifying people or clients. Rita Approver is fictional.*

## Check the result

Ask a person preparing work to submit a change set and an authorised approver to find it
on Home or in their notices. Follow
[Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/) for the complete review task.
With the second-person rule on, a submitter's own review says a second person must decide.

If saving reports that the policy changed meanwhile, choose **Reload the policy**, inspect
the current values and apply the intended change again. Other failures show their reason;
check it before retrying. To stop requiring approval, clear the first setting and save.
That also clears the second-person setting. This policy governs change-set publication;
it does not remove any grants that allow direct edits to Live.

A saved policy also applies to the next decision on work already waiting. It does not
decide those requests automatically. With the second-person rule on, the submitter cannot
send their own submission back; they can withdraw it, or another approver can decide it.

---
title: Narrow a grant to record types
description: Limit writes to selected applications or record types in one workspace.
reader: access-admin
---

Use a narrowed grant when someone may change only part of a workspace’s data. You need **Security administration**. This limits writes; **Browse** still reads the whole workspace. Use separate workspaces if readers must not see each other’s data. Read [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/#how-grants-combine) before proceeding.

1. Open **Settings › People and access › People** or **Groups**, or **Settings › Connections › Clients** and select the recipient. Inspect their direct and inherited grants first. Grants combine: another unrestricted grant can allow writes outside the restriction you are adding.
2. Choose **Grant**. For a client, choose **Roles**, rather than **Consumer APIs**. Select exactly one role containing a group that can be narrowed: **Edit live**, **Work in change sets**, **Publish**, **Bulk and import**, or **Copy and move**.
3. Under **Where**, choose **Workspaces** and select exactly one workspace with **Add workspace**. The narrowing control appears only for one role in one workspace. Instance grants and consumer API grants cannot be narrowed.
4. Under **Narrow what they may change**, choose **Only these applications and record types**. Select the intended applications and record types from that workspace’s model. Selecting an application permits its records; selecting a record type permits that type. Either match is enough, so choose a type alone when the whole application would be too broad.
5. Read the resulting permission sentence and the warning that reading is never narrowed. Check the selected role, workspace and restrictions, then choose **Add grant**.
6. Inspect the resulting **Narrowed to (writes)** entry. Have the recipient check **Account › What you can do** and try the intended task. A relationship can be changed when either endpoint is writable. A batch or import can refuse individual items outside the allowed types; publishing a change set with any unpermitted type is refused as a whole.

![Grant dialog limited to one role and workspace with record-type narrowing](/docs/screens/admin-grant-narrowed.png)

If an unrestricted grant already exists, remove that source separately after arranging the replacement. Simply adding a narrower grant does not reduce existing access. Group-supplied grants must be reviewed at their group too.

After a model change, review grants marked stale. A missing application or type no longer permits those writes; replace the old grant with the intended choices from the current model. If a grant is refused, keep successful grants in mind, read the retained failure reason and retry only after correcting it.

---
title: Check the AI provider
description: Read the AI configuration, send a data-free test request and investigate a failed call.
reader: access-admin
---

Use this guide to check whether the configured AI provider answers. You need **Operations** across the instance. The test can incur provider usage, but sends none of your reference data. It checks the provider, not the built-in assistant.

Read [AI settings and access](/docs/administer/ai/) for data sent, permissions, costs and retention. Only an operator can change the server configuration.

1. Open **Settings › This instance › AI**. Under **What is switched on**, check **Provider**. If neither feature is configured, the page says **Neither the assistant nor an AI provider is set up**. If only the assistant is on, there is no provider test button. Ask the operator to configure a provider if your task needs one.
2. Read **Settings**. Check **Model**, **Endpoint**, whether **Key** is set, and **What may be sent**. The secret is never displayed. A provider hosted outside your organisation receives the data allowed for each feature; make sure that arrangement is acceptable before inviting people to use it.
3. Read **What the AI provider is asked**. Each feature says **Available** or **Unavailable**. An unavailable feature needs more information than the configured send level permits; a successful connection test cannot make it available. Review the data policy with the operator rather than assuming the test failed.
4. Under **Test request**, choose **Send a test request**. The button says **Sending…** while it waits. The fixed request contains none of your reference data, and makes a call recorded below.
5. On success, **The AI provider answered** shows how long the answer took and which model answered. On failure, **The test request failed** gives the reason. This does not prove that suggestions are correct or that the built-in assistant works.

![AI provider test result with the answered notice and the recorded test call](/docs/screens/admin-ai-test-answered.png)

## If the test failed

Read the reason before retrying. If the key was refused, ask the operator to check the provider account and credentials. If the provider could not be reached or timed out, ask them to check the connection, service and timeout. An unreadable answer means the provider did not return what refiroo requested; ask the operator to check the provider's compatibility. Configuration changes require a restart.

![Failed AI provider test showing its reason and failed call](/docs/screens/admin-ai-test-failed.png)

After the cause is fixed, choose **Send a test request** again. Each attempt is another call and can incur usage.

## Check the call record

In **Calls**, find the newest **Test request** row. Check **Asked by**, **Model**, **Outcome**, **Tokens in / out**, **Cost** and **Duration**. A failed row gives its reason. **Load more calls** opens older entries when available; the totals cover the last 30 days.

A dash in **Cost** means no cost was reported. Check actual charges with the provider. When content logging is enabled, **Show what was sent and answered** displays the retained content; the normal default keeps call metadata without that content. The setting does not control an assistant's working files or transcripts.

To check a real feature next, use it with the relevant permissions, review what it proposes and find its call here. AI proposals still need human review and the normal permissions to apply them.

---
title: Find who changed something
description: Follow data history to its author, filter their changes and inspect security activity separately.
reader: access-admin
---

Start with the record or workspace when you do not know the author. Start with People or
Clients when you do. You need permission to read the affected workspace to inspect its data;
Security administration alone does not grant that. See [Who changed what](/docs/administer/audit/)
for the scope of each history view.

## Start from the changed data

1. Open the affected record and its **History**. Find the change by time and read the
   before and after values and the named person or client. For a broader search, open
   **Settings › Workspaces**, select the workspace and choose **Activity**.
2. Filter the workspace's activity to the relevant work and period. Use the entry's
   workspace, change set and publication context to distinguish authored changes from
   changes applied by publication. Follow [History](/docs/use/history/) for those controls.
3. Follow the author's name where it is linked to open their Changes page. If you already
   know the person, use the route below instead.

## Start from a person or client

1. Open **Settings › People and access › People** or **Settings › Connections › Clients**. Search and select the identity.
   Check their e-mail address or client ID if similar names exist. For a deactivated identity,
   use the **Deactivated** list.
2. Choose **See changes**. The page names that person or client and lists their visible
   changes, newest first, grouped by day. It can cover several workspaces.
3. Set **Workspace** to the relevant workspace, or keep **All workspaces**.
   Under **What**, choose **Records**, **Relationships**, **Change sets**, **Publications**
   or **Model**, or keep **Everything**.
4. Choose **Period**: **Last 24 hours**, **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days** or **Any time**.
   If no result matches, widen the filters. Use **Load more** to retrieve older entries.
5. Read the action, subject, changed-field summary, time and workspace. Open a linked title
   to inspect the surviving subject. Use the record's own History for the changed values;
   the person's Changes page is a summary.

![Person's changes with workspace, kind and period filters and dated entries](/docs/screens/admin-audit-person.png)

*Above: fictional Rita Approver's page shows her publication and the Davos Platz height
change applied by it in Graubünden. These are related entries, not proof of two separate manual edits.*

An empty list does not prove there were no changes outside your access. Check that you
can read the workspace. If the changed record was removed, its history entry can remain
without an openable record. A renamed person is shown by their current name.

## Find an account or access change

1. Return to the person's or client's security page and scroll to **Recent activity**.
   This is separate from their data changes.
2. Choose **Signing in**, **Roles and groups** or **Account** to narrow the events,
   or **All** to include every security kind associated with that identity.
3. Read the event, time and named actor. Use **Load more** for older activity and
   **Show fewer** to reduce the displayed list.
4. If loading fails, choose **Retry** after reading the error. A failed load is not an
   empty audit result. Do not look for passwords or secrets in this history; they are not shown.

![Person detail at the Recent activity section with its four filters](/docs/screens/admin-grants-person.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's security activity follows their roles and groups. A one-time password
link creation appears as an event without revealing the link itself.*

There is no separate instance-wide audit page to open. Use these identity views and the
workspace's Activity for the question at hand.

---
title: Help someone who lost a device
description: Restore sign-in after a lost authenticator or passkey device and end unsafe sessions.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Security administration** to change another person's sign-in methods.
Confirm the person's identity through your organisation's recovery process before removing
protection. A password reset alone does not bypass a second factor. See
[Sign-in and second factors](/docs/administer/sign-in/) for how the methods work.

If an administrator manages this account's sign-in, the person cannot replace their own
sign-in methods or end other browsers' sessions on Account. Use the administrator actions
below to remove a lost authenticator app or passkey, make a password link and sign them out.
They can still sign out of their current browser. A forgotten-password request sends no
mail for this account; make the link yourself. See
[People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/#sign-in-managed-by-an-administrator)
for changing this setting.

## Check the remaining ways in

1. Ask whether they have another registered passkey, a working authenticator app or a saved
   recovery code. On the sign-in screen, **Use a recovery code instead** lets an app user
   use one of their unused codes.
2. If they can sign in and manage their own sign-in, have them open **Account** to replace
   the lost method and manage their sessions. For an administrator-managed account, continue
   with the administrator actions below even if the person can sign in. A person with only passkeys has no app recovery codes; another passkey
   may still work. See [Your account](/docs/use/account/).
3. If they use the organisation's provider, recover the provider's factor there. Removing
   a refiroo authenticator does not reset a factor managed by the provider.

## Remove a lost local authenticator

1. Open **Settings › People and access › People**, search for the person and select them.
   Check their name, e-mail address and sign-in method.
2. Under **Sign-in**, choose **Remove second factor…** beside
   **Second factor: authenticator app**. This button appears only when an app is set up.
3. Read the confirmation, then choose **Remove second factor**. Their app and its recovery
   codes stop working. **Cancel** leaves the factor in place. The change is recorded in activity.
4. For someone who manages their own sign-in, a required second factor means setting up a
   new app at their next password sign-in if no passkey remains. Otherwise, ask them to set
   it up again on **Account** and save new recovery codes. An administrator-managed account
   cannot set up a replacement. With no remaining factor, it signs in with the password
   alone even if the instance requires a second factor.

## Remove a lost passkey

1. On the same person's page, find the named passkey under **Sign-in**. Compare its added
   and last-used times with the person to identify the lost device's registration.
2. Choose **Remove passkey…** for that entry. Check the name in the confirmation and choose
   **Remove passkey**. That registration can no longer sign them in; other passkeys remain.
3. Have them use another available sign-in method. Someone who manages their own sign-in
   can register a replacement on Account; an administrator-managed account cannot.
   If they also lost their password, use the password procedure below. An app still set up
   remains a required step; remove a lost app separately if necessary.

![Person's page with password status and account recovery actions](/docs/screens/admin-person-admin.png)

*Above: Guide Admin has a password but no authenticator app or passkey configured in this
capture, so the removal buttons described above are absent.*

![Fictional person’s Sign-in section with an authenticator, named passkey and removal controls](/docs/screens/admin-person-second-factor.png)

## Reset a forgotten password and end sessions

1. With the intended person still selected, choose **Reset password** if they need a new
   local password. It makes a link at once; there is no confirmation first.
2. Copy and pass on the link in **Pass on the password link** before choosing **I have copied it**.
   If available, use **Mail it to …** and check the sent-to message. A new administrator link replaces
   every earlier password link for that person; give them the newest administrator link.
   A later **Forgotten your password?** request does not cancel this administrator link.
   Read its expiry.
3. Have them open it and set a new password. The secret part of the link leaves the address
   bar before the form appears. They can reload the page in the same browser without losing
   the link. If the form no longer opens, reopen the original link while it is valid. Using it ends their refiroo
   sessions everywhere. A configured second factor remains in force. If the link expired,
   was replaced or was used, make another.
4. If the lost device may still hold a signed-in session, choose **Sign out everywhere**
   on the person's page and confirm. Every refiroo session ends at its next request.
   They can sign in again with their remaining or replacement methods. This does not sign
   other browsers out of the organisation's provider.

![Password-link dialog with one-time link and expiry](/docs/screens/admin-person-reset-password.png)

*Above: fictional Rita Approver's reset dialog. The captured link was not used.*

If an action fails, read the message and reload the person's page to check its state before
retrying. If no administrator can sign in, ask the operator to use the
[server recovery procedure](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/).
Do not turn off the requirement merely because one person needs a replacement factor.

---
title: Turn off local sign-in
description: Move ordinary browser sign-in to a working provider while preserving an administrator’s recovery route.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Security administration** and an enabled provider that has already signed someone in successfully. Keep a tested local recovery account. This change affects local password sign-in, not clients’ authentication. See [Sign-in and second factors](/docs/administer/sign-in/#local-accounts).

## Prepare a way back

1. Follow [Add a sign-in provider](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-sign-in-provider/) and prove a complete sign-in through **Continue with …**. Check that the right person and roles are reached.
2. Open **Settings › People and access › People** and select the recovery administrator. Under **Sign-in**, check that their password is set and **Keeps local sign-in** is on. This is separate from their Security administrator role.
3. If needed, turn **Keeps local sign-in** on. It saves immediately and offers **Undo**; turning it off asks for confirmation. Test the retained account before proceeding. It still needs any required second factor; keep that device or recovery route available.
4. Tell affected people to use the organisation’s provider. Arrange links for existing accounts so they keep their roles and history rather than acquiring duplicate identities.

## Turn off ordinary password sign-in

1. Open **Settings › People and access › Sign-in** and select **Local accounts**. **Turn off…** appears only after an enabled provider has successfully signed someone in. If absent, complete that proof first.
2. Choose **Turn off…**. Read **Turn local sign-in off?**, including which providers are offered and how many people keep password sign-in.
3. Choose **Turn off**, or **Cancel** to leave it enabled. Wait until Local accounts shows **Off**. If **Not changed** appears or details changed meanwhile, review the saved state before trying again.
4. In a separate browser session, check provider sign-in. Check the recovery account through **Sign in with a local administrator account**. Ordinary local accounts no longer sign in with a password.

While local sign-in is off, refiroo refuses to deactivate the last active person keeping it or remove their retained route. Keep more than one prepared recovery person if your organisation requires that resilience. Turning local sign-in off does not remove people, passwords, roles or the second-factor requirement.

![Local accounts after turning ordinary password sign-in off, with Turn on available](/docs/screens/admin-local-signin-off.png)

## Restore local sign-in

Open **Local accounts** and choose **Turn on**. This acts immediately, without a confirmation. Check **People sign in with a password again.** If no administrator can reach refiroo, the operator must use the server recovery procedure; see [Configure sign-in](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/).

---
title: Grant a role
description: Grant a role to a person, group or client, choose its reach and check inherited access.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Security administration**. Choose a role for the actual task using
[Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/); administrative roles do not automatically
allow reading or editing data.

## Open the grant dialog

1. Open **Settings › People and access › People** or **Groups**, or **Settings › Connections › Clients** and select the recipient.
   Choose **Grant** in their roles or access section. The recipient is already chosen.
2. Alternatively, open **Settings › Workspaces**, select the workspace and choose **Access**,
   then **Grant**. Choose **Who** by searching for the person, group or client by name.
   Check the kind as well as the name before selecting them.
3. For a client, choose **Roles** under **What** if you are granting management access.
   **Consumer APIs** is a separate kind of grant; see [Create a client](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-client/).

![Grant dialog with role selection and workspace or whole-instance scope](/docs/screens/admin-grant-dialog.png)

*Above: the dialog for fictional Rita Approver has no role selected and is open but unsaved.
Check the selected workspace's displayed name rather than assuming the default is the one intended.*

## Choose what and where

1. Tick the role or roles. Read **May** beside each role to check its action groups.
   More than one role adds those permissions together.
2. Under **Where**, choose **Workspaces** and use **Add workspace** to select the intended
   workspaces. Remove any initially selected workspace that should not receive this grant.
3. Choose **The whole instance** only for access that should apply to every workspace,
   including future workspaces. Roles greyed out for workspace grants require this reach.
4. If one role is selected in one workspace and narrowing is offered, review
   **Narrow what they may change**. Keep **Everything in …** for all permitted writes there,
   or choose **Only these applications and record types** and add the intended entries.
   This never restricts reading. To narrow several grants, make them one role and workspace at a time.
5. Read the summary in **Grant access** and choose **Add grant**, or **Add N grants** for several. **Cancel** before submitting makes no grants. Closing after some were saved does not undo those grants. If several grants are
   attempted and some fail, the dialog lists the failures and says whether the others were
   made. Successful grants remain. Failed choices stay selected with their reasons; correct them and use **Try again**.

## Verify or remove access

1. Check the recipient's table: **Where**, the role, any **Narrowed to (writes)** entries
   and **Through**. For a person, group membership can supply additional roles.
2. Open the workspace's **Access** tab to see the combined result. Use the search and
   **Role** or **Kind** filters to locate the recipient. Whole-instance grants are marked there.
3. To remove a direct grant, choose its **Remove** and follow any confirmation shown.
   For an inherited role, change the group's grant or the person's membership at its source.
   Removing one grant does not cancel another grant that allows the same work.
4. Ask the recipient to check the next action in that workspace. Changes apply on the
   next request. If they still have wider access, inspect direct grants, all groups and
   whole-instance grants before concluding removal failed.

![Person's roles showing direct grants for every workspace](/docs/screens/admin-grants-person.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's six grants are direct. A group-supplied role would identify its source in Through.*

The last active Security administrator cannot be removed. If a refusal says the recipient
or grant changed meanwhile, reload and review the current state before choosing again.

For the complete narrowing task, follow [Narrow a grant to record types](/docs/guide/administer/narrow-a-grant-to-record-types/). For clients reading a declared interface, use [Grant a consumer API to a client](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/) instead of adding a management role.

---
title: Create a custom role
description: Copy a role or start empty, select action groups and grant the resulting role.
reader: access-admin
---

Use a custom role when the predefined roles do not match a responsibility. You need **Security administration**. [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) explains what each action group permits and where it applies.

1. Open **Settings › People and access › Roles**. Read the matrix first: each column is a role and each row is an action group. A predefined role cannot be edited or deleted.
2. Choose **New role**. Enter **Name**, then choose **Start from**. **Nothing** creates an empty role; selecting an existing role copies its action groups. It does not change the source role or keep the two linked.
3. Choose **Add role**. The new role appears in the matrix with its editing controls. If **The role was not created** appears, correct the stated problem. **Cancel** closes without creating it.
4. Tick the action groups it needs. Set the name and optional description, then choose **Save**. An empty role permits nothing. Administrative groups do not imply Browse; add Browse only if the responsibility needs workspace data.
5. Follow [Grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) to give it to a person, group or client in the intended scope. Roles containing only instance responsibilities must be granted for **The whole instance**.
6. Check the recipient’s effective access, including other direct and group grants. Their own **Account › What you can do** shows the result. Changes apply on the next request.

![New role dialog with Name and Start from](/docs/screens/admin-role-new.png)

To change a custom role later, use its edit control in the matrix, change its action groups and choose **Save**. This changes access for everyone holding that role. Read **The role was not saved** before retrying a failure; reload if the role changed meanwhile.

To delete it, remove every grant first. **Delete role** is unavailable while it is granted. Once unused, choose it and confirm the named deletion. refiroo refuses any role or grant change that would remove the last active Security administrator.

---
title: Add a sign-in provider
description: Register organisation sign-in, save its provider and prove a complete sign-in before changing local access.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Security administration** and help from the organisation’s sign-in administrator. refiroo uses OpenID Connect. Keep a working local administrator account while preparing the provider. [Sign-in and second factors](/docs/administer/sign-in/) explains identities, sessions and recovery.

## Create the provider

1. Open **Settings › People and access › Sign-in** and choose **New provider**. The catalogue keeps **Local accounts** separate from **Providers**.
2. Enter **Name on the sign-in button**. People see **Continue with** followed by that name. Check the suggested **Key**: it forms part of the registered address and cannot change after saving. The names password, passkey and local are reserved; choose a distinct key.
3. Enter **Issuer**, **Client ID** and **Client secret** from the sign-in administrator’s registration. The issuer must match the provider exactly. The saved secret is kept sealed and never shown again.
4. If the provider supplies groups, enter **Groups claim**, using the field name supplied by its administrator. Empty means provider groups are not used. You can [create provider groups and grant their roles](/docs/guide/administer/manage-a-group/#use-a-provider-group) before anyone signs in.
5. Keep **Offer it on the sign-in page now** selected if it should be enabled, then choose **Add provider**. It shows **Checking and adding…** while checking an enabled provider. If **The provider was not saved** appears, correct the stated issuer, connectivity, certificate or registration problem with the sign-in administrator. **Cancel** leaves it uncreated.

![New sign-in provider with button name, registration and group fields](/docs/screens/admin-signin-provider-new.png)

## Register the return address and prove sign-in

1. On the saved provider’s page, find **Address to register with the provider**. Copy **Redirect address** and have the sign-in administrator register it exactly. Use the saved page’s address rather than inventing one.
2. If the provider is disabled, choose **Enable**. This acts immediately after the provider checks succeed. Open a separate browser session and choose **Continue with …**. Complete the organisation’s sign-in and check that refiroo opens the intended person.
3. A first sign-in creates a person but grants no access automatically. Grant their direct or group roles, or [link the provider sign-in to an existing person](/docs/guide/administer/link-a-provider-person/) when they already have an account. An e-mail match alone does not link accounts.
4. Confirm a complete successful provider sign-in before considering [Turn off local sign-in](/docs/guide/administer/turn-off-local-sign-in/).

![Saved fictional OpenID Connect provider with redirect address, settings and signing-out choices](/docs/screens/admin-signin-provider.png)

## Maintain the provider

The **Settings** form edits its button name, issuer, registration and groups claim. **Key** is fixed. Leave **Client secret** blank to keep it for an unchanged issuer; enter it again if changing an unused issuer. Once anyone has signed in through the provider, its issuer cannot change. Add another provider and link people instead. Choose **Save** to apply form edits; **Cancel** discards them.

Under **Signing out**, **Sign people out of … too** also signs the current browser out of the provider. Before turning it on, check provider support and register the displayed **Sign-out address**. It may sign people out of other organisation applications in that browser. It does not end provider sessions in their other browsers.

**Disable** acts immediately and ends refiroo sessions started through that provider. A provider used by a person cannot be deleted; disable it to preserve those identities. For an unused provider, **Delete** asks **Delete …?** and **Delete provider** confirms removal. Check remaining sign-in routes before either action. If a concurrent change is reported, reload the provider and review its current state before applying another change.

For public addresses, HTTPS and server recovery, involve the operator; see [Configure sign-in](/docs/run/sign-in-and-mail-setup/).

---
title: Rotate a webhook key
description: Replace a webhook signing key and coordinate the receiver’s switch during an overlap.
reader: access-admin
---

You need **Integration administration** in the webhook’s workspace. Arrange the switch with the receiver’s owner. The key belongs to this webhook; replacing it does not change a client’s sign-in secret. See [The Webhooks page](/docs/administer/webhooks/#signing-keys).

1. Open **Settings › Connections › Webhooks**, select the intended webhook and check its **URL**, consumer API and workspace. Under **Configuration**, note **Signing key created** and any **Previous key signs until** date.
2. Choose **Rotate key…**. In **Rotate the signing key of …**, choose **1 hour**, **24 hours** (the usual choice) or **7 days**. During this overlap each delivery has signatures for the new and old keys, so the receiver can accept either.
3. For a key that leaked, choose **Stop it now**. The old key stops signing immediately. Until the receiver has the replacement, it may refuse delivery and refiroo retries.
4. Choose **Rotate key**. **Cancel** keeps the current key. If **No new key was made** appears, read the reason and reload the webhook to establish its state before another attempt.
5. In **Keep the new signing key**, copy the replacement into the agreed secure store and pass it securely to the receiver’s owner. Check the displayed overlap deadline. Choose **I have stored the key** only after saving it; it cannot be displayed again.
6. Have the receiver owner switch to the new key and verify a fresh delivery. Check **Deliveries**, its attempts and response. A successful delivery during overlap alone does not prove the receiver uses the replacement; ask its owner to confirm which key verified it.
7. Check that delivery continues after the overlap. If it fails, have the receiver owner check its configured key, then follow [Find out why a webhook paused](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/).

![Webhook key rotation dialog with overlap choices, before making a key](/docs/screens/admin-webhook-rotate.png)

If the replacement was lost, make another rotation and arrange the handover again. Do not expect the old one-time dialog to reopen with the key.

If another rotation starts during an overlap, the key retained from the earlier rotation
stops signing immediately. Coordinate the receiver's switch before rotating again. A
rotation on a suspended webhook changes its key but leaves it suspended; resume it
separately when the cause is repaired.
guide/src/content/docs/use/account.md:
---
title: Your account
description: Check your sign-in, manage your own browsers and see what your roles allow.
reader: steward
---

Open the avatar at the top right and choose **Account** to see who you are signed in as,
manage your sign-in methods and inspect your permissions.

## The account menu

The avatar menu shows your name and the roles you hold in the workspace currently open. **Account**, **Notifications** and **All settings**
open those pages. **Theme** offers **System**, **Light** and **Dark**. System follows your device;
the choice is saved in this browser. **Sign out** ends your current sign-in.

![The avatar menu with account links, theme choices and Sign out](/docs/screens/use-account-menu.png)

*Above: Guide Admin's menu shows their roles in Graubünden. Other people can have fewer roles.*

## Your identity and sign-in

The account card shows your name, e-mail address, how you signed in and when.
These details help you check that you are using the intended account. **Sign out** on the card
ends the current browser's sign-in.

![Account with identity, password, passkeys and authenticator setup](/docs/screens/use-account.png)

*Above: Guide Admin signed in with a password and has not set up an authenticator app.*

### When an administrator manages your sign-in

If Account says **An administrator manages the sign-in of this account.**, the password,
passkeys, authenticator app and **Where you’re signed in** sections are not shown. Your
profile and **Sign out** remain. You can sign out of this browser, but you cannot sign out
other browsers or sign out everywhere.

You cannot change your own password, set up, confirm or remove an authenticator app, make
new recovery codes, or add, rename or remove passkeys. Ask a security administrator for a
password-setting link or help with a lost device. **Forgotten your password?** gives the
usual response but sends no mail for this account. See
[Help someone who lost a device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).

### When you manage your own sign-in

The controls depend on how you signed in. If your organisation provides sign-in, its password
is managed there. The local Password control appears when you signed in with your refiroo password.

To change that password:

1. Choose **Change password**. Enter **Current password** and **New password**.
2. Choose **Save new password**. A successful save keeps this browser signed in and signs out
   your other browsers. **Cancel** closes the form without changing the password.
3. If a password is refused, read the reason beside the field and correct it. A failed save
   does not change your password.

Under **Passkeys**, choose **Add a passkey** and follow your browser or device's instructions.
A WebAuthn passkey uses your fingerprint, face or device PIN to sign in, or to provide the second step.
Registered passkeys can be renamed so you can tell them apart, or removed. Removal asks for your
password or a code from your authenticator app. If the device prompt is cancelled, no passkey is added.

An authenticator app supplies time-based one-time passwords (TOTP). Under **Authenticator app**, choose **Set up an authenticator app**. Scan the displayed code with
your app, or enter its key, then enter **Code from the app** to confirm setup. Keep the recovery
codes shown afterwards somewhere safe: each works once if you lose access to your phone.
They are shown once. **New recovery codes…** replaces the old codes after you prove your sign-in;
the old ones then stop working. If the instance requires a second factor with a password, removal is offered only when a
passkey provides another way to meet that requirement. Otherwise, ask a security administrator.

## Where you’re signed in

Each row names a signed-in browser or other sign-in session and shows when it last acted and
when it signed in. **This browser** marks the one you are using. Several rows can have the same
browser name; use their times to distinguish them.

![Signed-in sessions with last activity, sign-in times and individual Sign out buttons](/docs/screens/use-account-sessions.png)

*Above: the reference account has many sessions from browser work and automated captures.
A row labelled Python-urllib is not another person's browser.*

Choose a row's **Sign out** to end that session. Choosing it for This browser signs you out here.
For a lost device or an unfamiliar session, **Sign out everywhere** asks for confirmation and
ends all your sessions, including this one, at their next request. It does not delete your work.
If ending a session fails, retry after reading the error; do not assume it has ended.

## What you can do

The bottom of Account lists your roles by workspace and what they allow: reading, proposing
changes, changing Live, publishing and approving. Restrictions may name particular applications
or record types. Instance-wide roles appear separately under **Across the instance**.

![Account permissions grouped by workspace and instance-wide responsibilities](/docs/screens/use-account-permissions.png)

*Above: Guide Admin holds Data owner for every workspace and five instance-wide administrative roles.*

This is a view of your access, not a form for granting yourself roles. Ask an access administrator
if something you need is missing. To act on a proposal, follow
[Prepare and publish a change set](/docs/guide/use/prepare-and-publish-a-change-set/) or
[Approve a change set](/docs/guide/use/approve-a-change-set/). For notices and their email options,
see [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

Each role is listed once, with the groups through which you hold it. A limited permission is
shown as a count: open it to see the applications and record types covered, and the roles that
allow each. On a phone, the workspace sections stack vertically.

Use **Settings › Notification email** for email choices: switch on **Email me when something arrives
in my inbox**, then choose **At once**, **Digest** or **Off** for each kind. Digests run every
morning or on Mondays at 07:00 in your browser's time zone; the page shows the next one. No unread
notices means no digest. The email switch is absent if mail is not configured or you have no
email address; the page explains why. **Settings › Appearance** holds display preferences.
For administrator-managed sign-in and help with lost devices, see
[Sign-in and second factors](/docs/administer/sign-in/).

## Sign-in and password help

Opening a saved application address without a session shows the sign-in page, in this browser's
theme. Use your e-mail address and password, a passkey, or the offered organisation's provider.
After signing in you return to the requested page. An ended session sends you there again.
A wrong e-mail address or password does not reveal which was wrong. Repeated failures slow attempts;
they do not permanently lock your account. Wait before retrying rather than repeatedly submitting.

Sessions renew while you work, but still have idle and overall expiry limits set by the operator.
If sign-in keeps ending unexpectedly, sign in again and ask an administrator to inspect the
session rather than changing unrelated record data. Under **General › Account**, **Loading your
account** is a loading state, not missing identity; retry a failed read.
The identity card can say **Signed in with your password**, **Signed in with a passkey** or
**Signed in with …**, with **Since …** for this session's start. **Where you’re signed in**
counts browsers and shows **Active now** or last activity with sign-in time.

The normal password rule is 15–128 characters. Common passwords and your e-mail address are refused;
use a longer distinct password, not repeated guesses. A development instance can have a lower
minimum, so the displayed refusal is authoritative. The current password is needed to change
it. Use the reveal buttons to check the current or new password privately. If you forgot it,
use **Forgotten your password?** when offered, or ask an administrator for a password-setting
link. The response does not reveal whether an account exists. Your organisation manages its
provider password separately.

**Add a passkey** opens a separate refiroo page. Give the passkey a recognisable name and provide
**Your password, or a code from your app** before the browser's device prompt. This proof prevents
an unattended signed-in browser adding a lasting sign-in method. Cancellation adds nothing.
Passkeys belong to the host where they were made; moving refiroo to another host affects them.
Renaming changes their display name only. Removing the last second factor can be refused where
one is required: add another passkey or set up an authenticator app first.

For display steps, see [Appearance and devices](/docs/use/appearance-and-devices/).
For the next digest time and delivery choices, see
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/).

An account using only an organisation's provider cannot add refiroo passkeys or an
authenticator app to bypass that provider. Manage those sign-in protections with your
organisation. If proof for adding or removing a passkey is refused, correct the password or
use a current authenticator or unused recovery code; a slowed sign-in needs time before retrying.

Select the passkey's name where it stands to edit it. Leave the field or press Enter to save;
Escape puts the old name back. An unchanged input saves nothing. The save notice offers **Undo**.
If refused, the input stays open with the reason and **Cancel** and **Save again** beneath it. **Remove …**
opens a separate confirmation with **Remove passkey**; it does not remove the device's other
passkeys. **New recovery codes…** asks for **Code from the app, or a recovery code**, then
**Rotate recovery codes**. Save the replacements: the old recovery codes stop working. Removing the
authenticator app uses **Remove the second factor** and **Remove it**; your recovery codes then
stop working too.

## Session limits and organisation sign-in

By default a session ends after 12 hours without use or 14 days in total, even if it has
continued renewing while you work. The operator can change these limits. Repeated failed
password attempts can delay another attempt by up to fifteen minutes; the account is not
locked permanently.

Your organisation can offer **Continue with** its OpenID Connect sign-in provider, such as
Microsoft Entra ID, Google or Keycloak. The provider handles its own second factors. On your
first sign-in, refiroo takes your name and email from the provider and updates membership of
its groups at sign-in. The roles granted to those groups determine what you can do here.

If you already had a local account, first provider sign-in can create a separate person.
Ask a security administrator to link the accounts so your existing roles and history stay
with the original person. Signing out of refiroo signs out of the provider too only when
that provider is configured to do so. If you can immediately sign in again without a password,
check whether the provider still has an open session.

**Forgotten your password?** asks for your e-mail address. It gives the same
response whether or not that account exists. A reset message is sent only for an account
with a local password and an email address whose sign-in is not managed by an administrator. For a provider account, reset your password with
the organisation instead. An administrator can supply a one-time password-setting link
when email recovery is unavailable.

## Sessions for an assistant

An external assistant you signed in for appears in **Where you’re signed in** as its name
followed by **(assistant)**. **Sign out** on that row ends its session, stopping it on its next
request. A blocked assistant also loses access; restoring it does not restore the ended session.
You must sign in for it again. Its sign-in page shows the name it claims and where it returns.
Check those details before allowing it. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/)
for what it may read, what it may prepare and why its provider privacy settings matter.

## Complete a second sign-in step

After your password, refiroo can ask for another proof of identity:

1. If **Use a passkey** is offered, choose it and complete the device prompt. Cancelling the
   prompt leaves you at sign-in; it does not remove your passkey.
2. To use an authenticator app, enter its current six-digit **Code** or **Code from the app**.
   Choose **Sign in** or **Sign in with the code**, as shown. A refused code needs a new
   current code; repeated failed attempts can require a wait.
3. If you cannot use the app, choose **Use a recovery code instead**, enter one unused
   **Recovery code** and choose **Sign in**. That code cannot be used again. **Use the app's
   code** returns to the ordinary code entry. **Start again** returns to the first sign-in step.
4. If setup is required before you can continue, scan the displayed code with your app or
   copy the displayed key into it. Enter **Code from the app** and choose **Confirm and
   continue**. Save the recovery codes when they are shown.

If you have lost all usable proofs, ask a security administrator to help restore access.
After removing a passkey in refiroo, also remove its saved entry from your device or password
manager; the entry there is not deleted automatically.

![Second sign-in step offering a passkey, an authenticator code and recovery-code sign-in](/docs/screens/use-sign-in-second-step.png)
guide/src/content/docs/use/notifications:
---
title: Notification settings
description: Choose immediate email or digests, and manage the workspaces you follow.
reader: steward
---

Keep your inbox in refiroo and choose which notices also reach your email address. Open
**Settings › Notification email**, or **Notification email settings** on the Notifications
page. Follow [Set up email notices](/docs/guide/use/set-up-email-notices/) for the steps.
