For the notices themselves, see [Inbox and approvals](/docs/use/inbox-and-approvals/).

## Email is your choice

**Email me when something arrives in my inbox** is off until you enable it. The page shows
the destination address. Under **How each kind reaches me**, choose **At once**, **Digest**
or **Off** for approval requests, decisions on your requests, jobs and other offered kinds.
These choices change only email: your inbox keeps every notice. Choices save as you make them;
read any error before assuming the new choice was stored.

If mail has not been configured or your account has no address, a sentence explains why no
email choice is offered. Ask an administrator about the missing setup or address. If email was
already on, the switch can remain visible so you can turn it off after mail becomes unavailable.
Email is for people's accounts, not clients used by other systems.

![Notification email for an account without an email address or followed workspaces](/docs/screens/notification-email-digest.png)

*Above: the reference account has no email address, so no email delivery choices are offered.
Its followed-workspaces list is also empty.*

**At once** sends an eligible unread notice once, provided it arrived since enabling email
and is less than 24 hours old. Previously read notices and notices from before enabling email
are not sent. Turning email off leaves inbox notices intact.

## A digest instead of separate messages

Choosing **Digest** for the first kind starts a daily schedule in your browser's time zone.
Under **The digest**, choose **Every morning at 07:00** or **Mondays at 07:00**. The page shows
the saved time zone and **Next digest**. There is no choice of another hour or an evening digest.
Enabling email recalculates its next time; changing the frequency or time zone moves it.
Saving the same schedule preserves its next time. With email off or no schedule, no next time
is shown. The browser supplies the time zone when you choose the schedule.

![Enabled notification email with delivery choices, digest frequency, time zone and next digest](/docs/screens/use-notification-email-digest-settings.png)

A digest counts all eligible unread, unhandled notices since email was enabled and lists the
newest 50, with links to the rest. Unlike immediate mail, it has no 24-hour cutoff. Job entries
can include applied and rejected counts while their results remain retained. Notices already
read or handled are omitted; nothing eligible means no message. A notice included in a digest
is not mailed again as a new digest entry.

Email uses fixed wording, kinds, times, counts and links. It contains no record, change-set,
workspace, person or file names. Digests do not require AI. If settings are refused, the prior
preferences remain; retry after checking the shown reason.

## Follow publication in a workspace

**Follow** on a workspace's Home card opts you into notices when someone else publishes a
change set there. Your own publication does not create a follower notice for you.
**Workspaces I follow** lists your choices with **Stop following**. Following requires Browse
and starts off. Selecting Follow again does not create duplicate subscriptions.

Losing Browse or deactivation stops notices while retaining your follow choice. Notices can
resume when access returns. Stop following to remove that choice deliberately. Following is
independent of whether email is available; its notices still appear in the inbox.
See [Follow a workspace](/docs/guide/use/follow-a-workspace/).

There is no browser view of a sent digest. Read the message in the receiving mailbox;
use **Notification email** to check its saved delivery choices and schedule.

## When email does not arrive

An unread notice alone is not enough: email must be enabled, the account active, a destination
address present and the instance able to send mail. A digest also needs a schedule and at
least one kind assigned to it. Choosing the first Digest kind saves a daily schedule with
your browser's time zone automatically. If that save is refused, your old choices remain;
read the error and retry rather than expecting a partly saved schedule.

Nothing eligible means no digest message. Check the inbox first: reading or handling a notice
can remove it from the next message. Turning a kind **Off** affects email only. There is no
interface-language or general account-locale chooser here; the digest time zone is a separate
schedule choice, not a language preference.

The unavailable-email messages are **Email is not set up for this installation, so there is
nothing to choose here.** and **Your account has no email address, so there is nothing to
choose here.** Neither means notifications are lost. Read them in **Notifications** and ask
an administrator to set up mail or correct your account's address.
guide/src/content/docs/use/jobs.md:
---
title: Jobs
description: Follow imports, exports and bulk work, inspect results and stop remaining work.
reader: steward
---

A job is work refiroo runs in the background, such as an import, export or change to many
records. Open **Settings › Data operations › Jobs** to find the jobs you may see across
workspaces, newest first. In **All jobs**, the list shows **Workspace**, **State**, **Items**, **Requested by**,
**Created**, **Finished** and **Actions**. Open a job to read its progress and results.

Follow [Follow and cancel a job](/docs/guide/use/follow-and-cancel-a-job/) for the steps.

## Jobs grouped under a task or a draft

Above the list, **Grouped** puts an assistant task's related work, including jobs queued by
its session, in one row. A model draft's jobs also form one row. A job with neither owner
remains a row of its own. **All jobs** shows the individual jobs instead. Your browser remembers
this choice when you return to Jobs.

The grouped table shows **Job or group**, **Workspace**, **Jobs**, **State**, **Latest** and
**Actions**. A group is labelled **Assistant task** or **Model draft** and named after its
workbook or draft. A workbook's extension appears beside its name. **Jobs** counts the group's
visible jobs; **State** gives counts for states with jobs, such as running, failed and completed.
**Latest** is the latest job time. These counts describe retained jobs you may see, not every
job ever started or every job in the instance.

Open the group name to see its jobs:

1. The heading names the workbook or draft. Above it, **Assistant task** or **Model draft**
   and the workspace identify the group; **‹ Jobs** returns to the main list.
2. **Summary of the group** gives the job count and latest time. **All** shows the total;
   state buttons show non-zero counts for **Running**, **Queued**, **Awaiting confirmation**,
   **Failed**, **Completed**, **Cancelled** or **Expired**. Select one to narrow the table;
   select **All** to restore every visible job. The selected state stays in the page's address.
3. The **Jobs** table shows **Job**, **State**, **Items**, **Requested by**, **Created**,
   **Finished** and **Actions**. Inspect processed, applied, rejected and unprocessed counts.
   **Refresh** reads again; **Load more jobs** continues the list. **Cancel** is offered
   for queued or running work where cancellation is available; it opens a confirmation.
4. **Open the task** or **Open the draft** opens the owning work. The button appears only
   after refiroo has confirmed you can read that task or draft. Seeing a group's jobs does
   not itself grant access to its owner; a missing button is not a stopped job.
5. Open a job to inspect its result. When opened from the group, its trail includes
   **‹ Assistant task: [name]** or **‹ Model draft: [name]**. Use that link to return to
   the group with the state choice preserved, or **Jobs** to return to the main list.

**Esc** goes up one level: job to the group it was opened from, then group to Jobs. A job
opened from the flat list returns directly to Jobs. Esc does not navigate while a dialog
is open or you are editing a field.

If the group says **This group has no jobs you can see**, its task or draft may have been
removed or its jobs may have expired. Return to Jobs. **No jobs in this state** means the
selected state has no visible rows; try **All** or **Refresh**. A read failure offers a retry;
it does not establish that the group is empty.

## States and results

A job can wait in the queue, run, wait for confirmation, complete, fail, be cancelled or expire.
**Cancel requested** means stopping has been requested, not that all work has stopped.
An import moves through **Reading the file**, **Previewing** and **Loading**. A waiting preview
has not applied its changes. **Load the file** confirms an import; **Apply** confirms a bulk
preview. Review the counts and item reasons before confirming.

Completion does not mean every row succeeded. Read applied, unchanged, rejected and unprocessed
counts and the item outcomes. A failure has **Why it failed**; a stopped job explains **What
stopped it**. Fix that cause before starting fresh work. A sample preview is informative, while
execution checks every item, the stored file, versions and the current context again.

An expired preview cannot be confirmed, even if a stale page still says it is waiting.
Start a new preview. The **Kept until** fact tells you when the job's retained results expire.
The list's **Limits** describes this deployment's batch, job and retention limits; do not rely
on a universal file size or item count.

## What a job's page shows

An import has its file/profile choices, row outcomes and column report. An export has **The
file**, with counts by type, format, size, checksum, context and **Download** after success.
An unsuccessful export has no file. Keep any file you need before its retention ends.

A copy or move shows records and relationships made, refused and not moved, breakdowns by type,
and outcomes filterable by reason. Source record names open in their original workspace.
Older retained jobs may lack relationship-type counts. A migration shows converted, type-changed,
removed and must-be-fixed counts. These operations are described under
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).
A job without item outcomes instead explains what it belongs to and links there where allowed.

## Cancellation and access

Cancel queued, running or waiting work with the offered cancel button and its confirmation.
Cancellation stops future work; it does not roll back already committed chunks. All-or-nothing
work commits as one unit, while independent work can leave partial results. A colleague's edit
to a shared change set between chunks can stop the next chunk; earlier chunks remain.

Jobs run with the requester's current rights. Deactivation or losing a required permission can
fail work at its next step. You see your own jobs and jobs your permissions allow; knowing a
job's address does not grant access. A retired workspace refuses new data changes.

The tab that starts work reports progress and completion while open. The inbox can also receive
waiting and finished-job notices. Opening a job marks its notices read, including notices that
arrive while it stays open. Closing a page does not itself stop a running job.

![Completed export with state, retention, counts, file details and Download](/docs/screens/job-results-and-file.png)

## Read the job labels

| State | Meaning and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Queued | Waiting to start. Cancel if the work is no longer wanted. |
| Running | Work is in progress. Follow its counts or leave it running in the background. |
| Awaiting confirmation | A preview is ready; review it before Apply or Load the file. |
| Completed | Processing ended. Check the result and refused items before relying on it. |
| Failed | Work stopped with an error. Read Why it failed and any applied counts. |
| Cancelled | Cancellation has finished. Check what was applied before it stopped. |
| Expired | Retention ended. Start new work if you need another preview or file. |

The result label is separate: **Every item applied**, **Partly applied** or **Nothing applied**.
A failed independent chunk is rolled back, while earlier committed chunks stay applied.
Cancelled all-or-nothing work rolls back its transaction completely. **Not reached** items
can mean cancellation, failure, a model change or a colleague changing the change set. With
all-or-nothing work, an otherwise valid item can be unwritten because another was refused.

The list distinguishes **Batch**, **Import**, **Export**, **Workbook for people**, **Profile**,
**Profile check**, **Dry run**, **Inference**, **Mapping proposal**, **Migration** and **Move**.
Some belong to model-administration tasks; their pages link to that work. **Refresh** reloads
the list and **Load more jobs** continues it. **New export** starts a file; **New import**
appears when your permissions allow importing.

**State** names the workspace and requester and shows creation, start and finish times.
For an export, **The file** also records **Sheets**, its Live/change-set/publication scope,
**Change feed position**, **Valid on** when chosen and **Checksum (SHA-256)**. Use those facts
to distinguish similar retained files; the checksum identifies the completed file's contents.

**Cancel this job?** offers **Stop the job** or **Keep the job**. If it finished first, read the
refusal and refreshed state rather than assuming it was cancelled. **The change was not applied**
after confirmation leaves the preview waiting: cancel it and create a fresh preview against
current data. The old result remains readable until retention ends.

Copies keep their source identity so a later copy can update its earlier counterpart instead
of making another one. Moving a copy back can update the original, or recreate its original
identity if it was removed. Inspect the source links and results before publishing. A move's
source deletions wait for the target copy to be published first; the deletion proposal cannot
be published ahead of the copy it depends on. See [Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/)
for mapping design, or [Copying and moving records](/docs/use/copying-and-moving/)
for preparing and reviewing a transfer.

On a waiting preview's own page, **Cancel this import?** offers **Discard the import**,
or **Cancel this preview?** offers **Discard the preview**. **Keep the import** or **Keep the
preview** returns to the preview. Discarding writes nothing and leaves the preview readable
until expiry. On the Jobs list, the confirmation button is **Cancel job** instead.
Results and files are normally kept for seven days; your deployment's **Limits** and the job's
**Kept until** give the applicable retention.

guide/src/content/docs/use/importing-and:
---
title: Importing and exporting
description: Choose a file for editing or exchange, preview its changes and load it safely.
reader: steward
---

Export data to read or edit outside refiroo, then import it with a preview. Export needs
**Browse** in the workspace. Import needs **Bulk and import** and permission to write the
target record types in Live or a change set. The deployment must allow new jobs. Publications
and retired workspaces can be exported but cannot receive an import.

Use [Export records](/docs/guide/use/export-records/),
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/), or
[Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/).

If a workbook should become a workspace of its own, see [A workspace from a workbook](/docs/use/workspaces/#a-workspace-from-a-workbook).

## What an export contains

Open **Workspace actions › Export**. On a view, **What** starts with **This view** and its
name. This takes the view's search, supported filters, parent scope and chosen columns,
including matching rows beyond those on screen. The count line names its context and size
when known: rows × columns for a matrix, records for a tree or mapping grid.

Choose **The type**, **The application** or **The whole workspace** for whole types rather
than the view's narrowed selection. From **Settings › Data operations › Jobs**, choose types
in a workspace. **Valid on** optionally limits an export by business date; ordinary browser
lists have no equivalent selector. When a page's search is not included, the dialog says so.
A filter on a relationship's own values is not carried into a view export; read that notice
before assuming the file contains exactly the connections left on screen.

**Kind of file** offers **For editing in a spreadsheet** and, for a table view or a selection
of types, **Technical**. Other view kinds export as an editing workbook.
Technical exports offer **Excel (XLSX)**, **CSV** and **JSON Lines**. Choose **Between exported
records**, **All their relationships** or **None** for relationships. All their relationships
can refer to records outside the chosen record scope. Everything is read at one instant.
The job's file summary records its scope, counts, size and checksum. Failed or cancelled exports
have no downloadable file. Downloads remain subject to job and file retention.

## Workbook layouts

**For editing in a spreadsheet** makes an Excel (XLSX) workbook. Its shape follows the selection:

| Selection | What the workbook holds | What loads back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table view | The table's columns, labels and order, with optional related sheets. | Editable record values and relationships, according to the saved layout. |
| Matrix showing record fields | One row per row record; each column record has a group of cell fields, with hidden cell identities and versions. | The cell records only. Row labels are for reading. |
| Matrix showing links | One column per column record, listing linked records by a chosen text field, with dropdowns backed by a value sheet per column. | Connections within each row and column; value-sheet records where editing or creation is enabled. |
| Relationships table, rows | One row per connection, showing both records and the relationship's values. | Connection values; a new row without identities can connect two named records. |
| Relationships table, grid | One row per source record, with Linked and relationship values under each target. | Connection values; Yes can link a missing pair. No removes nothing. |
| Mapping grid | One row per source record, with its target in a relationship column. | The target relationship, as in a table workbook. |
| Tree | One sheet per type, with its parent by name. | Editable records and parent choices. |
| Type, application or workspace | One sheet per type, parents' types first, with fields, parents and relationships by name. | Editable values on each sheet; a connection between sheets loads from the later sheet only. |

A view enabling **Link existing** or **Unlink** uses the link-matrix layout, even when it also
enables **Create**. Otherwise the matrix shows its cell fields. Keep hidden identity and
version columns, including those that distinguish parents with the same name.

Every XLSX export, including a technical workbook, has **About this export** as its second
sheet. Read it for the view or scope, workspace, context, search and filters, export time,
counts, relationships and load-back rules. It is for reading and is ignored on import.
CSV and JSON Lines files have no sheets.

### Text in CSV files

In a CSV export, text beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets one
extra leading single quote, so a spreadsheet shows it as text rather than a formula. The same
rule applies when one or more single quotes already precede that character. For example,
`=1+1` is written as `'=1+1`, and `'=1+1` as `''=1+1`.

Keep that added quote when returning an exported CSV. With **Profile: None**, import removes
exactly one protective quote from record names and text fields. Returning an unchanged export
therefore leaves the original values unchanged, including their original quotes. Other quotes
are kept. This reading applies to exported CSV layouts, not to an ordinary CSV read through a
stored profile. XLSX files are unaffected; their values need no added quote.

### Matrix cells and new records

Export does not ask where new matrix records go. The relationship's candidate rules limit
which groups can hold them. If the rules identify one group and it is missing, it is created
with the record. Otherwise the group holding the most of this view's records in the column
is used; a tie gives no choice. An unused group is never picked automatically, even if it is
the only one.

When neither the rules nor data give a place, refiroo can propose a new group named like the
groups this view uses in other columns, where the structure and rules allow it. In the browser,
review or edit its proposed name, or choose an existing group. An import preview says
**will create … under …**; confirming creates the group and record together. No model change
is needed. If no suitable place is found, a new record is refused with the column and reason.
Choose or prepare a group in the app before previewing again.

The main matrix sheet loads only its cells; value sheets load their records separately.
Empty or cleared cells change nothing; removing all
values or links in a cell is done in refiroo. In the record-field layout, a cell holding several
records is shown joined and not loaded back. Edit those records individually in the app.
In the link layout, a non-empty list replaces only that cell's connections: listed records are
linked, omitted records are unlinked, and other columns are left alone. Names containing a
semicolon are written and read with a comma instead. Keep that displayed form when editing.
Where the matrix also permits creation, an unknown value can create a record in the derived
or proposed group; otherwise the list must identify existing candidates.

### Value sheets and matching fields

For a link matrix, **What each cell lists** selects **Name** or a text field of its records.
The default is Name. The file records the field so it can be read back. A linked record with
no value in that field refuses the export; choose another field or supply the missing value.
The selected values need to distinguish records within each column for import to resolve them.

Each **Values · …** sheet lists the column's eligible and already-linked records, their fields
(except fields holding JSON), their group and hidden identities and versions. Its values back
the main-sheet dropdowns. With Edit or Create enabled, edits update by identity; where Create
is enabled, a new row creates a record. A row not selected in any cell still loads. With only
Link existing and Unlink, value sheets are for reading and do not load. A matrix showing the
record's own fields has no value sheets.

A main-cell value matching a value-sheet row refers to that record. Renames are recognised by
the new value and also the old one unless another sheet row now uses it. The same new value
in both places is one record. A value in neither the sheet nor existing records creates one
where allowed, supplying its name and the chosen field only. Other required values still
apply. Duplicate matching values are refused as ambiguous. Spreadsheet edits do not themselves
synchronise the two sheets; import resolves them together.

The preview's **How the file is read** shows matching fields, values matched, value-sheet
counts and where new records go. For an unrecorded reading, it guesses the field and marks
it **Guessed**, with a note when the choice is uncertain. Choosing another field runs the
preview again. **Save these fields in the profile**, where offered, keeps the reading for
later files. No records are written before **Load the file**. Follow
[Import a file](/docs/guide/use/import-a-file/#check-how-the-file-is-read).

For steps, see [Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/).

## A workbook for people

For a table view, **For editing in a spreadsheet** makes a workbook shaped by your table: visible columns in their order,
readable labels and typed cells. **Advanced: columns and sheets** changes the columns, their
order, which field a relationship column shows and which relationships get separate sheets.
Related records are exported in full, even where the browser showed only a few chips.
Record identity and versions are held in hidden columns. Keep those columns and the workbook's
saved import information when editing. Cells choosing a single record offer dropdowns from
sheets of eligible records.

Columns marked **(not imported)** are for reading. A table relationship column that owns its
records is read-only; edit those records on their own sheet or in refiroo. An ambiguous or overlong relationship cell
becomes a read-only summary pointing to its sheet. Several owned records for one parent also
form a summary rather than an editable single value. Edit the appropriate sheet instead.

When imported with **Profile: None**, the workbook is read as exported. An untouched workbook
changes nothing; changed names, fields and added rows are loaded as edits. A record changed by
someone else since export is refused unless you deliberately choose the overwrite option.
A main-sheet relationship list replaces that whole set; connections still chosen keep their
identity and values. A relationship sheet adds or updates connections, but omitting a row does
not remove one.

**Blank ordinary field and owned-record cells leave values unchanged.** To clear such a value,
use refiroo's field editor. **An empty table cell replacing a relationship set empties that set**,
where its rules permit it. Check the preview carefully when clearing a relationship list.
A required connection still cannot be cleared.

An owned-record relationship can use **Columns per parent** to make a workbook for filling in.
Each chosen parent contributes columns for its owned record's fields. Filling an empty column
creates that record under its parent and connects it to the row's record. See
[Add a language with a workbook](/docs/guide/use/add-a-language-with-a-workbook/) for the generic
steps and an example. Excel permits at most 16,384 columns; a wider layout fails when the export
job runs. Reduce parents or fields and export again.

## Read a file through a profile

An import profile tells refiroo how sheets and columns become records, names, fields, parents
and relationships, and which values identify existing records. Choose the file first, or drop it onto the file field. The form selects a profile when exactly one valid profile fits; you can still choose **None** or another fitting profile. JSON Lines uses none; CSV accepts a profile with CSV settings or a single source, and a workbook accepts any valid profile for this workspace's model. Invalid profiles and profiles for other models are omitted. The three loading-policy choices are under **Options**. Profile setup belongs to
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/); a steward can
[load its next version](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

Under **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles**, **Upload the next version…** stores
an XLSX or CSV file and starts a job to read its sheets and columns. While waiting, the page
says **Checking [file name]: profiling its sheets, then reading it through the profile…**.
This reading step writes no records. If **The file could not be read** appears, follow its
reason and upload a corrected file. A file that is too large or is neither XLSX nor CSV is
refused. Checking and loading must wait until its analysis is finished.

The profile page reports **Columns**, **Values**, **Records** and **Profile against the active
release**. To inspect the source's sheets, detected lists, header rows, column statistics
and cell ranges while changing the mapping, a model administrator uses the draft's
[source pane](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/#source-file-and-draft). Those statistics show
filled and distinct values, candidate keys, frequent values, placeholders and shared values
with other columns or records in the comparison workspace; they are evidence to review.

A newer upload supersedes the earlier file for this profile in this workspace. The earlier
file is kept for the job retention period after replacement, then deleted. It does not replace
another workspace's upload. The stored file is shared with its uploader and holders of
**Bulk and import** in its workspace; a file naming no workspace requires that access at the
instance. Keep your own original if it needs to outlive this retention.

A missing or ambiguous related name is refused. Parents can be resolved from existing records
or the same file, and are loaded before children. Repeated keys with compatible filled cells,
in one sheet or several sheets of the file, combine into one record; conflicting filled values refuse all contributing rows. Blank cells
do not conflict with another row's supplied value. A profile without a stable key warns that
later uploads may create new records instead of finding earlier ones.

A profile can keep or delete records missing from the next file. Deletion of missing records
is allowed only in a change set, so review those removals before publication. A profile must
still fit the workspace's model; ask its model administrator to fix named problems.

## Preview and load

The import always previews first in the browser. Choose whether to **Load the rows that can
load** or **Load nothing unless every row loads**, and whether found records may be updated.
The preview reports creations, updates, unchanged and refused rows. Its column report shows
empty, converted, mapped and refused cells, and found, missing or ambiguous record matches.
A large file may be sampled; the page says how much was tried. Loading checks the whole file
against current data, so the final result can differ.

**Load the file** confirms; **Cancel import** ends the preview without writes. Expired previews
cannot load. Correct refused rows in the original file and resend the whole file: already
loaded rows should preview unchanged when their data and matching choices are unchanged.
Refused rows are listed on the job page; there is no download of just the refused rows.

For an export from another workspace, **Load them as this workspace's own** creates separate
records with stable identities derived for the destination. Parents and relationships stay
together; resending the file finds those copies. They do not stay linked to the originals.
**Refuse them** instead reports the source workspace on the refused rows.

Read [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for progress, cancellation, access and retention.

## Read the preview's evidence

**The preview** counts **Created**, **Updated**, **Unchanged**, **Deleted**, **Refused items**
and **Rows**. **A sample** means only part of the file was tried. In **Rows in the preview**,
choose **All rows**, **Refused** or **Not loaded**. Read **Outcome** and **Why, or what it does**
for the individual rows; a refused cell gives its column and reason.

**How the file was read** explains each sheet and column:

| Count | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Bound to | The field, name, parent or relationship receiving this column. |
| Cells and Empty | Whether the expected rows supplied anything to read. |
| Read and Value-mapped | Values successfully read or translated through the profile's value choices. |
| Refused | Cells that could not be used; correct their stated cause before loading. |
| Found, Not found and Ambiguous | Whether a name or key identified exactly one existing record. |

A **Check** marker calls attention to a column. The **Read as exported** summary identifies a
workbook using its saved import information. **This import** records the chosen file, profile
and load policy. After confirmation, **The result** reports **Applied items**, **Refused items**
and **Not loaded**. Read that result even when the preview looked right.

![Import preview with one refused Height cell, 115 unchanged rows and per-column reading counts](/docs/screens/import-preview-columns.png)

*Above: one row in the reference Stops workbook is refused because Height (m) contains
“not a number”. The column counts show 115 height values read and one refused; the preview
has written nothing.*

## Profiles and recurring keys

In **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles**, **Valid** means the profile fits its
model; **Needs a fix** means a named problem must be resolved. Neither guarantees that every
row in the next file is valid. **Not loaded yet** means no retained last load is shown.
**Load more profiles** continues the catalogue. If there are no profiles, ask a model
administrator to prepare one through [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

**Last load** offers **Open the change set review** while its work is proposed, or
**Open the load's job** for the retained operation. A load can be missing here because it has
passed retention. Uploading the next file checks it without changing records. Accepting a
column rename or ignoring a new column changes the profile used for subsequent checks; review
those decisions with its owner. See [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/).

A matching key may combine several columns. Every component must be present and identify at
most one stored record. Fill incomplete keys or ask the profile owner to resolve ambiguous
combinations. Changing only a display name need not create a new record when a stable key still
finds the original.

An export uses one consistent reading of the data. If its worker restarts after a crash, it
starts the export again rather than appending new data to half of an old file. Follow the job
until it has a completed file. Home itself has no Import or Export action; open an application
or use Jobs. A record's History is a list of changes, not an earlier-state viewer, and offers
no restore or undo. See [History](/docs/use/history/).

## What the next file can change

A profile belongs to one model. Use it in a workspace running that model; a different model
needs its own suitable profile. A file carrying records from another workspace with a
different model cannot load them as counterparts: those rows are refused while other valid
rows can load under the chosen load policy.

The next-version check can recognise a renamed header when its column stays in the same
position and holds the same values. **Accept** saves that rename; **Ignore** saves the decision
not to load a new column. Each decision checks the file again before loading.

For a lookup allowing one related record, a changed value in the next file switches the
connection to the newly named record. Missing records are kept unless the profile says to
delete them. That deletion also removes their connections, but refuses a record that others
depend on. Review the refused items and the change set before publishing.

## File refusals and completion notices

A preview can refuse all rows participating in a parent cycle, rather than loading either
record into an invalid hierarchy. If the file cannot be read or does not fit the profile,
loading changes nothing. Correct the file or ask the profile owner to repair its mapping.

The tab that starts an import reports when its preview is ready and when loading finishes,
unless you already have that job open. A collection reloads after an import started in this
tab loads into it. For exports, the completion notice offers **Download** and the job page;
a failed or cancelled export instead reports that state. Keep the tab open for these notices,
or return to **Jobs** to inspect the result later.

A stored upload used by an import profile is visible to its uploader and to people allowed
to import in its workspace. Treat the file as shared with those workers when choosing what
to upload. Losing a write permission can stop a job at its next step; review its applied counts
before asking an authorised colleague to continue the work.

## Let the assistant prepare the import

When the assistant is enabled and you have the required access, **Import…** in the workspace
menu first opens **Load a workbook**. Give it one XLSX or CSV file, instructions, or both.
It proposes the model and load for review rather than publishing records. **Import without
the assistant…** opens the ordinary manual import. See
[Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/) and
[Load a workbook with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/).
The whole file and your words go to Claude Code, turns can incur costs, and task files are
retained; [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) explains those rules.

## Remove an uploaded file or an import profile

Open **Settings › Data operations › Import profiles** and select the profile. People with
**Bulk and import** are offered the deletion buttons; without that access the buttons are absent.
Deleting either item does not undo a load or remove records already loaded into a workspace.

- **Delete the file…** asks **Delete <file name>?**. **Delete the file** removes that upload,
  its stored cells and the analysis of its sheets and columns. This analysis is not the saved
  import profile that maps the columns. A check still reading it is
  asked to stop. The import profile stays. Upload the file again before checking or loading it.
- **Delete the profile…** asks **Delete the profile <profile name>?**. **Delete the profile**
  removes the saved instructions for reading the workbook and returns you to the profile list.
  Loading the workbook again needs a new profile saved by installing a model draft that holds it;
  ask a model administrator to prepare this through [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

Choose **Cancel** in either confirmation to keep the item. A refusal stays in the confirmation
with its reason. If someone changed the file or profile since you opened it, cancel, reload the
page and inspect the latest version before trying again. There is no undo button for either
deletion. Keep the original workbook outside refiroo if you need to upload it later.

![Import profile showing separate buttons to delete its uploaded file and the profile](/docs/screens/use-import-profile-delete-actions.png)

## Default file and preview limits

An import normally accepts a file of up to 200 MiB. Its preview tries at most 10,000 items;
**Load nothing unless every row loads** normally allows at most 10,000 items. Your operator
can change these limits. Read **Limits** on Jobs and the limit reported by the import form.
If a file exceeds the limit, split or reduce it, or agree a suitable limit with the operator.
If splitting a recurring workbook whose profile deletes missing records, ask its owner first:
each part could otherwise treat records in the other parts as missing.

Jobs and their downloadable files are normally retained for seven days. Download an export
before its **Kept until** time. A retained import profile can outlive its last load's job;
**Last load** is not an archive of every workbook loaded through it.

![Confirmation to remove an import profile while retaining previously loaded records](/docs/screens/use-import-profile-delete-confirm.png)
guide/src/content/docs/use/workspaces.md:
---
title: Workspaces
description: Choose the right dataset and understand its model, access and workspace management.
reader: steward
---

A **workspace** holds its own reference data, change sets and publications. Before editing,
check the workspace name and its model release. Follow [Switch workspace](/docs/guide/use/switch-workspace/)
to open another dataset.

## Each workspace runs its own model

Two workspaces can run the same model and hold different records. They can also run different
models, with different applications, types, fields and views. Changing one workspace's model
does not change another workspace's model. Switching workspaces copies and moves nothing.

[Home](/docs/use/home/) shows the workspaces you may browse, their models and releases, and their
application buttons. **Default** marks the instance's default workspace; it does not mean other
workspaces share its data. The workspace called Default need not be the default workspace.

![Home with workspace cards, model names, releases and application buttons](/docs/screens/use-home.png)

*Above: Graubünden is marked Default. The workspace named Default runs a different model.*

Within an application, **Workspace** in the sidebar names the dataset. The text beneath names its
model and release. The banner above the records identifies **Live**, a [change set](/docs/use/change-sets/)
or a [publication](/docs/use/publications/). Those are contexts within a workspace.

## The workspace's page

Choose a workspace's name on Home to open its page. **Find a record** searches names across its applications and lists. Up/Down chooses a result; Enter opens it. **Applications** offers each application's starting view and links straight to its lists.

**Your shelf** keeps the lists and other views you use most, from any application in this workspace. Choose **Add a list** and tick the lists, trees or matrices you want. You can also use the pin button in a list's header. A tile opens that view; its count, when available, is the number of live records of its source type, not a count of matrix cells or a filtered view.

Drag tiles to arrange them. For keyboard or touch use, open a tile's menu and choose **Move earlier** or **Move later**. Right-click also opens that menu. **Take off your shelf** removes the shortcut, leaving its data in place. The shelf and its order stay in this browser, separately for each workspace.

**Needs you** lists your waiting change sets. **What changed** groups recent activity by day; consecutive repeats of one kind of change fold with a count such as **4 in a row**. These are summaries, not a complete history. Workspace actions, including **Edit model**, appear only when your permissions allow them.

## Switching and access

The selector offers workspaces you may browse. **Other model** identifies a different model;
**Other release** identifies a different release of the same model. After switching, check the
applications and views again. The former view may not exist in the destination.
With only one available workspace, its name appears without a selector.

You need **Browse** access to read data, and the appropriate editing permissions to change it.
Reader can browse; Contributor can prepare changes in change sets; Data steward and Data owner
can also change Live. Custom grants can narrow writes to particular applications or record types.
See [What you can do](/docs/use/account/#what-you-can-do) for your own access.

If no workspace is offered, ask an administrator for access. A loading failure does not mean
there are no workspaces: retry the failed read first.

## Workspace administration

A retired workspace remains readable but refuses changes. Where your access permits it, open it
from **Settings › Workspaces**, rather than the active workspace selector. Creating, renaming,
retiring and deleting workspaces are described in
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/).

## A workspace from a workbook

Choose **New workspace from a workbook** on Home beside **Your workspaces**, in
**Settings › Workspaces**, or on a workspace's page. This creates a separate workspace;
it does not load into the workspace you have open.

The action appears when you hold **Workspace administration**, **Install a model** or
**Model release**, and **Bulk and import** at the instance, plus **Model authoring**.
Workspace administration, model administration and integration jobs must also be switched on
for the deployment. If any required access or capability is missing, the action is hidden.

1. Choose an XLSX workbook or CSV file in **Workbook**. **Name** starts with a name taken
   from the file; change it if needed. Choose **Read the workbook**. refiroo reads the file,
   finds its lists and checks every row before creating the workspace.
2. Review **What refiroo found**. Each list shows its source sheet where applicable, its row
   count, how many rows load, any rows skipped for want of a key, and why rows do not load.
   The total covers every row, not a sample. Choose **Create workspace** to install the
   model, create the workspace and start loading the workbook into Live. A refused row does
   not stop the other rows from loading.

**Adjust** keeps the draft and opens it in the model editor so you can change the structure
or how the workbook is read. If no list was found, or checking did not finish successfully,
**Create workspace** is unavailable; read any explanation and use **Adjust** to inspect the
draft. A read failure appears under **Not read**. A creation refusal appears under
**The workspace was not created**, with the problems to resolve.

**Cancel** closes the sheet and removes the draft made for the review. If removal fails,
the draft remains under **Settings › Model**. To start on an existing model instead, open
**More ways to start** in the file step and choose **New workspace on an installed model**.
From Home or a workspace's page this takes you to Settings › Workspaces; from Settings it
opens the **New workspace** form. You can also make a workspace without data that way.

After creation, the new workspace's page shows **Loading** with the file name and the
number of items processed, out of the total when available. When loading finishes, the
notice shows counts for **created**, **updated** and **unchanged**, followed by how many rows
did not load or that every row loaded. For refused rows, choose **See the rows** to open the
job's details. **Dismiss** removes the notice; it does not undo the load. If loading fails
or stops, the page shows the reason. The workspace already exists, so inspect the load in
**Settings › Jobs** before trying again. The notice is kept only for the current page load;
after a browser reload, find the job in Settings › Jobs.

## When a destination cannot open

The selector searches workspace labels; the page address keeps the workspace's key. Switching
can show a toast explaining that the destination runs another model or release.
**Not in this model** means the address names an application, collection or record type this
workspace lacks. Use the offered workspaces whose models contain it, or choose an available
application here. An unknown workspace or a release that cannot be served has its own explanation.
Read that reason and ask the operator to restore a supported release where needed; retrying a
record edit cannot make an unavailable model readable. Other workspaces can still be used.

## Refresh after the model changes

If the workspace changed release while your page was open, the message can say **… now runs ….
Nothing was saved.** or **Reload to see it.** Choose **Reload**, then review the current form
and context before editing. A stale screen must not overwrite data under a different model.

**Manage workspaces**, beside or inside the selector, opens its Settings entry where permitted.
Its **Applications · …** links open the workspace's applications. Loading the catalogue or an
individual workspace is distinct from an empty result; wait or retry the error.
Creating, renaming, setting the default, retiring, reactivating and deleting are administration
tasks. Their controls and deployment availability belong to
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/). **Capability groups** is an operator
status panel, not a setting a steward changes to gain access.

To open retired or unreadable data, follow
[Open a retired or unavailable workspace](/docs/guide/use/open-a-retired-or-unavailable-workspace/).
To read activity across workspaces, use [History](/docs/use/history/).

A retired workspace is marked **Retired · read only**. In Settings its **Overview** shows the
model, creation and last-change facts, and **Open workspace** leads to its start page. Wait
while **Loading workspace catalogue…** or **Loading workspace…** is shown; an error is not an
empty catalogue.

A missing model element can say **No other workspace's model has it.** Choose **Go back** or
the offered workspace start page, then choose a collection present in that model. If another
workspace is offered, its **Open in …** action changes the workspace as well as the page;
check the destination before making changes.

## Actions for this workspace

![Workspace menu offering Import, Export and Edit model beside the selected workspace](/docs/screens/workspace-actions-menu.png)

*Above: the menu for Graubünden while reading the Stops collection in Network. Its actions
apply to this workspace and the data context being viewed.*


The **⋯** menu beside the workspace selector offers **Import…**, **Export…** and **Edit model**
when your permissions and the current context allow them. Export starts from what the current
page shows; check the chosen columns, filters and data context in its dialog. See
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for what the file includes.

**Edit model** opens the workspace's model draft, returning to that draft on later visits.
It changes the structure rather than an individual record. Ask a model administrator when you
need that change; see [Models](/docs/model/models/). Applying a model shows its effect before
confirmation. If records must move, the migration preview must be confirmed before they move.

The workspace's Settings page offers **Overview**, **Access**, **Approval** and **Activity**
according to your permissions. Overview links to its applications; Activity shows changes newest
first, grouped by day. Access and Approval describe who can work here and how publication is
approved. They do not grant editing rights simply because you can read the workspace.

## A context that could not load

**Loading the model…**, **Loading change set…** or **Loading publication…** means the read
is still pending. **Could not load this content** reports a failed read, not an empty dataset.
Read its explanation and use **Retry** after correcting a connection or service problem.
**Return to Live**, where offered, leaves the failed snapshot view for this workspace's
current data. Check the context banner before continuing; changes made in Live take effect immediately.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/set-up-:
---
title: Set up email notices
description: Turn on email, choose notice kinds and check your digest schedule.
reader: steward
---

Choose email copies without changing your inbox. See
[Notification settings](/docs/use/notifications-settings/) for eligibility and limits.

1. Open **Settings › Notification email**, or choose **Notification email settings** from
   the Notifications page. Check the address under **Email**.
2. Turn on **Email me when something arrives in my inbox**. If no switch is offered, read the
   reason: mail may not be set up or your account may have no address. Ask an administrator
   to resolve it; following workspaces can still work without mail.
3. Under **How each kind reaches me**, choose **At once**, **Digest** or **Off** for each kind.
   Changes save immediately. If an error appears, correct the cause and try again.
4. For a digest, choose **Every morning at 07:00** or **Mondays at 07:00** under **The digest**.
   Read the displayed time zone and **Next digest**. The browser supplies the zone; the hour
   is fixed. The first kind put into Digest starts a daily schedule automatically.
5. Return to **Notifications** for the full inbox. Reading a notice before its digest is sent
   leaves it out. Nothing eligible means no digest; older unread notices are not excluded
   merely because they are more than a day old.

To stop all email, turn the master switch off. To stop just one kind, choose **Off** beside
it. Inbox notices remain either way. Immediate mail does not backfill notices from before
you enabled email and only sends unread notices less than a day old.

![Notification email enabled with one kind assigned to a daily digest and its next time visible](/docs/screens/use-notification-email-digest-settings.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/follow-:
---
title: Follow and cancel a job
description: Read a background operation’s progress and results, or stop remaining work.
reader: steward
---

Follow work after leaving its collection or import dialog. See [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/) for
states, access and retention.

1. Open **View job** in the starting notification, or go to **Settings › This instance › Jobs**
   and open the job; a group of related jobs opens first, and its jobs under it. Check **Workspace**
   and **Requested by** before acting.
2. Read **State** and progress. A preview waiting for confirmation has not written its proposed
   changes. Review the items before choosing **Load the file** for an import or **Apply** for
   a bulk preview. A running job updates while the page stays open.
3. To stop remaining work, use **Cancel job**, **Cancel import** for a waiting import,
   or **Cancel preview** for a waiting batch preview.
   Read the confirmation, then choose **Stop the job** for running work or **Discard the
   import** / **Discard the preview** for a waiting preview. From the Jobs list, choose **Cancel
   job** in its confirmation. **Keep the job**, **Keep the preview** or **Keep the import**
   dismisses that confirmation.
4. Wait for the state to settle. **Cancel requested** is still pending. Already committed
   chunks remain applied: inspect the final counts rather than assuming cancellation undoes them.
5. For an export that completed, read **The file** and choose **Download**. For an import or
   batch, read refused and unprocessed items and their reasons. Fix the source and preview
   again before retrying work.

If the job failed, read **Why it failed**. Loss of the requester's permissions can stop a job;
a changed change set can stop its next chunk. Expired previews require a fresh preview.
Retained results and files disappear after their retention; download what you need in time.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/import-:
---
title: Import a file
description: Choose a file, review its preview and load the rows you approve.
reader: steward
---

Load into Live or a change set after checking exactly what the file means. See
[Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for file and profile rules.

If **Load a workbook** opens because the assistant is enabled, choose **Import without the
assistant…** to reach the manual import form used below. That manual path does not send the
file to an AI assistant.

1. Open the intended workspace and collection. Choose **Workspace actions › Import**. To
   choose another destination, open **Settings › This instance › Jobs › New import** and
   choose the workspace and **Load into** context.
2. Choose **File**, or drop the file onto that field. The chooser accepts Excel workbooks, CSV and supported technical export
   files. After choosing the file, check **Profile**: refiroo selects it when exactly one valid profile fits. You may choose **None** or another fitting profile. A JSON Lines file takes none; CSV offers profiles with CSV settings or one source; a workbook offers any valid profile for this workspace's model. Invalid profiles and other models' profiles are omitted. Use **None** for a file exported by refiroo. Read any profile problems before continuing. For an exported CSV,
   keep the protective single quotes added to formula-like text. With **None**, import removes
   exactly one such quote from names and text fields; an unchanged export changes nothing.
   XLSX is unaffected. See [CSV text rules](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#text-in-csv-files).
3. Open **Options**. Under **Rows that cannot load**, choose **Load the rows that can load** or **Load nothing
   unless every row loads**. Under **Records the file finds**, decide whether to update or
   refuse them. For an export, **Only if unchanged since the export** protects newer work;
   **Update them anyway** deliberately relaxes that protection.
4. If the file names another workspace's records, choose **Load them as this workspace's own**
   for separate destination records, or **Refuse them**. Check this choice before continuing.
5. Choose **Preview**. The job page opens while the file is read. Check its context, counts,
   column report, **How the file is read** where shown, and refused rows. Each failing cell identifies its column and reason.
   If only part of a large file was tried, its sample is not a promise about every row.
6. Choose **Load the file**, or **Cancel import** if the result is wrong. Loading checks
   current data and can refuse rows that passed preview. Read the final applied and refused counts.
7. Correct refused rows in the file and import it again. Resend the whole file: rows already
   loaded should be unchanged when their values and matching rules are unchanged.

## Check how the file is read

1. In the preview, open **How the file is read** where offered. Each matrix or relationship
   column shows **Matched by**, **Values matched** and **New records go into**. For a workbook
   exported by refiroo, the file records the matching field. When a file does not record it,
   refiroo compares its values with existing records and marks its choice **Guessed**. Read
   any note about an uncertain choice; do not assume a high match count proves it is right.
2. Check each column's field against what its values mean. Where a selector is offered under
   **Matched by**, choose the intended field. This starts a new preview of the same file;
   wait for it and review its counts and refusals again. Nothing is loaded by either preview.
3. For a link matrix with value sheets, check how many rows update existing records and how
   many are new. The main columns also report values found on value sheets and new values.
   An unselected value-sheet row can still create or update a record; review it too.
4. Check **New records go into**. A proposed or rule-defined missing group says
   **will create … under …**. Confirming the load creates that group with its records.
   If there is no suitable place, follow the reason and prepare the place in the app before
   previewing again. You do not need a model change to accept a proposed group.
5. When using a stored profile, choose **Save these fields in the profile** if this reading
   should apply to later files. Saving the reading does not load the file. Review all changes
   and refused rows, then choose **Load the file** only when the preview is right.

For the workbook editing rules, see
[Edit in Excel and import back](/docs/guide/use/edit-in-excel-and-import-back/#edit-the-value-sheets-of-a-link-matrix).

A malformed file or invalid profile changes nothing. Ask a model administrator about profile
rules you cannot fix. A profile deleting records absent from the file must load into a change
set. An expired preview needs a new import preview, rather than another confirmation attempt.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/load-th:
---
title: Load the next version of a workbook
description: Check a recurring workbook against its profile and stage its differences in a change set.
reader: steward
---

Use a saved import profile to recognise a recurring workbook. This differs from creating a
model from a new workbook; that task belongs to
[Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/).

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces and models › Import profiles**. Select the profile and read its
   **Last load**: file, destination, row counts and whether its change set was published.
2. If your permissions offer **Upload the next version…**, choose it and upload the newer
   workbook. Choose the intended comparison workspace and wait while it is checked.
   The profile is checked and saved against that workspace’s model. Nothing is loaded
   into its records by this check.
3. Review new, missing and renamed columns, new values, changed names and missing records.
   Choose **Accept** on a **Renamed** row only where the proposed column really replaces the old one.
   Choose **Ignore** on a **New** row to leave that column out. Ask the profile's model administrator to
   fix ambiguous bindings or model problems; do not guess which field a column represents.
4. Check the missing-record choice. Keeping missing records leaves them; deleting them stages
   removals and is allowed only in a change set. A missing key means reliable recurring
   matching is not available: resolve it before relying on repeated uploads.
5. When the report allows loading, choose **Load into a change set…** and review the destination
   and proposed changes in its dialog. Loading creates a new change set containing differences.
6. Choose **Open the change set review** from the completed load or **Last load**. Review
   additions, corrections and removals before publishing or submitting for approval.

If the file could not be read or the profile could not be saved, correct the displayed cause
and check again. Missing controls can reflect your access; ask the responsible model
administrator. See [Importing and exporting](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/) for row refusals.

![Import profile after a next-version check, with Accept and Ignore beside column differences, Needs a fix and disabled Load into a change set.](/docs/screens/import-profile-next-version.png)

The pictured profile still **Needs a fix**, so **Load into a change set…** is disabled. Resolve
the reported problems before loading.

In **Load … into a change set**, check the proposed name and workspace before choosing
**Load**. The steps **Open a change set** and **Load the rows** show what is happening.
The suggested name starts with **Load**, the file name and a date. If loading fails after the
change set was opened, inspect that change set and the load's job before starting again;
do not assume the first proposal disappeared.

## Use a saved profile through the assistant dialog

A workbook loaded from the assistant’s checked records and relationships saves no import
profile. For that route, send the next file to the assistant again and explain how to match
existing records; see [Loading with the assistant](/docs/use/loading-with-the-assistant/#the-next-file-and-the-saved-profile).

If you already have a separately saved import profile, follow the steps above to reuse it.
Starting through **Import…** can also recognise that saved layout and prepare the file without
an assistant session or AI cost. You still review the proposal and row check. **The saved layout does not fit this file**
offers **Read it with the assistant**. That sends the file and instructions to Claude Code,
can incur costs and keeps task files; see [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/).
A new sheet or changed layout needs review, not an assumption that the previous mapping fits.

## Remove a file you no longer need

1. On the profile page, choose **Delete the file…** beside the upload and load actions.
2. Read **Delete <file name>?**. It removes the upload and its stored analysis, stops a check
   still reading it, and keeps the profile and already loaded records.
3. Choose **Delete the file** to continue or **Cancel** to keep it. After deletion, upload a
   file again to check it. A failed deletion leaves its reason in the dialog; resolve that
   cause before retrying.

To stop reusing the profile itself, choose **Delete the profile…** and confirm **Delete the
profile**. Read [what each deletion keeps](/docs/use/importing-and-exporting/#remove-an-uploaded-file-or-an-import-profile)
before confirming; deleting a profile does not reverse its earlier loads.

![Delete an uploaded workbook while keeping its import profile and loaded records](/docs/screens/use-import-file-delete-confirm.png)
guide/src/content/docs/guide/use/open-a-:
---
title: Open a retired or unavailable workspace
description: Read a retired workspace and understand why another workspace cannot be opened.
reader: steward
---

A retired workspace is readable history. An unavailable workspace cannot currently be served.
See [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/) for choosing a dataset.

1. For a retired workspace, open **Settings › Workspaces** where your access offers it.
   Select the workspace and choose **Open workspace**. It may be absent from the active
   workspace selector. Check the **Retired · read only** mark and the context band’s
   **Retired: read only.** message.
2. Browse its applications, records and retained publications. Editing records, relationships,
   change sets and migrations is refused. Ask the workspace administrator about reactivation;
   do not try to work around read-only status.
3. If the destination says **Workspace … cannot be opened** or **Cannot be opened**, read its
   reason. The model's language can be too old or too new, or its release can be invalid.
   Other workspaces are not affected and nothing was changed by opening the address.
4. Send the reason to the responsible model administrator or operator. **Bring it up to date**
   and **Review the change**, when offered to an authorised administrator, belong to
   [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/). A steward should choose
   another readable workspace while that is resolved.
5. If the page instead says **No workspace …**, check the address with its sender. If an
   application or type **is not in this workspace's model**, use **Workspaces whose model has …**
   to select a suitable destination, or **Go back**. If none exists, the page says **No other workspace's model has it.**

![Unavailable example workspace with its model-language reason, recovery review and other workspaces](/docs/screens/workspace-cannot-open.png)

An unavailable model is different from missing Browse access. Ask about the displayed reason;
repeatedly retrying a record save does not repair it.

For a missing application, collection or record type, the suggested destination button reads
**Open in …** with the workspace name. It opens that workspace; recheck its model and context
on arrival. The start-page button instead keeps you in the workspace already named.
guide/src/content/docs/model/managing-wo:
---
title: Managing workspaces
description: Create and manage independent datasets and choose which model each runs.
reader: model-admin
---

Manage datasets under **Settings › Workspaces**. You need **Workspace administration** for
workspace changes; reading data, changing models and granting access need their own permissions.
For everyday navigation, see [Workspaces](/docs/use/workspaces/).

## Find a workspace


Where your access permits it, **Manage workspaces** or **Settings**, **Workspaces** opens the
workspace list. It shows the model and release of each workspace and marks the default.

![Workspace management listing each workspace and its model release](/docs/screens/use-workspaces-manage.png)

*Above: Graubünden and Default run different models. This capture only views the list.*

Open a workspace row to inspect **Overview**, **Access**, **Approval** and **Activity**.
**Open workspace** returns to its data; **Activity** shows [history across records](/docs/use/history/).
The other actions require administrative permissions: **New workspace**, **Edit model**,
**Copy or move data…** and **Retire…** change the workspace or its configuration.
Opening the page does not perform them.

![A workspace detail with its actions and Overview, Access, Approval and Activity tabs](/docs/screens/use-workspaces-detail.png)

*Above: Graubünden's Overview shows its key, model, applications and default status.*

A retired workspace remains readable but refuses changes. Open it through workspace management,
rather than the active workspace selector. The default workspace cannot be retired or deleted;
an administrator must make another workspace the default first.

## Create or rename a workspace

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**. Search the list before creating another dataset. Active
   workspaces appear first, then retired ones.
2. Choose **New workspace**. Complete its name and key. The key forms its address; choose it
   carefully. Use the default workspace's model, or choose another usable installed release.
3. Choose **Add workspace** and check the new workspace's **Overview**, model and applications. It has
   its own data; creation copies no records from the default workspace. Read any refusal before
   retrying. Cancel leaves the list unchanged.
4. To change its displayed name later, select the name where it stands, enter the new name,
   then leave the field or press Enter to save. Escape puts the old name back; an unchanged
   input saves nothing. The save notice offers **Undo**. If refused, the input stays open
   with the reason and **Cancel** and **Save again** beneath it.
   Renaming does not change its key or create a new dataset.

## Retire, reactivate, make default or delete

- **Retire…** asks for confirmation. It removes the workspace from the active selector and
  refuses writes, keeping data, change sets, publications and history readable. Open it from
  this list later. **Reactivate** makes it available for work again.
- **Set as default** chooses the default destination. It neither copies data nor changes the
  models of other workspaces. Check the Default mark after the action.
- **Delete…** is only for an empty, never-published workspace with no change sets or webhook
  subscriptions. A workspace ever published can only be retired, even after its data is removed.
  The screen explains what prevents deletion. Confirm only after checking the name and key.

The default workspace cannot be retired or deleted. Make another active workspace the default
first. If another administrator changed the workspace or default while the page was open, review
the refreshed state and repeat only the action still needed.

## Tabs and model changes

**Overview** shows the workspace's facts and its model's applications; each application opens
in this workspace. **Access** lists grants for people, groups and clients. **Approval** holds
[publication policies](/docs/administer/approval-policies/). **Activity** lists changes newest
first, grouped by day, with filters; see [History](/docs/use/history/). Only tabs your access allows
are shown.

**Edit model** opens the saved draft for the workspace, reopening it on later visits. It needs
Model authoring, Model release and Browse, and an active workspace. Check **Applies to**, then
use **Apply to this workspace…** after editing. The confirmation lists model changes, data
compatibility, open change sets left behind and other workspaces left unchanged. If records must
move, review the separate preview before confirming. Follow
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/).
**Copy or move data…** starts [a copy or move](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/).

Workspace administration can also be switched off by the deployment. The page then stays read
only and names the setting; ask the operator to enable it if administration is needed.

## Workspace tasks

[Create a workspace](/docs/guide/model/create-a-workspace/),
[Edit its model](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-workspaces-model/),
[Make it the default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/) and
[Retire or delete it](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-workspace/) give the steps.
To choose an installed release, use [Change a workspace's model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/).

**Cannot be opened** on a workspace whose model language is unsupported needs the offered
model-language repair or operator help; see [Model language versions](/docs/model/model-language-versions/). A missing application
bookmark can instead mean **Not in this model**: open a collection declared by this workspace.
Editing the displayed name keeps the permanent key. A stale save asks you
to review newer state; it does not silently overwrite another administrator's edit.

## Permanent keys and changes made at the same time

A workspace key has at most 160 characters, using lowercase letters and digits separated by
single hyphens. Leading and trailing spaces are removed. Its key cannot be changed after
creation, and a retired workspace still reserves its key. Change **Name** to rename the dataset.

Retirement waits for a write already in progress to finish. Once retirement succeeds, later
live and change-set writes are refused. If two administrators change the default from the same
starting state, one succeeds and the other must refresh and review the new default.

Retiring also suspends active webhook subscriptions for this workspace. Reactivation makes the
workspace writable again but does not resume those subscriptions automatically. Ask their
administrator to review and resume them; undelivered events are kept only for their retention
period. See [Webhooks](/docs/administer/webhooks/) for delivery recovery.
