guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/creat:
---
title: Create a workspace
description: Create an empty dataset and choose its installed model release.
reader: model-admin
---

You need **Workspace administration** and workspace administration enabled on the instance.
See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for permissions and lifecycle.

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**. Search for the intended dataset before creating another.
   Choose **New workspace**.
2. Enter **Name** and review **Key**. The suggested key follows the name until you edit it.
   Use lowercase letters and digits separated by single hyphens. The key is permanent and
   identifies this workspace in links; renaming later does not change it.
3. Under **Model**, choose **The default workspace’s model** or **Another installed release**.
   For the latter choose **Installed release** and check the model name and version. The
   picker initially shows each model's newest usable release; reveal older versions if needed.
4. Choose **Add workspace**. The new workspace starts empty. It copies the selected definitions,
   not the default workspace's records, change sets or publications. Changing the default
   workspace later does not change this workspace's selected release.
5. Check its **Overview**, model and applications. Use **Open workspace** to browse its data.
   Arrange data access separately; workspace creation does not grant every person access.
   To start an empty hierarchy, open its tree view and choose **Add …** for its top-level
   type. Create that record first, then add children beneath it; see
   [Arrange records in a tree](/docs/guide/use/arrange-records-in-a-tree/#add-the-first-top-level-record).

![New workspace dialog showing name, key and model choice](/docs/screens/workspaces-new-dialog.png)

**The workspace was not created** explains a refusal, such as a duplicate key or unusable release.
Correct that cause before retrying. **Cancel** leaves the list unchanged.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/retir:
---
title: Retire or delete a workspace
description: Take a dataset out of active use while preserving its history, or delete an eligible empty one.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Workspaces** with **Workspace administration**. See
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for active and retired states.

1. Open the workspace and check its name, key and default status. The default cannot be
   retired or deleted; [make another workspace default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/) first.
2. To keep the data but stop changes, choose **Retire…**. Read the confirmation and choose
   **Retire workspace**, or cancel. It leaves the active selector and becomes read-only.
   Records, change sets, publications and history remain readable through workspace management.
3. To resume work later, open the retired workspace in this list and choose **Reactivate**.
   Check the active state. Reactivation does not change its model release. Retirement also
   suspends its active webhook subscriptions; ask their administrator to resume them separately
   after reactivation.
4. Use **Delete…** only for an empty workspace that has never been published and has no change
   sets or webhook subscriptions. Read the page's explanation of anything preventing deletion.
   Even an emptied workspace with past publications must be retired instead.
5. If eligible and no longer needed, read the deletion confirmation's name and key, then
   choose **Delete workspace**. Cancel preserves it. Do not treat deletion as reversible retirement.

![Retire workspace confirmation](/docs/screens/workspace-retire-dialog.png)

If an action fails or reports a newer workspace version, review the current state before
retrying. A missing action can also mean insufficient permissions or disabled administration.

---
title: Retire or delete a release
description: Stop offering a release for new use or remove an unused release with confirmation.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Model**, then the model's **Releases** and the release. These lifecycle
changes need installation permission. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/).

1. Check its version, workspace use and whether it runs the default workspace. **Retire…**
   stops new selection but keeps existing users on the release. The default workspace's release
   cannot be retired; move that workspace to another usable release first if appropriate.
2. Choose **Retire…**, read the named release and confirm. Cancel keeps it available. Check
   the **Retired** state afterwards. Workspaces and change sets already using it keep working.
3. To offer it again, choose **Bring back** and check that it is available. A model with every
   release retired and no running workspace appears under **Retired** in the model list.
4. Use **Delete…** only for a release with no remaining use or references. **Run by no workspace**
   alone does not prove it is deletable: records, publications, change sets, profiles or mappings
   can still refer to it. Read the confirmation and any refusal before proceeding.
5. Confirm deletion only when the named unused release is no longer needed. Deleting its release
   does not delete editable drafts. If refused, retain it or retire it; do not delete history to
   force a release removal.

![Release retirement confirmation](/docs/screens/release-retire-dialog.png)

If the release changed state elsewhere, reload it and review the current state before retrying.
Retirement is reversible; deletion is not the same operation.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/make-:
---
title: Make a workspace the default
description: Select the default destination without changing other workspaces’ models or data.
reader: model-admin
---

You need **Workspace administration** and the deployment must allow workspace changes.
See [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) for the default workspace's role.

1. Open **Settings › Workspaces**, then the active workspace you want as the default.
   Read its name, permanent key and model in **Overview**.
2. Choose **Set as default**. Check the success notice and **Default** mark afterwards.
   The previous default remains a separate workspace with its own records and model.
3. If another administrator changed the default while your page was open, read the notice,
   reload the state and choose again only if your intended change is still correct.
4. Inspect new-workspace creation choices when relevant: **The default workspace’s model**
   now refers to this workspace's release. Existing workspaces keep their selected releases.

![Workspace management showing the Default mark](/docs/screens/use-workspace-default.png)

Making a workspace default copies no records and grants no access. The default cannot be retired
or deleted. To take it out of use later, first select another active default.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/compa:
---
title: Compare releases
description: Choose a baseline and read the definitions added, changed or removed in an installed release.
reader: model-admin
---

Open **Settings › Model**, select a model, **Releases**, then the release to inspect.
See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) for immutable definitions and permissions.

1. In **Release history**, find **Changes in this release**. Read **Before** and **After**;
   After is the open release. The suggested predecessor comes from activation history or the
   earlier installed release. It is not necessarily the workspace you currently have open.
2. Use **Compare with** to choose another baseline. A comparison may cross model families,
   so check both names and versions rather than assuming they share a lineage.
3. Read the changes table's **Kind**, **Path**, **Before** and **After**. These describe model
   definitions, not a history of record edits. Inspect removals as well as additions.
4. **No semantic changes** means the two documents define the same model. **No earlier release**
   means no predecessor is available; select another baseline if offered.
5. If **Comparison unavailable** names an unsupported model language, choose another release.
   Its metadata and **Export JSON** remain available for specialist inspection. A loading or
   failed comparison is not an empty comparison.

![Release history with baseline selector and semantic before and after changes](/docs/screens/model-release-compare.png)

The separate **Activation check** reads each workspace's data. A small or empty comparison alone
does not establish that activation in a chosen workspace is safe.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/expor:
---
title: Export a release
description: Download the immutable model document and identify its exact release.
reader: model-admin
---

Use export to hand a model document to a specialist author or keep a copy of its definitions.
It exports the model, not workspace records. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/).

1. Open **Settings › Model**, the model's **Releases**, then the intended version. Check its
   name, version and **Immutable release** state rather than opening a similarly named draft.
2. Choose **Export JSON** and keep the downloaded document. The installed release is unchanged.
   Export is also available for historical definitions the current editor cannot interpret.
3. If you need to identify it precisely, open **Technical details**. Use **Copy** beside
   **Release ID** and **Content hash**. The hash identifies the content; the displayed version
   is a human-facing release label.
4. To edit a copy, use **Create draft from release** or the draft creation dialog's **Import
   JSON** option. Importing a document does not activate it. For data backup, use the operator's
   backup procedure instead of treating this file as a workspace export.

![Immutable release with export and draft creation actions](/docs/screens/model-release-detail.png)

![Technical details identifying the release and its content hash](/docs/screens/release-technical-details.png)

If the download fails, read the displayed failure and retry after correcting its cause.
The downloaded file alone does not include records, access grants or publication history.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/chang:
---
title: Change a workspace’s model
description: Choose an installed release and read its data and consumer compatibility checks.
reader: model-admin
---

Choose an installed release for one workspace with **Model release** there. The release must
be usable on this instance. See [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) and [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/).

1. Open **Settings › Model**, select the model and its **Overview**. Beside the workspace choose
   **Change model…**. Alternatively open a release and choose **Activate in a workspace…**.
2. Check **Workspace** and its current model. Under **Release**, choose the target version.
   Expand another model only if you intend to replace the workspace's definitions with it.
3. Wait for the check and read its result:

   | Result | What to do |
   | --- | --- |
   | Compatible with the workspace's data | No record, value or relationship needs migration. Review the destination before activating. |
   | A migration is needed | The same model's definitions require data changes. Use the offered migration preview. |
   | A different model | The different model does not fit the data unchanged. Review its reasons and the migration preview where available. |
   | A consumer API needs a higher contract version | Correct or version the named contract in a draft before activating. |
   | Could not be checked | Correct the stated failure and check again. This is not a compatible result. |

4. Read the listed open change sets left on the old release and other workspaces left unchanged.
   If compatible, confirm activation. If conversion is needed, use **Preview the migration…**
   and follow [Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/).
5. After success, reopen the workspace and inspect its applications. Reload a page reporting a
   model change before editing. A bookmark to a missing application or type shows **Not in this
   model**; choose a collection declared by this workspace's current model.

![Activation dialog selecting a release for one workspace](/docs/screens/model-release-activate-dialog.png)

**Not activated** means the switch failed. Read why, refresh the workspace and check again.
Choosing an older version runs the same checks; it does not restore older record values.


## Check which consumer versions stay available

Compare the target release with the workspace’s current contract, including any earlier
versions it serves. A higher current number does not itself prove every existing consumer
can continue: the target release must retain the earlier definitions. An older installed
release or publication does not keep their live routes available.

A finding ending **a kept version is served as it was: restore it, or stop serving it**
means an earlier contract would read differently. Prepare a corrected draft that restores
that definition and its sources, or coordinate stopping it, then install a new release.
Raising the current contract again does not repair the retained version.

The activation dialog shows blocking consumer differences, and a warning when an earlier
version **stops serving**, naming the version and that its consumers get
`CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`. Agree that removal with all consuming teams
before activating. That version’s reads and feed stop. Webhooks bound to
it can suspend; the integration administrator must check the receiver before resuming on
the current contract. If the version remains retained, its consumers and webhooks continue
in its own shape. A **Sunset day** announces an end but never stops service automatically.

To change which versions the target release retains, use
[Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) or
[Stop serving an earlier contract version](/docs/guide/model/stop-serving-an-earlier-contract-version/)
in a draft. Releases themselves are immutable. **Cancel** leaves the workspace on its
current release; a draft undo does not reverse an activation already completed.
guide/src/content/docs/guide/model/delet:
---
title: Delete a draft
description: Remove an editable draft while keeping installed releases.
reader: model-admin
---

Delete a draft only when its saved design work and attached source are no longer needed.
You need **Model authoring**. See [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the distinction between a draft and a release.

1. Open the draft and inspect **About this draft** and **History** to identify it. If you need
   a copy of its model document, use **JSON**, then **Export JSON**, before deleting.
2. In the editor's **More actions** menu choose **Delete draft…**.
3. Read **Delete this draft?**. This removes the editable draft, its proposals, history and
   attached workbook. Installed releases are not changed. Choose **Cancel** to keep it.
4. Confirm deletion only for the intended draft. Return to **Settings › Model** and check the
   remaining drafts. If deletion fails, read the notice and reload the list before retrying.

![Editor menu with Delete draft and workbook actions](/docs/screens/model-more-actions.png)

Deletion is not an undo of activation or a removal of records. To stop offering a release for
new use, see [Retire or delete a release](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-release/).
guide/src/content/docs/run/ai.md:
---
title: About AI in refiroo
description: Choose which AI features to enable, control what leaves the instance, and understand access, costs and retention.
reader: operator
---

AI is optional. You choose which features to enable in the engine's environment, then restart it.
People review the proposals before using them. To enable it, follow [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/).

## Choose what to switch on

Three settings control separate capabilities. None requires the other two.

| Setting | What it enables | When left unset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AI_AGENT_COMMAND` | The built-in assistant: a Claude Code session that reads a workbook or instructions, works with the workspace's model and records, and prepares changes for review. | No built-in assistant is offered. |
| `AI_PROVIDER` | Requests for mapping targets, questions in words, and accounts of model changes or what changed over a period. | No provider features are offered. |
| `MCP_ENABLED=true` | Access for external assistants through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). | The MCP endpoint, metadata and registration are absent. |

The built-in assistant uses Claude Code's own credentials. Setting `AI_PROVIDER` does not configure
it. Conversely, you can run the assistant without a provider. With both AI settings empty, refiroo
sends no AI requests; separately enabled MCP access still lets an external assistant read what its
permissions allow.

The provider can be `claude`, `openai-compatible` for an endpoint using the chat-completions
protocol, or an operator-supplied factory named `package.module:function`. A locally hosted provider
is an option when reference data must stay within your organisation.

## Control what leaves the instance

`AI_SEND_LEVEL` sets the most data an AI feature may send. The default is `values`.
A feature that needs more than you allow is unavailable.

| Level | What may be sent |
| --- | --- |
| `structure` | Model keys, labels, headers and types, with the question or facts needed by the feature; no record values. Summaries can include counts. |
| `samples` | Also sample values, normally up to `AI_SAMPLE_VALUES` per column or attribute. The default is 20. |
| `values` | The values the feature needs. `AI_SAMPLE_VALUES` does not cap this level. |

A question in words is available at every level. At `samples` and `values`, it can also send all
record names for a relationship's type when its list in the current context has at most 50 records.
That list is not capped by `AI_SAMPLE_VALUES`. At `structure`, it sends none of those names.

The assistant requires `values`: it receives your words, the workspace's model and the whole workbook
if supplied, and can read workspace records as needed. Mapping targets also require `values`:
requests include the source and candidate target names and the fields displayed in the view.
Sources are sent in groups of 25; candidates are all eligible targets up to 100, or each source's
20 closest targets by name for larger sets.

An account of a model change sends the changes and record counts, without record values. An account
of what changed sends counts and model labels; names of records, people, change sets and files are
included only at `values`.

These settings govern refiroo's AI features. They do not impose a send policy on an external MCP
assistant after it reads permitted data. Check that assistant's settings and your organisation's
agreement with its provider too. Even `structure` sends information outside the instance when the
provider is external.

## Who can use it

The **Use AI proposals** action group allows a person to request AI help. The predefined **Data
steward**, **Data owner**, **Model administrator**, **Workspace administrator** and **Integration
administrator** roles include it. Grants determine where those rights apply.

Other permissions still matter: AI access alone does not grant permission to import, edit a model
or work in a change set. People without the action group are not offered AI actions. Operators need
**Operations** to inspect **Settings › This instance › AI** and send a provider test request.

External MCP assistants act within their person's or client's permissions, restricted to browsing
and work in change sets. They cannot approve, publish or write directly to live data. Security
administrators manage them on **Settings › Connections › Agent access**.

## The assistant's session

In the shipped engine container, sessions run as users from a pool, `assistant-1` to
`assistant-N`. Each turn takes a free user until it ends. An engine process runs one session at a time,
so sessions running at the same time use different users. They cannot read each other's process
environment. The image's `ASSISTANT_USERS` build argument sets the pool size, default 8; it must
cover the engine processes in the container (`WEB_CONCURRENCY`). If no user is free, the task
fails with a note naming `ASSISTANT_USERS`; rebuild with a larger pool before trying again.

Each task has a randomly named folder under `/opt/refiroo/rdm-engine/data/assistant`. Session
users can enter that parent folder but cannot list it to discover another task. Inside the task's
folder, `work` holds working files and `claude` holds its own Claude Code configuration and
transcripts. The engine sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for each session. Turn logs are kept inside the
same task folder and are readable only by the engine.

Unix permissions separate the tasks. Between turns, only the engine can enter a task's folder.
For a turn, the engine opens it only to the session user running that turn, then closes it
again afterwards. At engine startup it also closes folders left open by stopped turns; a folder
held by another running turn stays open for that turn. Knowing a folder's name gives another
session no access.

Before each turn, while the task folder is closed, the engine runs
`/usr/local/bin/refiroo-session-reset` as the selected session user, never as root. The reset
repeatedly ends that user's processes until none remain, then empties its home and its files in
`/tmp`, `/var/tmp` and `/dev/shm`. Only a successful reset allows the task folder to open and the
turn to start. After the turn, the reset runs again while the folder is still open. It also makes
that user's files in `work` and `claude` readable and writable by the group, so another session
user can continue the task, and ends the user's processes once more. The engine then closes the
folder. A failed reset before a turn fails the turn; a failure afterwards is logged, and the next
turn under that user must pass its own reset.

Compose runs the engine with `init: true` to collect ended processes. If you run the image directly,
use `docker run --init`.

Each task has a separate client, workspace scope and jobs; concurrent tasks do not share them.
A task is visible only to its requester and the workspace's administrators. The session receives a dedicated refiroo client and temporary grants drawn from the requesting
person's permissions. It cannot publish a change set or activate a model release, even if that
person can. A person reviews the result and takes those steps. Grants end with the session's turn.

The engine does not pass its database address, encryption key or other server secrets to the
session. It passes only named variables: the temporary API token, `LANG`, `LC_*`,
`TMPDIR`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`,
`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`,
`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. The switch
`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` is passed when set; only when it is on are `AWS_REGION`,
`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` and `AWS_PROFILE`
passed too. Other variables, including `HTTPS_PROXY`, are not passed. The session user cannot
read the engine's job-file directory or its process environment.

**The provider's key or token still reaches the session.** Claude Code calls the provider itself.
A session steered by text in a workbook could use or send that credential. Use a dedicated
credential with a spending limit and no unrelated access.

With `AI_AGENT_SANDBOX=container`, Claude Code's own operating-system sandbox is off because it
cannot run there. The session runs with Claude Code's permission prompts off so it can execute
shell commands. The separate session user, which cannot read the engine's secrets or job files,
is its boundary inside the container. **The container does not restrict the session's network
access.** Apply any required outbound network restrictions in your deployment. Outside a container,
refiroo requires the operating-system sandbox; an unavailable sandbox refuses the session.

**Isolation between tasks inside one container rests on Unix permissions and the reset around
each turn.** This has been reviewed twice, with defects found and fixed each time; those reviews
are not proof of isolation. A separate container for each session is a stronger boundary and is
not built into refiroo. Together with the provider credential and unrestricted network access
above, this is a limit to consider before enabling the assistant.

A turn running longer than `AI_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (30 minutes) is stopped like a person's Stop. The task returns to where it can be continued or tried again. Text in records is treated as data, but AI output can still be wrong; review
proposals before accepting them.

## Calls and costs

Open **Settings › This instance › AI** to see which switches are on, the send level and, when a
provider is configured, its model, endpoint, whether a key is set, and the features available.
The key itself is never shown. This page displays settings; change them in the environment.

**Calls** lists provider requests and assistant turns, newest first: who asked, what for, the model,
outcome, tokens, cost when reported, and duration. A failed call includes a failure message.
**Load more calls** reads older entries. With no entries, the page says **No call has been made yet.**
When content logging is on and has not expired, expand **Show what was sent and answered** on a row.
Treat that content as sensitive.

Totals cover the last 30 days. An assistant turn counts as one call, including cache reads and
writes in its token figures. A dash for cost means no cost was reported, not that the call was free.

Claude Code authentication and billing belong to Claude Code. An API key uses API billing; a
subscription token uses its Claude subscription. Provider requests use their separately configured
credentials. Check actual charges and usage limits with the provider; refiroo's call log is not a
billing statement.

**Send a test request** sends a fixed request containing none of your reference data. It tests the
provider, appears in the call log and may incur usage. It does not test the assistant.

## What is kept

| Information | Retention in refiroo |
| --- | --- |
| Call metadata, outcome, tokens and reported cost | Kept after request content expires. There is no configured expiry for the call records themselves; the 30-day totals are a reporting window. |
| A call's request and answer | Not kept in the call log by default. `AI_LOG_CONTENT=true` keeps them for `AI_LOG_CONTENT_DAYS`, default 7, after which content is cleared while the call record remains. For assistant turns this is the prompt and final answer, not the full stream. |
| Assistant task and workbook | `AI_TASK_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 90 days after completion or the last change. The worker's expiry sweep deletes the task and its files; cleanup needs a job-enabled instance. |
| Session folder, session logs and Claude Code transcript | Kept while the task can continue, including failed, stopped and loaded tasks. Once the change set is published or discarded, the migration confirmed, or the task discarded, the next task read removes them and deactivates its client. Expiry also triggers cleanup. |
| MCP tool-call records | `MCP_CALLS_DAYS`, default 90 days. Argument names are recorded, not their values. |

`AI_LOG_CONTENT=false` does not disable the assistant's working files or Claude Code transcripts.
Enable call-content logging only while needed: it can contain reference data. These settings do not
control the provider's own retention.

The shipped Compose file persists each task's working files, Claude Code configuration,
transcripts and turn logs in the `assistant` volume at `/opt/refiroo/rdm-engine/data/assistant`.
Container replacement keeps that volume. A backup may omit it: losing it loses open tasks'
folders and session logs, not records. Normal task cleanup still applies.

When upgrading from the earlier shared-transcript layout, the engine gives existing task folders
random names and keeps their workbooks and files. A task begun before the upgrade starts a new
Claude Code session on its next turn; the old shared transcripts are not moved. The obsolete
`assistant-claude` volume is no longer mounted. See [Upgrades](/docs/run/upgrades/#volumes-and-open-assistant-tasks)
before removing it.

## Provider and assistant settings

Set these in the engine's environment, then recreate the Compose container or restart the host
service. **Settings › This instance › AI** displays them; it does not edit them.

| Setting | Default | What to choose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AI_PROVIDER` | Empty | `claude`, `claude-code`, `openai-compatible`, or a factory `package.module:function`. Empty disables provider features, independently of the assistant. See [credential choices](/docs/run/set-up-ai/#choose-the-features-and-credentials). |
| `AI_MODEL` | Empty | Provider model. Claude defaults to `claude-opus-5-5`; a compatible endpoint requires a model. A factory defines its own default. This does not choose the assistant's model. |
| `AI_API_KEY` | Empty | Provider secret; required for `claude`, optional for compatible endpoints. Never displayed. |
| `AI_BASE_URL` | Empty | Required for a compatible endpoint, for example `http://models.internal:8080/v1`. Claude uses `https://api.anthropic.com` unless a gateway is specified. |
| `AI_SEND_LEVEL` | `values` | `structure`, `samples` or `values`; see the send policy above. A request can choose a lower level, never exceed this ceiling. |
| `AI_SAMPLE_VALUES` | `20` | Positive number of sample values per column or attribute at `samples`. Does not limit `values` or the short relationship lists described above. |
| `AI_MIN_CONFIDENCE` | `0.5` | Number from 0 to 1. Mapping proposals below this confidence are left unmapped. |
| `AI_LOG_CONTENT` | `false` | Keep requests and answers with call records for debugging. |
| `AI_LOG_CONTENT_DAYS` | `7` | Positive number of days to keep logged content; metadata remains. |
| `AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` | Positive number of seconds per provider call. The Claude API adapter makes up to three attempts for temporary failures, so total time can be longer. Does not change the assistant's 30-minute turn limit. |
| `AI_REASONING_EFFORT` | Empty | Compatible endpoints only: `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`. Empty omits the option. For a local thinking model, `none` can avoid a long reasoning phase. |
| `AI_CONTEXT_TOKENS` | Empty | Actual context window of a small model, at least 256 tokens. Mapping requests are sized to half this window; too small a window can refuse even one source. Empty uses the feature's own batch limit. |
| `AI_TASK_RETENTION_DAYS` | `90` | Positive number of days to retain tasks after completion or last change; see retention above. |
| `AI_AGENT_COMMAND` | Empty | Claude Code command, for example `claude --model sonnet`. Empty disables the assistant. refiroo enforces its own tools and permission mode even if the command supplies another. |
| `AI_AGENT_SANDBOX` | Empty | `container` is set in both the shipped image and Compose; Compose overrides any .env value. Otherwise the operating-system sandbox is used. Do not use `container` on a host to bypass sandbox requirements. |
| `AI_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `1800` | Longest one turn of the assistant's session may take; a turn over it is stopped like a person's Stop and the task goes back to its last point. |
| `AI_AGENT_API_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8000` in Compose; otherwise `PUBLIC_URL` | Address the session uses to reach this engine's API. Compose supplies the address inside the engine container unless overridden. Outside Compose, unset or empty uses `PUBLIC_URL`; override it if the engine's machine cannot reach that address. See [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/). |

The Claude API needs outbound HTTPS to `api.anthropic.com`, or the configured gateway. Compatible
endpoints need JSON-schema answers. For Ollama, use its reachable `/v1` address and set
`AI_CONTEXT_TOKENS` to the window the server actually serves, rather than the model's advertised
maximum. `localhost` inside Docker means that container. Increase the provider timeout if the model
cannot answer within it; inspect failed calls before changing it.

## What people review

- **Mapping targets:** the person chooses **Propose targets**. Results are mappings in a change set,
  with confidence and a reason. The **Proposed** filter finds them. A person reviews and edits them,
  then uses the normal approval and publication flow. Editing a target removes its AI mark; history
  retains the origin of published proposals. Sources changed while the request ran are left alone.
  Stopping the job keeps proposals already written.
- **Questions in words:** **Ask** on a table list turns the question into editable filters. It
  changes no record. If only part can be expressed, nothing is applied until the person chooses
  **Use these filters**. It is absent from trees, mapping grids and the Changes page.
- **Model and history explanations:** **Explain this change** or **Explain this period** sends
  facts only when pressed. Counts cover the whole set; the provider receives at most 40 facts of
  each kind with the true totals. Statements link to the facts behind them. Unsupported statements
  are dropped. An empty history period makes no call. Matching facts are cached for an hour, so a
  repeated explanation can avoid another call. Current explanations are in English; they are not
  an assurance that a change is safe.
- **The built-in assistant:** the person reads the proposed model, the check of every workbook row,
  questions and warnings, and can edit the draft or tell the assistant what to change. **Accept the
  model** lets it install a release and load a change set. A person takes the activation, approval
  and publication steps. A saved import profile that still fits can load without an AI session or
  AI cost. Words alone can also prepare changes; a workbook is optional.

A whole type becoming another ends with **Preview the migration**: a person checks and confirms the
migration, which goes live at that confirmation. A partial move uses three steps: activate a release
with both types, review and publish the change set, then activate the final release to remove emptied
types. The proposal is checked against live records and consumer API contracts before this handoff.
An incompatible consumer contract needs its contract version raised; a proposal the data cannot
accept returns with the reason for correction. The assistant does not confirm these steps itself.
If the final model keeps the old type, only activation and publication are needed; no removal step
is shown. Unused session-installed releases are retired when the task ends; a final release needed after a
partial move survives. Do not prune releases in use by workspaces or change sets.

## Recover an assistant task

A task's page gives its reason and the next action. **Stop** ends the current turn, preserving the
task so the person can continue. A stopped correction returns to the last proposal, with a warning
if the draft was already changed. A stopped load discards the change set it was making and returns
to the accepted proposal. With no proposal yet, the task is stopped and takes words or discard.

After a failure or stop, give corrected instructions or choose **Try again as it was**. The same
session continues, or starts if it never ran. If the worker died during a turn, the next turn records
that earlier call as `interrupted` from the session log. Look for **Failed** and the failure sentence
in **Calls**, not only at the latest successful turn. In the container, turn logs sit inside the task folder beside `work` and `claude`; on a host they sit beside the task folder.

On a loaded task, **Discard and load again** discards the unpublished change set, including manual
edits, and asks the assistant to reload with the new words. **Discard this task** ends the task;
if it has an unpublished change set that set is discarded too. A published task cannot be corrected
this way: start a new task. A missing or expired task leads back to workspaces. A saved layout's
check offers **Back to the proposal**; if it no longer fits, **Read it with the assistant** starts a
session. A refused migration leaves the reason and the words box on the task.

## External agent access

`MCP_ENABLED` enables MCP Streamable HTTP, protocol `2025-11-25`, at `/mcp`. The shipped web proxy
passes `/mcp` and `/.well-known/`; forward both when supplying your own proxy, and keep `PUBLIC_URL`
consistent with the public HTTPS address. With the switch off the endpoints return 404 and no agent
token is issued. **Settings › Connections › Agent access** then says **Agent access is off**.

| Setting | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MCP_ENABLED` | `false` | Expose agent access after restart. Independent of both AI switches. |
| `MCP_RATE_PER_MINUTE` | `120` | Positive number of calls per person or client per minute, shared across processes. A refused excess call says how long to wait and is recorded as **Limit reached**. |
| `MCP_OPEN_REGISTRATION` | `true` | Allow assistants to register themselves. Turn off to require registration by a security administrator. |
| `MCP_REDIRECT_HOSTS` | Empty | Comma-separated HTTPS hosts a self-registered assistant may return to, besides loopback addresses. The assistant's displayed name is its own claim. |
| `MCP_CALLS_DAYS` | `90` | Positive number of days to keep tool-call records. Names of arguments are kept, never their values. |
| `MCP_ANSWER_BYTES` | `40000` | Positive maximum bytes for a tool answer. Large pages shrink and return a cursor; an oversized answer that cannot page is refused. Resources return whole. |

A person's assistant opens this instance's own sign-in page with OAuth and PKCE; signing in is
consent. A system's assistant uses an agent client and its grants, with an `agent` token. These
tokens reach only MCP; management and consumer tokens cannot call MCP. A consumer-only grant exposes
only that consumer API's lookup tool. Browse exposes model, record, mapping coverage, history and
change reads. Work in change sets permits adding or editing records and relationships, setting
values, checking and submitting the caller's own change sets. It cannot remove records or clear
values, discard or withdraw change sets, batch, restructure the model, approve or publish. Submitted
change sets stay frozen. Under a second-person rule the person who asked the assistant cannot also
decide its submission.

Security administrators manage clients, registrations and call records on **Agent access**. Blocking
an assistant or deactivating its client stops access on the next call. Restoring a blocked assistant
does not restore ended sessions. People can end their own assistant sessions in their session list.
Unused self-registrations with no open session are removed after 30 days; at most 1,000 unused
registrations can stand. A registration accepts at most 10 return addresses, each at most 2,000
characters. Repeated registrations from one address are slowed; self-registered return hosts are
checked again at sign-in. Tool and resource listings count against the rate limit too. Neither your provider send level nor provider content retention controls
what an external assistant keeps after reading permitted data.

## Read failures and restore service

| Code or outcome | Meaning and action |
| --- | --- |
| `AI_NOT_CONFIGURED` | The feature's own switch is missing: assistant command for tasks, provider for tests and suggestions. No provider means no test call is recorded. Configure the required switch and apply settings. |
| `AI_SEND_LEVEL_TOO_LOW` | The feature needs more data, or the request exceeds the instance ceiling. Agree a send policy before changing it. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | Check the missing action group and workspace grants. AI permission alone grants no other write rights. |
| `AI_TASK_NOT_FOUND` | The task expired, does not exist or belongs to someone else. Ask its requester or a workspace administrator; start a new task if expired. |
| `AI_TASK_VERSION_CONFLICT` | Another action changed the task. Reload it before trying again. |
| `AI_TASK_CHECK_STALE` | The draft changed after the check. Check it again before loading. |
| `AI_TASK_NOTHING_TO_LOAD` | The check has no work to load. Review the proposal and its counts. |
| `AI_TASK_STATE` | That action is unavailable at this stage. Reload and use the page's offered next action. |
| `AI_TASK_DRAFT_HELD` | Another task owns the draft; use a separate draft rather than changing that task's work. |
| `AI_TASK_NEEDS_WORDS` | Supply instructions or a supported workbook. |
| `IMPORT_TOO_LARGE`, `UNSUPPORTED_FILE_FORMAT` | Respect `IMPORT_MAX_BYTES`; supply XLSX or CSV instead of legacy XLS. |
| `unreachable`, `unauthorized`, `rateLimited` | Check endpoint/connectivity, replace the refused key, or wait before retrying, respectively. |
| `declined`, `malformed`, `failed` | The provider declined, returned the wrong shape or otherwise failed. Inspect the failure sentence, model and gateway. No partial malformed answer is used. |
| `timeout`, `cancelled`, `interrupted` | An assistant turn exceeded the session limit (`AI_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), was stopped or lost its worker. Read the task's notes and continue when the cause is resolved. |

A failing provider leaves the feature's ordinary work available. Explanations still show their
facts; a failed question applies no filters; a mapping request reports a warning and a failed
call. **Neither the assistant nor an AI provider is set up** is the AI page's notice when both are
unset. For command, credential, sandbox and startup failures, follow [Set up AI](/docs/run/set-up-ai/#if-startup-or-a-request-fails).

![AI settings showing the assistant and provider on and the permitted send level](/docs/screens/run-ai-settings.png)

![AI provider test result and recorded calls](/docs/screens/run-ai-provider-calls.png)


## Switch off a feature or change its credentials

Use each feature's own switch. Empty `AI_PROVIDER` removes provider features; empty
`AI_AGENT_COMMAND` removes the built-in assistant; `MCP_ENABLED=false` removes external agent
access. Apply the change by [recreating the engine](/docs/run/configure/#apply-a-change) on every
instance that serves the feature. Turning off one switch leaves the other two independent.

Before a planned assistant shutdown, ask requesters to stop running turns and review outstanding
loads. Removing a command is not a way to undo an accepted proposal or published data. Stored call
records, tasks, drafts and files are not erased by these switches; their normal lifetimes still
apply. Keep job workers enabled where expiry cleanup is needed. For external agents, use the
[registration and session controls](/docs/administer/agent-access/) when access must be revoked,
rather than assuming an endpoint switch deletes identities or stored grants.

To replace a provider credential, change `AI_API_KEY` in the private environment, recreate the
engine and send the fixed provider test. To replace the assistant credential, update its
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, recreate, then test an actual assistant turn.
These are separate checks. Revoke the previous credential at its issuer after checking the new
one, or immediately when responding to a leak. refiroo does not renew external credentials for you.
Changing the sealing key does not rotate a provider's API key.

A provider/model change affects later requests; it does not rewrite existing proposals or call
records. Keep the previous private configuration for a reversible setting change, apply it again
if needed, and repeat the relevant feature test. The provider's credential expiry and billing
limits are determined by that provider; inspect a refused call and its issuer's controls.

---
title: Set up AI
description: Enable the assistant and AI provider in Docker Compose, supply credentials, and check that each works.
reader: operator
---

Use these steps for an existing Docker Compose installation. Claude Code is already installed in
the engine image. You do not need `docker exec`, an installation command inside the container, or
an interactive sign-in there.

First decide what data may leave the instance and which features you need. [About AI in
refiroo](/docs/run/ai/) explains the separate switches, permissions, session guards and retention.

## Choose the features and credentials

Both switches are needed for all AI features. Set `AI_SEND_LEVEL=values` for the assistant and
mapping targets. The two switches can use different credentials.

| Features | Switch | With a Claude subscription | With an Anthropic API key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Load a workbook or change records with the assistant; **Change this model…** | `AI_AGENT_COMMAND="claude --model sonnet --permission-mode bypassPermissions"` | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| Proposed mapping targets, asking a list in words, explanations of model changes and what changed | `AI_PROVIDER` | Development and trying features: `AI_PROVIDER=claude-code`, `AI_MODEL=sonnet`; built into the engine image, uses Claude Code's sign-in or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | `AI_PROVIDER=claude`, `AI_API_KEY`; optional `AI_MODEL` |

For a production provider, use the Claude API with an API key, or `openai-compatible` with a
chat-completions endpoint, including a model hosted inside your organisation. `AI_PROVIDER=claude`
cannot use a Claude subscription token. The development subscription option is explained below.

## 1. Open the installation's environment file

Run the commands below from the repository root, where `compose.yml` lives.

- For the normal Compose installation, edit `.env`. If you use a different environment file,
  edit that file and use your existing Compose invocation; `RDM_ENV_FILE` must name the file
  passed to the engine.
- For the documentation's reference instance, edit `guide/reference/.env`. It is generated on the
  first `guide/reference/reference.sh up`. If the instance has not been created, run that command
  first. Do not replace the generated database, encryption or sign-in settings.

Compose passes this file's settings to the engine, including Claude Code's credential variables.
Editing an example file does not configure a running instance.

**`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and `AI_API_KEY` are secrets. Never commit them or a
filled environment file.** The examples below contain placeholders: replace them only in your
private environment file. Do not paste credentials into the assistant's instructions or a support
report.

## 2. Enable the assistant

Add or update these lines in that environment file:

```dotenv
AI_AGENT_COMMAND="claude --model sonnet --permission-mode bypassPermissions"
AI_AGENT_SANDBOX=container
AI_SEND_LEVEL=values
```

The command selects Claude Code and its model. refiroo adds its own session restrictions and
replaces the command's permission-mode option with the mode it enforces. The example does not
remove those guards. `AI_AGENT_SANDBOX=container` runs the session without Claude Code's permission
prompts so it can execute the shell commands needed for a task. The image and Compose already
set it to `container`; Compose overrides a different value in `.env`. Each turn takes
one of the image's separate session users, which cannot read the engine's secrets or job files.
Permissions open the task's folder only to that user for the turn and close it afterwards.
The engine resets that user's processes, home and temporary files before and after the turn;
a failed reset before a turn prevents it from starting. Compose supplies `init: true` to collect
ended processes; a deployment using `docker run` needs `--init`.
The pool has 8 users by default; see [session isolation](/docs/run/ai/#the-assistants-session).
**The provider's key or token reaches the session, and the container does not restrict outbound
network access.** Use a dedicated credential with a spending limit and apply any required network
restrictions in your deployment. **Task isolation inside one container depends on Unix permissions
and the reset around each turn.** Reviews found and fixed defects; they do not prove isolation.
A separate container per session is stronger and is not built in. `values` allows the assistant to read the
workbook and records needed by the task. Lower levels make the assistant unavailable.

`AI_AGENT_API_URL` is the address the assistant's session uses to reach this engine's API.
Compose sets it to `http://127.0.0.1:8000` unless you override it in the environment file, so no
extra setting is needed for the shipped installation. The session runs inside the engine container:
`localhost` there names that container, so a public address such as `http://localhost:8480` would
send it to the wrong port. Keep `PUBLIC_URL` as the address people open in their browsers.

Choose **one** of the following credential methods for Claude Code.

### Use an Anthropic API key

Put your API key in the same environment file:

```dotenv
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=replace-with-your-anthropic-api-key
```

This is Claude Code's variable. `AI_API_KEY` alone does not authenticate the assistant. Leave
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` unset for this method.

### Use a Claude subscription token

On a computer with Claude Code installed and access to your Claude subscription, run:

```bash
claude setup-token
```

Follow Claude Code's browser authorisation and copy the token it prints. Put it in the engine's
environment file:

```dotenv
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=replace-with-the-token-from-claude-setup-token
```

Leave `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset in that file when using the subscription token. Claude Code reads
these variables itself; refiroo passes only the [named session variables](/docs/run/ai/#the-assistants-session),
not every variable with an `ANTHROPIC_` or `CLAUDE_` prefix. Creating the token on your computer
does not automatically transfer it to the engine.
See [Claude Code's authentication documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token)
for its token requirements and lifecycle.

The engine sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` separately for each task, inside its randomly named folder
in the `assistant` volume. No shared Claude Code configuration folder needs mounting.

## 3. Enable the provider if needed

For mapping targets, questions in words and summaries through the Claude API, add:

```dotenv
AI_PROVIDER=claude
AI_API_KEY=replace-with-your-anthropic-api-key
```

This key is separate from the assistant's credential setting. A subscription token is not a
replacement for `AI_API_KEY`. If you use API-key authentication for both, put the API key in both
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `AI_API_KEY`. If you only need the assistant, leave `AI_PROVIDER` unset.

You can set `AI_MODEL` to choose the provider's model and `AI_BASE_URL` to use a gateway. Leaving
both empty uses refiroo's default Claude model and Anthropic's API. The assistant's `--model sonnet`
does not select the provider model.

For an endpoint using the chat-completions protocol, set `AI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible`,
`AI_BASE_URL` and `AI_MODEL`; set `AI_API_KEY` if that endpoint requires one. A provider on another
container or host needs an address reachable from the engine container: `localhost` inside the
container refers to that container.

Keep `AI_SEND_LEVEL=values` for mapping targets. If you enable only features that need less data,
choose `structure` or `samples` instead. `AI_SAMPLE_VALUES=20` controls sampling at `samples`,
not the amount read by the assistant at `values`.

### Use the subscription for provider features in development

The built-in `claude-code` provider answers through Claude Code using the token's or the
developer's sign-in and limits. It is part of the engine image, so it works on a
[developer instance](/docs/run/developer-instance/), on the guide's reference instance and in a
container without extra files.

For a developer instance, put these settings in `.dev/settings.env`; install and authenticate
Claude Code on the host. For the reference instance, put them in `guide/reference/.env` beside the
assistant settings and subscription token from step 2:

```dotenv
AI_PROVIDER=claude-code
AI_MODEL=sonnet
```

Leave `AI_API_KEY` unset for this provider; it authenticates as Claude Code does (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for API billing). Each request runs a separate Claude Code call with no
tools, MCP servers or saved session. It still sends the feature's context to Claude. Usage and
cost are recorded in **Calls**; reported dollar amounts are usage at API prices, not a
subscription invoice. With a subscription token this option is for development and trying the
features. A production installation normally uses `claude` with `AI_API_KEY` or `openai-compatible`.

A custom provider can also be named as `AI_PROVIDER=package.module:function`. The module must be
installed in the engine's Python environment; the factory takes no arguments and returns an object
with `propose(request)`. A missing module or unsuitable result refuses startup.

## 4. Enable external agent access if needed

To let external MCP assistants connect, add:

```dotenv
MCP_ENABLED=true
```

This is optional and does not enable or authenticate the built-in assistant. The shipped web image
already forwards `/mcp` and `/.well-known/`; another reverse proxy must forward them too. After
restart, a security administrator can open **Settings › Connections › Agent access** to register and
manage assistants and agent clients. Their grants determine the data they can reach.

## 5. Apply the settings

:::caution[Automatic HTTPS needs both Compose files]
With [automatic HTTPS](/docs/run/install-with-compose/#5-start-with-automatic-https), run `docker compose up -d` with
`compose.acme.yml` too: keep `COMPOSE_FILE=compose.yml:compose.acme.yml` set in the shell, or add
`-f compose.yml -f compose.acme.yml` to each command. Without it, web is recreated without Caddy
in front and the site stops answering until you run the command again with both files.
:::

For the normal Compose installation, run:

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
```

For the documentation's reference instance, use its own command instead:

```bash
guide/reference/reference.sh start
guide/reference/reference.sh status
```

The reference `start` command starts or recreates its dedicated Compose project's containers without
rebuilding the images or rerunning the data loader. Use `up` for the initial build and data load. It uses `guide/reference/.env`, rather than the repository-root `.env`. Open
`http://localhost:8480` and sign in with the reference administrator's credentials from that file.

Changing the environment requires the engine container to be recreated; `up -d` applies those
changes without rebuilding the image. A plain `docker compose restart` does not load an edited environment file.
The shipped Compose file keeps task folders, Claude Code configuration and session logs in the
single `assistant` volume. Recreating the container keeps it. After upgrading from the earlier
shared-transcript layout, existing tasks keep their files but start a new session on their next
turn; see [Upgrades](/docs/run/upgrades/#volumes-and-open-assistant-tasks).

## 6. Check the provider and assistant separately

1. With **Operations** access, open **Settings › This instance › AI**. Under **What is switched on**,
   check **Assistant** and **Provider** against what you enabled. **Assistant: On** means the command
   is set; it does not prove a session can authenticate. Check **What may be sent** too.
2. If a provider is configured, select **Send a test request**. Success shows **The AI provider
   answered** and a new **Calls** entry. The request contains none of your reference data. With
   only the assistant enabled, this button is absent.
3. To test the assistant independently, use an active workspace and a person with **Use AI proposals**,
   **Work in change sets**, **Bulk and import**, and permission to create jobs there. The model-change
   test also needs **Model authoring** and **Model release** access. Open the workspace's
   **⋯** menu and choose **Change this model…**. Enter a small proposed change in **What should
   change?**, then select **Ask the assistant**. Wait until the task presents its proposal, then
   read it without applying it. Reaching the proposal checks that the assistant can reach the
   engine's API as well as authenticate with Claude Code. This exercises a real session and sends
   the instructions, model and any records it needs.
4. Return to **Settings › This instance › AI**. The session's turn should appear in **Calls** with
   its outcome, tokens and any reported cost. Review or discard the test task when finished.

## If startup or a request fails

| What you see | What to check and do |
| --- | --- |
| The engine refuses to start and names `AI_API_KEY`. | `AI_PROVIDER=claude` needs that setting even if the assistant has credentials. Add the API key, or unset `AI_PROVIDER` if you only want the assistant, then apply the settings again. |
| Startup names `AI_BASE_URL`, `AI_MODEL` or a provider factory. | Supply the required endpoint and model for `openai-compatible`, or correct the factory named in the message. Apply the settings again. |
| Startup names `INFERENCE_ASSISTANT` or `INFERENCE_ASSISTANT_ROWS`. | Remove these retired settings. Use `AI_PROVIDER` and `AI_SAMPLE_VALUES` for the corresponding configuration. |
| The provider test says the key was refused. | Replace `AI_API_KEY` with a valid provider key, apply the settings, and test again. Changing the assistant's token does not fix this test. |
| The provider cannot be reached or returns an answer in the wrong shape. | Check the displayed endpoint, outbound connectivity and gateway settings. A compatible endpoint must support JSON-schema answers. The failed call remains visible; ordinary work can continue without the proposal. |
| The assistant action is missing. | Check `AI_AGENT_COMMAND`, `AI_SEND_LEVEL=values` and the person's grants. The provider switch and MCP switch do not make it appear. |
| A task reports `AI_AGENT_COMMAND could not start`. | Check the command and the image being used. With the shipped image, use `claude` and `AI_AGENT_SANDBOX=container`; its executable and session users are already installed. |
| A task reports that no session user is free and names `ASSISTANT_USERS`. | The image has fewer session users than engine processes need. Rebuild with a pool at least as large as `WEB_CONCURRENCY`: `docker compose build --build-arg ASSISTANT_USERS=16 engine`, then `docker compose up -d engine`. Choose the count for your process count, then retry the task. |
| A task reports that its session user could not be reset. | The turn has not started. Check the engine log and that the image installs `/usr/local/bin/refiroo-session-reset` and permits the engine to run it as a session user through sudo. Restore the shipped image and its init-process setup, recreate the engine, then retry. A reset failure after a turn is logged; the next turn must pass its own reset. |
| A task stops at once with an internal error. | Check `AI_AGENT_API_URL`: an unreachable engine API address can cause this failure. With the shipped Compose installation, remove an incorrect override so Compose supplies `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. On a host installation, use an address reachable from the engine's machine. Apply the settings, start another task and check that it reaches its proposal. |
| A turn fails or says `The session ended without an answer.` | Check the task's warnings and its failed call. Verify the assistant's credential variable, token validity, network access and container sandbox setting. Inspect the task's session log if the message is insufficient; it is inside its randomly named task folder under `/opt/refiroo/rdm-engine/data/assistant`. Treat logs as sensitive. Correct the configuration, apply it, then continue or start the task again. |
| A task's note says the session took longer than the limit | The turn exceeded `AI_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 1800) and was stopped; the task is back at its last point. Check service availability, reduce the task or raise the limit, then continue or try again. `AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` controls provider calls, not this session limit. |
| The task reports `AI_ASSISTANT_ROLE_CHANGED`. | An assistant role no longer has the required action groups. Follow the message to restore them or have an administrator delete that role so refiroo can recreate it, then try again. |

For startup diagnostics on the normal installation, use a bounded log read:

```bash
docker compose logs --tail=100 engine
```

For the reference instance, select its project and environment explicitly:

```bash
docker compose -p refiroo-guide-ref -f compose.yml \
  -f guide/reference/compose.override.yml \
  --env-file guide/reference/.env logs --tail=100 engine
```

## Other installations

On a host installation, install Claude Code where the worker can run it. Set the same credentials
in the worker's environment, leave `AI_AGENT_SANDBOX` unset to use the operating-system sandbox,
and restart the engine and worker through your service manager. The session refuses to run if the
sandbox is unavailable. For the repository's developer installation, settings live in
`.dev/settings.env` rather than Compose's `.env`.

Outside Compose, an unset or empty `AI_AGENT_API_URL` uses `PUBLIC_URL`. Set it yourself when the
engine's machine cannot reach that public address, for example behind a proxy that only answers
outside callers. Use an address for this engine's API that the session can reach from that machine,
then run the assistant check in step 6. Provider credentials still use their own settings; an
internal API address does not change the AI provider's endpoint.


## Maintain or remove the setup

After a credential, endpoint or model change, recreate the engine and repeat the two independent
checks in step 6. Keep the `assistant` volume mounted through replacement. To recover after a
host failure, restore the matching database, job files and keys; preserve the `assistant` volume
as well if open sessions must retain their folders. Without that optional volume, records remain
but an open task can lack the files needed to continue.

For planned switch-off, credential replacement and what stays stored, follow
[AI maintenance](/docs/run/ai/#switch-off-a-feature-or-change-its-credentials).
Do not delete a volume to turn off a feature. Subscription-token renewal takes place through
Claude Code's authentication process; refiroo has no automatic renewal setting for that credential.
guide/src/content/docs/run/webhook-deliv:
---
title: Webhook delivery
description: Enable event delivery, diagnose retries, and retain enough history for recovery.
reader: operator
---

Enable `CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=true` in the engine environment and recreate the container
to serve subscription routes and run delivery. The default is `false`. Subscriptions are deployment
state, separate from model releases. Switching delivery off removes all subscription routes, including reads, and stops the dispatcher.
It preserves stored subscriptions, but their undelivered events can expire while it is off.
Turning it back on resumes delivery subject to subscription validation and event retention;
expired positions suspend delivery as `EVENTS_EXPIRED`. Repeated requests to an absent route do
not turn it on. Check Deployment, enable the setting on the intended instance and recreate it.

An administrator or integration owner manages subscriptions on **Settings › Connections › Webhooks**.
Use [Subscribe a webhook and verify it](/docs/guide/integrate/subscribe-a-webhook-and-verify-it/) for the integration sequence and the
[API reference](/docs/api) for operations. Receivers need a consumer API that declares events.

## Find the subscription's state

Subscription management requires Integration administration for its workspace; an Operator role
alone does not grant it. On **Settings › Connections › Webhooks**, open the subscription by name.
Check the address, consumer API, workspace, selected events, filter tags and request format against
the receiver's configuration. The **Configuration** tab shows its state, suspension reason and
recovery advice. Authorised owners can edit, suspend, resume, rotate its key or delete it there.
Read current state before an edit: a version conflict requires reloading and reviewing the other
administrator's change.

A workspace with subscriptions cannot be deleted. Its refusal identifies the subscriptions to
review; delete unneeded subscriptions or keep the workspace. Retiring a workspace suspends its
subscriptions instead. Before resuming, correct the recorded cause: resume checks the model,
contract, filter and retained position again.

## Network and receiver requirements

Allow direct outbound HTTPS from the engine to receivers. A redirect is not followed: configure
the final URL. By default, a destination is refused if its address, or any address its host name
resolves to, is loopback, private, IPv6 unique-local, shared `100.64.0.0/10` or otherwise non-public.
The check runs when a subscription is created or changed and again at every delivery attempt.
Each attempt resolves DNS again and connects to the checked address. There is no host allowlist.

For a receiver inside your network, set `WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES_ALLOWED=true` and recreate
the engine. It is off by default. Plain HTTP is accepted only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or
`::1`, and also needs this setting on. Link-local addresses are always refused, even with the
setting on. A refused delivery records an `address` attempt with its reason in the delivery log.
After upgrading, existing subscriptions on private addresses stop delivering until the setting
is on; check their attempts and resume any that became suspended after correcting the cause.

Certificates must verify against the system trust store. For an internal CA, supply a bundle with
`SSL_CERT_FILE`. Delivery does not use an outbound proxy.

A receiver must durably accept the POST and return 2xx within ten seconds. Allow bodies up to 1 MiB
and larger for an unusually large single object. Verify the timestamp and `RDM-Signature`, and
deduplicate events by `eventId`: delivery is at least once. During key rotation, accept any valid
signature in the comma-separated header. Signing secrets must never be committed or logged.
[Consumer events and webhooks](/docs/integrate/consumer-events-and-webhooks/) explains the protocol.

## Retries and suspensions

Requests to one subscription stay ordered. A failed batch blocks later batches and keeps its events
and delivery ID while retrying after 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 1, 2, 5, 10 and 30 minutes, then hourly,
with 20% jitter. After 24 hours from its first failure, the subscription is suspended.
Inspect its pending attempt, last error and next-attempt time before restarting anything.

| Suspension | Recovery |
| --- | --- |
| `DELIVERY_FAILED` | Fix the receiver or URL, then resume from the first unacknowledged event. Editing the URL retries immediately. |
| `FILTER_MATCHES_NOTHING` | Fix the filter and resume. |
| `EVENTS_EXPIRED` | Resume with reset first (it starts after the feed head named in the message), then reload the receiver from current data taken after the reset. The publication named in the details may be older than the head. |
| `MODEL_CHANGED` | Review what the activated model removed; correct the subscription before resuming. |
| `CONTRACT_VERSION_CHANGED` | Update the receiver for the selected consumer contract, then resume. |
| `WORKSPACE_RETIRED` | Resolve the workspace's retired state before resuming delivery. |

Events derive from the change feed in the background, normally checked once per second. They expire
with `FEED_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 30, and are cleaned hourly. A consumer's `headPosition` is the
derived event head, which can lag the workspace feed. Several processes divide derivation by
workspace and delivery by a 60-second subscription lease.

## Retain delivery evidence

`CONSUMER_WEBHOOK_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` defaults to 7. The delivery log keeps request bodies up to
1 MiB and response excerpts up to 4 KiB, with attempts and durations. Retried or awaiting-resume
batches can remain longer. Expiry runs at most hourly. Inspect **Deliveries** on the webhook's page. Choose **Status**: **All**, **Queued**, **Sending**,
**Retrying**, **Succeeded**, **Failed** or **Dropped**, and use **Refresh** to read again.
The table shows **Event ID**, **Event**, **Object ID**, **Status**, **Attempts**, **Response** and
**Sent**. Open an event ID for the request as sent, each attempt and its response excerpt.
**No delivery has this status** can mean the filter is too narrow; **Nothing delivered yet** means
there are no retained deliveries to show, not proof the receiver never received data.

**Resend** sends the selected event again; an already delivered event asks **Resend a delivered
event?** before **Resend event**. A failed event can be resent directly. An event never sent has
nothing to resend and the control is disabled. A manual resend is marked with `RDM-Redelivery`;
the receiver must still deduplicate by event ID. It does not repair the subscription's normal
position or replace resolving its suspension. Operations summarizes failing and suspended subscriptions. Budget database space for these payloads
and restrict access to logs containing reference data. Your delivery capacity is **not measured**.

Rotate a subscription key when it leaks or policy requires it. The default overlap is 24 hours,
up to seven days; **Stop it now** selects zero, which ends the old key at the next delivery. Give the receiver the new key before
the overlap ends. This is separate from [resealing the installation's secrets](/docs/run/secrets-and-keys/).

Filters use a record's state at delivery time. A record leaving a filtered scope is not delivered
as a removal; deletions are always delivered. A receiver needing exact scope membership should
subscribe by type and narrow locally, or periodically reconcile its list.

The subscription defaults to one event per request. For a bulk workload, choose a larger batch
(up to 1,000 events); requests stop at 1 MiB except that a single larger event is sent alone.
A slow receiver adds its response time to each sequential request. Increase batching before
assuming another engine process speeds up one subscription; several processes share its lease
and preserve its order.

## Enable and check delivery without creating duplicate loads

Before enabling delivery, have an Integration administrator for the workspace, a consumer API with
events, a working HTTPS receiver, its signing-secret storage and enough retained feed history for
the expected outage window. The operator needs Docker and Operations access. CPU, database sizing
and delivery throughput for that receiver are **not measured** by this guide.

1. Set the capability in the private environment and recreate the engine:

   ```dotenv
   CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=true
   ```

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d engine
   curl -i https://refiroo.example.org/health
   docker compose logs --tail=100 engine
   ```

   Expect readiness 200 and `webhookDispatcher` Running on Operations once a model is servable.
   No subscription means there is nothing to deliver; a running dispatcher alone is not a test
   of the receiver.
2. Ask the Integration administrator to review the subscription's URL, workspace, contract version,
   filter and retained position. Coordinate a harmless reviewed change with the data owner, then
   check the event and successful attempt in Deliveries and the receiver's durable event log.
3. Compare delivery ID, event ID and response status across both sides. Confirm that a retry of an
   already stored event is acknowledged without applying it again. Verification/deduplication is
   the receiver's responsibility; a successful HTTP answer does not prove its downstream update.
4. If delivery is failing, inspect the same pending batch and fix its cause. Do not delete and
   recreate the subscription merely to clear its state: that can abandon its recorded position.

These delivery-related environment settings are non-secret and need engine recreation:
`CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED`, `WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES_ALLOWED`,
`CONSUMER_WEBHOOK_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` and `FEED_RETENTION_DAYS`.
The subscription's signing secret is secret database state sealed with the installation key.

## Recover a suspension in order

For `DELIVERY_FAILED`, repair the receiver's certificate, body limit, authentication or response
time, then resume the existing subscription. Inspect the first resumed delivery and the receiver
before declaring the backlog recovered. Later events wait behind the failed batch by design.
For `FILTER_MATCHES_NOTHING`, correct the saved filter, then resume and check its scope.

For `EVENTS_EXPIRED`, coordinate a full receiver re-sync with the integrator. Reset the subscription
first, then load the publication/list named by the refusal and reconcile the receiver. Reset starts
after the current head; it does not replay expired events. A receiver loaded before reset could
miss the interval between loading and reset. Preserve the old receiver state or a rollback copy
until reconciliation and later deliveries have been checked.

After `MODEL_CHANGED` or `CONTRACT_VERSION_CHANGED`, involve the model administrator and receiver
owner before resuming. After `WORKSPACE_RETIRED`, resolve the workspace's retirement intentionally;
repeated engine restarts do not change that state. Manual **Resend** is for a retained event and
does not move the normal subscription position or repair a suspension.

To pause the entire capability, restore `CONSUMER_SUBSCRIPTIONS_ENABLED=false` and recreate.
Subscriptions stay stored, while their events continue to age. To undo that pause, enable it again,
then inspect each subscription for expiry and validation failures. This is not an indefinite queue
retention switch. For a single receiver pause, use the subscription's suspend operation through
its administrator, retaining its identity and position.

The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a literal dot and the exact request body:
`{RDM-Timestamp}.{body}`, using the subscription's signing secret. Receivers must check timestamp
freshness as well as the signature. An nginx receiver with its default 1 MiB body limit may refuse
an unusually large single event; arrange an adequate receiving limit before enabling delivery.

A dispatcher handles four subscriptions concurrently, while requests for each subscription stay
sequential. Each failed attempt writes one INFO line and each suspension one WARNING line. Check
these alongside the saved attempt history; adding processes does not parallelise one subscription.
guide/src/content/docs/run/background-jo:
---
title: Background jobs
description: Operate workers, retained files, imports, exports and model-authoring jobs.
reader: operator
---

Background workers run inside each engine process. `INTEGRATION_JOBS_ENABLED=true`, the default,
enables creating and running jobs. Turning it off keeps job reads available but stops workers and
job mutations. Work also needs a healthy model. Check **Settings › This instance › Jobs** for job
state and outcomes, and **Operations** for worker health. Permissions determine which jobs a person
may inspect or cancel; see [Jobs](/docs/use/jobs/).

## Inspect results before retrying

A job may be queued, running, awaiting confirmation, completed, failed, cancelled or expired.
A completed job can still contain rejected rows. Read its applied, unchanged, rejected and
unprocessed counts, and open individual outcomes for the refusal code and reason.

The request's failure policy matters. An `atomic` batch applies all its items in one transaction
or none if an item is refused; an `independent` batch keeps successful items and reports refused
ones separately. Cancellation of independent work retains committed chunks. Do not promise an
all-or-nothing result merely because the work was submitted as one job.

Correct refused rows before retrying. For imports, preview the corrected file again: already-loaded
rows can be reported as unchanged. For a batch, submit the corrected items with current versions;
blindly sending every create again can return duplicate-ID refusals. An expired preview needs a
new preview, even if an old browser page still shows it waiting.

For an integration, the sequence is submit a batch or import, follow the returned job, inspect its
outcomes, then confirm a preview or correct its refusals. See the [batch, import and job operations
in the API reference](/docs/api). The requester needs write permissions in the chosen workspace
and any required change-set claim; jobs recheck the requester's rights as they run. Losing access,
retiring the workspace, or changing its selected release can stop remaining work.

If creation or cancellation routes are missing, check `INTEGRATION_JOBS_ENABLED` on Deployment.
With it off those routes are absent, not merely paused buttons. Existing job reads still work.
Enable it on the intended deployment and recreate the engine before retrying; enabling it grants
no additional permissions. Monitor the worker before submitting the same work again.

## Restart and cancellation

A graceful stop finishes the running chunk and releases the lease. After a crash, that chunk rolls
back. Another worker resumes at the first item without an outcome after the lease expires;
completed items are not applied twice. `JOB_LEASE_SECONDS` defaults to 120 and is renewed by a
heartbeat every third of that interval. A queued job may be waiting behind another batch or import.

Cancellation takes effect at the next chunk boundary. An atomic job rolls back completely.
An import that is still reading checks cancellation every 10,000 rows. Exports also check every
10,000 rows, with CSV checks between records and relationships. A database outage is retried every
two seconds and does not need a process restart when connectivity returns.

`JOB_CHUNK_ITEMS` defaults to 500; larger chunks keep a workspace's write lock longer.
`JOB_RETENTION_DAYS` defaults to 7 for finished outcomes and idempotency keys. Expiry runs hourly.
Check the [limits catalogue](/docs/run/configure/) before raising item counts or file sizes.

## Keep and back up the file directory

`JOB_FILE_DIR` defaults to `var/job-files` under the backend; the Compose image uses the persisted
`/opt/refiroo/rdm-engine/data/job-files` volume. Startup creates it and refuses an unwritable directory when job creation
is enabled. Share it across instances. Do not remove files manually to free space: extend storage
or adjust retention and let cleanup enforce the lifecycle.

| Work | File lifetime and recovery |
| --- | --- |
| Export | Writes a `{jobId}.{lease}.partial` belonging to that worker, then renames to JSON Lines, CSV or XLSX on completion. Output remains until job expiry; failed/cancelled and orphan files are cleaned at startup or the hourly sweep. `410 JOB_OUTPUT_MISSING` means rerun the export. |
