The subscription ID is an extension attribute; the event type combines `rdm.`, the declared event name and its change.

Follow [Subscribe a webhook and verify it](/docs/guide/integrate/subscribe-a-webhook-and-verify-it/) for setup, testing, rotation and recovery in order. The [Events reference](/docs/api/?api=consumer-stops-v1#consumer-stops-v1/GET/api/consumer/stops/v1/events) documents the actual contract on your instance.

*Source: opentransportdata.swiss, Service Points (Didok), Federal Office of Transport / SBB, snapshot 2026-11-02. Wikidata, CC0. Webhook event occurrence, delivery IDs and the verification key are illustrative; the Events response above was read from the reference instance.*

## Rules for event declarations

An event lists at least one exposed object type and at least one of `created`, `updated` and `deleted`, without duplicates. Custom event keys are unique lowercase URL keys. `watch.fields` uses output names, including declared parent, path or hierarchy outputs and `objectType`; `watch.related` uses related-block names. A watch must name at least one output or block, without repeats, and requires updated among the changes. No watch means every output is watched. Watches restrict updates; they do not suppress creation or deletion.

Reducing notification coverage is breaking: removing an event, type, change kind or watched output, or adding a limiting watch, needs a higher contract version. Adding coverage or dropping a watch is compatible. The `stops-changed` example above is a custom event, not the automatically named event for its type.

## Subscription defaults and lifecycle

The defaults are `maxEventsPerBatch: 1`, `payload: "full"` and `format: "rdm"`. Batching, payload and format are independent choices. Creation starts after the workspace’s committed feed head, so it receives future changes even if event derivation is behind. To catch up from a retained earlier position, supply `startAfter`, for example a publication’s `eventSequence`; expired or future positions are refused. Omitted workspace selects and stores the deployment’s default workspace at creation.

Subscriptions have active or suspended status and use optimistic concurrency for edits. The creator appears as `owner` (kind, ID and name); older entries can have a null owner. The list can filter by owner. Ownership itself grants no permission: Integration administration in that workspace is required. The [subscription reference](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/consumer%20subscriptions) describes creation, reads, edits, suspend, resume, rotation and deletion.

On activation, the subscription is checked against its accepted version while that version remains served, including a retained earlier version. A missing API, event or filter produces `MODEL_CHANGED` and findings. When the accepted version stops being served and the current declaration still supports the subscription, it suspends with `CONTRACT_VERSION_CHANGED`. It does not silently rewrite the subscription. Retirement produces `WORKSPACE_RETIRED`. A stale filter is checked before sending, including before its deletions; fix the filter and resume to receive unacknowledged events. Resume preserves the accepted version while it remains served; otherwise it validates and accepts the current one. Treat that changeover as a receiver contract change.

A signing secret is generated from 32 random bytes, shown once as `signingSecret`, and stored sealed with AES-256-GCM under the deployment’s `SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Obtain a new secret through rotation if it is lost. Operators manage the sealing key; it is separate from the receiver’s HMAC secret.

## Delivery boundaries

The fixed body limit is 1,048,576 bytes in the selected format, except that one larger event is sent alone. [Capabilities](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/model) reports this as `consumerSubscriptions.delivery.maxBytes` and the event maximum as `maxEventsPerBatch`. Check the receiver and reverse proxy limits: nginx’s default `client_max_body_size` is exactly 1 MiB and can reject that single-event exception.

HTTPS accepts any port, subject to the address checks. By default, loopback, private, IPv6 unique-local, shared `100.64.0.0/10` and other non-public addresses are refused, including when any address returned by DNS falls in those ranges. An operator can allow them with `WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_ADDRESSES_ALLOWED=true`. Plain HTTP accepts only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`, with that setting on. The dispatcher resolves the host on every attempt and connects to the checked address. IPv4 link-local `169.254.0.0/16` and IPv6 link-local `fe80::/10` are always refused. Refused deliveries have an `address` attempt and a reason in the delivery log. After an upgrade, existing private receivers stop receiving until the operator enables the setting; see [Webhook delivery](/docs/run/webhook-delivery/#network-and-receiver-requirements). It uses the system TLS trust store and no outbound proxy. There is no destination-host allowlist.

Retries run for 24 hours from the first failure, rather than from the most recent attempt. Success resets the failure count. Inspect `delivery.pending` for attempts, first failure, last error and next attempt. An edit or resume drops the pending batch and attempts delivery again from the unacknowledged position, using the revised configuration.

CloudEvents uses structured JSON only, with no binary mode, `dataschema`, OPTIONS webhook handshake or bearer-token handshake. HMAC signs every delivery. The `source` is a relative URI for the API and workspace; resolve it against your instance if an absolute address is needed. The pull feed always uses RDM JSON.

## Feed defaults and version changes

Full event pages default to 100 objects, with a maximum of 100. Identity pages default to 500 events, with a maximum of 1,000. Use `after` or `cursor`, never both. Filtering scans at most ten pages of underlying events per response, which explains a short page that is not caught up.

Derivation happens after commit and can lag writes. `headPosition` and `caughtUp` describe derived events, not every committed write. Each entry is evaluated under the model release used for the original write. A feed at the current contract version includes older events too: each event retains the `contractVersion` that derived it, while a full object is composed under the requested version. A retained earlier version reads events derived for that version, including those from when it was current, and composes full objects with its own definition. It continues receiving new changes in its shape while retained. Do not treat that full object as a historical copy.

Retention is controlled by `FEED_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30), bounded by the active publication’s position so its baseline remains usable. With no active baseline publication, events do not expire. Save the lasting cursor after durable processing, including on empty filtered pages, and reconcile from the indicated baseline after `410 EVENTS_EXPIRED`.

Delivery progress changes neither the subscription’s `version` nor `updatedAt`; suspension does. Do not poll the edit version as a delivery checkpoint. The delivery list has one row per event of a request, sharing the request outcome. Request details show the latest sent body, byte count and attempts with timing, status and at most 4 KiB of the receiver’s response. Before the first attempt there is no sent body to resend. Use the [delivery operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/consumer%20subscriptions) to diagnose these states.

## Move or remove a receiver

For a new receiver address, read the subscription and edit its URL using the current version through the [subscription operations](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/consumer%20subscriptions). Preserve the signing secret in protected receiver configuration, or rotate it if the new receiver cannot use it. Editing clears a pending batch and starts again from the unacknowledged position under the new configuration. The old receiver may already have accepted events; transfer its deduplication records and durable queue, or deliberately reconcile duplicates. A delivery already in flight can finish during a changeover.

Suspend when stopping temporarily; resume continues from the unacknowledged position while retained events are available. Delete when retiring the integration, using the current subscription version. Deletion removes its delivery log and signing-key configuration; it does not undo effects at the receiver or remove business records. Save the required diagnostics first. A newly created subscription starts after its chosen position, not the deleted subscription's checkpoint.

The instance's database and encrypted subscription secrets belong to [operator backup and restore](/docs/run/backup-and-restore/); the receiver's queue, accepted secrets and deduplication records need its own backup. After restoring either side, inspect positions and local processing before resuming. Expect replay where the receiver's state is older. Rebuild a baseline when the server no longer retains the receiver's missing range. Losing the sealing key requires operator recovery; rotating a receiver secret is not a replacement for restoring that deployment key.

## Keep a receiver on an earlier contract

Raising a consumer API’s current version does not pause a subscription if its accepted
version remains in `earlierVersions`. It keeps its position and receives that earlier
version’s events and full-object shape. The pull feed remains available at the earlier
version’s `/events` path, subject to the normal retention window. Neither method returns
historical object values: full objects are composed from live data in the requested shape.

When creating through the [subscription operation](/docs/api/?api=management#tag/consumer%20subscriptions),
set `contractVersion` to the served earlier version you want. If omitted, creation accepts
the current version. The browser’s **Consumer API** selector creates subscriptions at the
current version; use the operation to bind a new subscription to an earlier one. The
following illustrative request binds a receiver to v1 while the active release serves v2
and retains v1:

```http
POST /api/v1/consumer-subscriptions HTTP/1.1
Host: <instance>
Authorization: Bearer <management-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Stop mirror v1",
  "consumerApi": "stops",
  "contractVersion": 1,
  "workspaceKey": "graubuenden",
  "events": ["stops-changed"],
  "url": "https://receiver.example/refiroo-events",
  "payload": "full",
  "format": "rdm",
  "maxEventsPerBatch": 1
}
```

Replace the reserved example receiver with your endpoint. The successful creation returns
201 and records `contractVersion: 1`; store the one-time signing secret
as usual. An unserved requested version is refused with HTTP 400 `CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`;
its details name the current `contractVersion`, all `servedContractVersions` and the
`/contractVersion` pointer. For example, after stopping v1 with only v2 remaining:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Consumer API 'stops' has no contract version 1; it serves 2",
    "details": {
      "contractVersion": 2,
      "servedContractVersions": [2],
      "pointer": "/contractVersion"
    }
  }
}
```

This refusal is illustrative. Rediscover the available versions rather than silently choosing a different one.

When an activated release stops that version, the subscription is suspended with
`CONTRACT_VERSION_CHANGED` if its events and filters remain valid against the current
contract. The diagnostic says, for example, **Consumer API 'stops' is served at contract
version 2 now; resuming accepts it**. If its declarations no longer resolve, it instead
reports `MODEL_CHANGED` and lists what must be edited. The pull route for the stopped
version returns `404 CONTRACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`.

Read the new document and update the receiver before resuming. Editing or resuming while
the accepted version is still served preserves it; once that version stops, resume accepts
the current version. Check the resulting `contractVersion` and first deliveries. Normal
resume continues from the unacknowledged position; reset skips waiting events and needs
reconciliation. See [earlier-version discovery and headers](/docs/integrate/consumer-apis/#earlier-contract-versions)
and [diagnose a paused webhook](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/).
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/manage-a:
---
title: Manage access
description: Connect sign-in, people, roles, system clients, key rotation and security review.
reader: access-admin
---

These journeys connect getting into refiroo with granting and reviewing access. People and
systems need permission for the work they do, in the workspace where they do it. An administrative
role does not automatically grant access to reference data. Start with
[People and access](/docs/about/people-and-access/) for the distinction between roles and grants.

## Sign in and work

A person opens refiroo, signs in by an offered method and returns to the page they wanted.
[Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/) explains local passwords, an organisation's provider, passkeys
and second factors. [Account](/docs/use/account/) connects personal security settings, password
changes and sessions. Use the account menu to sign out when finished, or end other sessions from
your account when needed.

Repeated failed sign-ins are slowed. If a required second factor is unavailable, use a saved
recovery code or ask an administrator to
[help after a lost device](/docs/guide/administer/help-someone-who-lost-a-device/).
Where mail is configured, a forgotten-password request can provide a fresh one-use link; a reset
does not remove the second factor. If sign-in succeeds but no workspace opens, ask for Browse
access rather than resetting the password again.

## Manage who can do what

A security administrator [adds a person](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-person/), who sets their
password through the one-use link, or arranges the organisation's provider sign-in.
Next read [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) and
[grant a role](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-role/) directly or through a
[group](/docs/guide/administer/manage-a-group/). Choose the workspace and, when appropriate,
[narrow writes to record types](/docs/guide/administer/narrow-a-grant-to-record-types/).
Browse covers the workspace; narrowing writes does not hide other records there.

Review effective access, including grants inherited through groups and from the installation.
A Reader reads but cannot write; a Contributor proposes changes in change sets. Grants and
activation state take effect on the next request, and jobs recheck their requester's permissions.
The last security administrator cannot be removed. Use [Audit](/docs/administer/audit/) to check
who changed access and investigate a refusal against the action and workspace it names.

## A system calls with a client

An integration team asks a security administrator to create a separate identity for its system.
Read [Clients](/docs/administer/clients/), then
[create a client](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-client/) and save its secret when it is shown
once. Give it management roles for the work it must perform, or
[grant a consumer API](/docs/guide/administer/grant-a-consumer-api-to-a-client/) in the intended
workspace. One kind of grant does not imply the other.

The integrator then follows [system sign-in](/docs/integrate/signing-in-and-tokens/) and
[obtain system access](/docs/guide/integrate/get-a-token/) to connect the system under those grants.
Check allowed work and refused work before relying on it. Later,
[rotate the client secret](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-client-secret/) with an overlap when
needed, or deactivate the client to end its access. A deactivated client cannot keep working
with previously issued access. Keep a client separate from a person's browser account so its
activity and grants remain identifiable.

## Rotate a key

A security or integration administrator first identifies which credential needs replacement.
[Signing keys](/docs/administer/signing-keys/) explains ordinary replacement and emergency
retirement; [Rotate signing keys](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-signing-keys/) carries the chosen
action through verification. Normal replacement preserves existing access until expiry.
Emergency retirement ends access signed with the retired key immediately; browser sessions renew
and integrations must obtain fresh access.

For a delivery-signing key, [rotate a webhook key](/docs/guide/administer/rotate-a-webhook-key/)
from that webhook instead. Share the new key securely with its receiver and use the chosen overlap
to maintain verification during handover. These actions do not replace a client's secret.
Changing the encryption key used to store secrets is a separate operator procedure in
[Secrets and keys](/docs/run/secrets-and-keys/); coordinate that work with the operator.

## Check the security model

A security reviewer, administrator or integrator needs to understand where access is enforced
and how to assess the deployment. Begin with [Security, audit and privacy](/docs/about/security-and-trust/),
then compare the intended access with [Roles and grants](/docs/administer/roles-and-grants/) and
[Audit](/docs/administer/audit/). Include direct, group and installation-wide grants, writes
narrowed to types, background work and the separate grants for consumer APIs.

The service enforces permissions across browser and integration operations. Hiding a button is
not the security boundary. Deactivation and revoked permissions affect later requests and job
steps. Use the [Security checklist](/docs/run/security-checklist/) with the operator for HTTPS,
credential storage and deployment controls. Integrators can continue with
[the security model for integrations](/docs/integrate/security-model-for-integrators/).
This review connects the documented rules and evidence; it is not a separate security-checking
screen in refiroo.

## Move people to the organisation's sign-in provider

A security administrator [adds a sign-in provider](/docs/guide/administer/add-a-sign-in-provider/)
and tests complete sign-in, then [links an existing person](/docs/guide/administer/link-a-provider-person/)
where needed to preserve their grants and history. Review any provider-group mappings as well
as direct grants. Changing the provider's credentials requires coordination with its owner;
[Sign-in](/docs/administer/sign-in/) explains the recovery path.

[Require a second factor](/docs/guide/administer/require-a-second-factor/) for local accounts
and prepare recovery before losing a device. When provider sign-in is proven,
[turn off ordinary local sign-in](/docs/guide/administer/turn-off-local-sign-in/) only after
testing the retained local administrator route. That switch keeps accounts, roles and existing
second-factor requirements. Test both intended sign-in and recovery afterwards.

## Tailor a responsibility and remove access when it ends

[Create a custom role](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-custom-role/) from an existing role or
from nothing, choose its action groups, then grant it in the intended scope. Changing it later
affects every holder; copying a role does not keep the copy linked to its source. Review the
[permissions reference](/docs/administer/permissions-reference/) and the recipient's effective
access after changing it. Remove all grants before deleting an unwanted custom role.

When a person leaves, [People and groups](/docs/administer/people-and-groups/) connects
account deactivation, membership and retained attribution. Removing one grant can leave other
access in place. Deactivation stops the next request without erasing data history; refiroo
refuses changes that would remove the last active security administrator.

## Configure publication review and system delivery

[Set an approval policy](/docs/guide/administer/set-an-approval-policy/) with the workspace's
administrator, then use [Change with approval](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/) for an
actual proposal and decision. A changed policy affects waiting decisions too; inspect the
current policy rather than assuming the one used during preparation still applies.

For event delivery, [create a webhook](/docs/guide/administer/create-a-webhook/), agree its
signing key with the receiver and inspect a real delivery. If it stops,
[find out why a webhook paused](/docs/guide/administer/find-out-why-a-webhook-paused/) before
resuming or resetting. Reset can skip changes; restore the receiver's baseline when needed.
See [Webhooks](/docs/administer/webhooks/) for disabling, deleting and rotating delivery keys.

## Control assistant access and inspect AI use

[Manage agent access](/docs/guide/administer/manage-agent-access/) to inspect external-assistant
registrations, clients and call records, or stop an unwanted connection. Its read-and-prepare
ceiling still applies when the underlying person's grants are broader. Ending a personal
connection and blocking an assistant have different scopes.

With **Operations**, [check the AI provider](/docs/guide/administer/check-the-ai-provider/),
read the send policy and inspect calls and costs. Server settings are changed by the operator,
not by this page. [AI administration](/docs/administer/ai/) explains retained records and
separately enabled features; [Work with an assistant](/docs/journeys/work-with-an-assistant/)
connects them to their actual tasks.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/work-wit:
---
title: Work with an assistant
description: Find records in words, review AI proposals and connect an assistant that prepares changes.
reader: steward
---

Choose the help that fits your task. A provider proposes mapping targets, turns questions into
list filters and explains changes. The built-in Claude Code assistant prepares models and data
from words or a workbook. An external assistant connects separately through the Model Context
Protocol (MCP). Your operator enables each separately.

Built-in actions need **Use AI proposals** in the workspace and the permissions for the task.
Your words and the information allowed by the instance's send level are sent to the configured
service; an external assistant instead receives what its grants allow it to read. Requests can
incur charges. refiroo keeps call records and, for built-in tasks, the workbook and proposal for
the configured retention period. Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for the full
access, disclosure, cost and retention rules before starting.

## Use AI proposals

An operator enables the assistant or provider in the server configuration, chooses how much
information may be sent, and restarts the service. [Running AI](/docs/run/ai/) explains the
settings and failure recovery. A configuration that cannot work refuses startup and names the
setting to correct.

With **Operations**, open **Settings › This instance › AI** to inspect which help is on and
what may be sent. [Check the AI provider](/docs/guide/administer/check-the-ai-provider/) leads
through **Send a test request**, which contains no reference data, then the call records and
30-day totals. A refused key, unreachable service or unreadable answer is recorded as a failure.
An absent provider does not disable an independently enabled built-in assistant. Neither enabled
means no built-in AI action and nothing sent by those features.

## Targets for unmapped values

A steward with **Use AI proposals** and **Work in change sets** opens a mapping grid and chooses
**Propose targets**. This needs a provider and permission to send record values. Follow
[Propose targets](/docs/guide/use/propose-targets/) to choose an existing or new change set,
start the job and inspect the outcome. The grid's search and chosen parent bound the sources.
The provider receives source names and displayed fields, with only eligible target candidates:
all up to 100, otherwise each source's 20 closest by name.

Use **Show proposed** and the **Proposed** filter to review the mappings, confidence and reasons.
A low-confidence or missing answer leaves its source unmapped; a source changed meanwhile is
left alone and counted. **Stop** keeps proposals already saved. Correct a target with **Change**
and **Save**; the replaced mapping loses its AI mark. Validate and publish through the
workspace's normal approval process. Live stays unchanged until publication, and published
history records the AI origin and publisher. See [Mapping grids](/docs/use/mapping-grids/#targets-proposed-by-ai).

## Load a workbook, or change records, with the assistant

A steward starts from **Import** on a collection, or the workspace's **Ask about these records…**.
The built-in assistant needs permission to send values, **Use AI proposals**, **Bulk and import**
and **Work in change sets** to accept and load. Model work also needs the appropriate model
permissions. Follow [Load a workbook with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/load-a-workbook-with-the-assistant/)
or [Change records with the assistant](/docs/guide/use/change-records-with-the-assistant/).

Give a file and a few words, or words alone. Review the proposed types, fields, relationships,
questions and **Checks**. For a workbook, **What the load does** shows new records, existing
records matched, new relationships, refused items and rows read. Open a type's row for example
records with their source cells; inspect repeated-name findings and **Where each part of the
file goes**. Unexpected new records can mean an intended update failed to match them. Answer
questions, tell the assistant what to change or edit its draft in the model editor. If the draft
changed after the check, acceptance checks every record and relationship again first.
[Review the assistant's workbook design](/docs/guide/model/review-an-assistants-workbook-design/)
explains this review.

![Workbook proposal showing what the load does, its results by type and the choices before acceptance](/docs/screens/use-assistant-proposal.png)

*Above: the workbook proposal for the Graubünden reference data, showing What the load does
and the table of results by type. Below it, Questions marks the assumed answer, and the acceptance
bar explains that the checked records go into a new change set. Nothing is loaded or published yet.*

A words-only proposal that says **No change to the model.** uses **Accept**. It has no model
draft and prepares a change set on the workspace’s current release, installing and activating
nothing. A workbook proposal uses **Accept and load to change set**: the engine installs the model if it
changed and loads exactly the checked records and relationships into a change set as one batch,
without another assistant turn. Nothing is activated or published. If any item is refused,
none of the batch is loaded and its change set is discarded; read the reason and correct the
proposal. A release installed before a failed load can remain installed. Review and publish
the successful change set through the normal approval process. If it uses a different model
version, review offers migration and publication together; a model administrator with
publication permission previews it and confirms **Migrate and publish**. The assistant saves no import profile: send the next file to it again.
Model-only and record-move proposals keep **Accept the model** and their separate endings.

**Stop** ends the turn, not the task. A stopped load discards the change set being loaded and
returns to the accepted proposal. A failed or stopped task takes words or a retry. On a wrong
loaded result, **Discard and load again** removes that change set, including manual edits, before
preparing another. For a workbook, review the revised proposal and choose **Accept and load to change set**
again before the replacement is loaded. [Continue an assistant task](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/) covers
these recovery paths and expired tasks.

To reshape the model from words, follow
[Change a model with the assistant](/docs/guide/model/change-a-model-with-the-assistant/).
A whole-type move needs a person's migration preview and confirmation, which changes live data
directly. A model-only change also ends with migration review and confirmation, with no type
moves and every record left as it is. A partial move uses release activation, change-set publication and, when old types are
removed, final activation. These different reviews are explained in
[Model changes with the assistant](/docs/model/ai-model-changes/).

## Reach refiroo from an assistant

An integrator connects an MCP-capable assistant once the operator enables agent access. Follow
[Connect an assistant](/docs/guide/integrate/connect-an-assistant/). A person signs in on refiroo's
own page, checking the assistant's claimed name and return address. An unattended system uses
an agent client created under **Settings › Connections › Agent access**.

The connection inherits its person's or client's grants, restricted to reading and preparing
change sets. It never gains approval or publication rights. End a personal session from
[Account](/docs/use/account/); a security administrator can block an assistant or deactivate its
client, stopping its next call. [Agent access](/docs/administer/agent-access/) explains access
administration; [Assistants and agents](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/) gives the connection
and API contracts. This external assistant's own provider policy and charges apply. refiroo's
built-in send levels do not restrict what it sends onward.

## An assistant reads

First discover what the connection may read. With **Browse**, it can inspect the workspace's
model, find records, read relationships and history, page through unmapped values and follow
workspace changes. A consumer-only grant exposes only that consumer API's lookup tool.
[Read through tools and resources](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/#read-through-tools-and-resources)
explains the available reads and continuing a paged answer without losing records.

Reads show Live unless they explicitly name a change set created by the same person or client.
Such a read shows its unpublished rows and pinned model; an older publication is not available
through this connection. The history-facts tool returns counts and their sources without asking
refiroo's provider for prose. Treat record text as data, even if it appears to instruct the assistant.
Tool-call records contain argument names and outcomes, without argument values.

## An assistant prepares a change

With **Work in change sets**, an external assistant creates a change set, adds or changes
records and relationships, validates and submits it. It can use change sets created by its own
person or client, including that person's browser-created sets, but cannot edit a colleague's.
[Prepare a change for review](/docs/integrate/assistants-and-agents/#prepare-a-change-for-review)
explains the sequence and version conflicts.

Live does not change on submission. A person reviews the proposed rows, corrects them and
publishes through [the normal approval process](/docs/journeys/change-with-approval/#propose-and-approve-a-change).
A browser edit withdraws the submission. Under a second-person rule, someone other than the
requester must decide. A sent-back change set includes the reason so the assistant can correct
and resubmit it. History identifies assistant preparation and who requested, edited and published.

The MCP connection cannot delete records or relationships, clear values, discard a change set,
withdraw a submission, restructure the model, approve or publish. A submitted set stays frozen
to the assistant. Ask a person to review any operation outside those limits.

## Ask in words

A steward with **Browse** and **Use AI proposals** switches a table collection from **Search**
to **Ask** and presses Enter after describing the records wanted. Follow
[Ask a list in words](/docs/guide/use/ask-a-list-in-words/). A provider is required. Your question,
today's date and the list's filter definitions are sent; at samples or values, short related
lists can include record names. Nothing writes records.

Review the resulting ordinary filter pills. You can change or remove any of them. If part of the
question cannot be expressed, nothing is applied: dashed pills show the possible part, and
**Use these filters** accepts it explicitly. Ordering, who changed a record, and missing or
ambiguous record names need a revised question or manual work. A failed call leaves your words
and the earlier list in place.

![A question translated into editable filters on a table list](/docs/screens/use-ask-filters.png)

*Above: the reference Stops list after asking a question. Review the filters to check what the list answers.*

Ask uses the current Live, change-set or publication context. Created and Updated conditions
need Live. The switch is absent on trees, mapping grids and the Changes page. See
[Asking a list in words](/docs/use/ask-in-words/) for supported questions and limits.

## What changed in a period

A reader with **Browse** and **Use AI proposals** opens workspace **Activity** or a record's
**History**, chooses dates under **What changed** and selects **Explain this period**. Follow
[Explain a period in history](/docs/guide/use/explain-a-period-in-history/). Nothing is sent just
by opening the page. The provider receives counts and model labels; names of records, people,
change sets and files are included only at values. Requests can incur costs; the same facts are
reused for up to an hour. See [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for retention.

Read each statement's numbered sources, then use **Show them** to inspect the changes it counted.
The facts cover live changes, including publication, rather than counting unpublished row edits
as live work. A period without changes makes no provider request. If the provider fails, the
facts remain readable. A removed job has no link to open. The account can be wrong and is English
only. [History](/docs/use/history/#what-changed-in-a-period) explains periods and attribution.

## Reuse a checked layout or stop using AI

An assistant load saves no import profile. Send the next workbook of the same layout to the
assistant again. If you already have a separately saved import profile, the engine can check
and load a matching file without an assistant session. Follow [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/)
and inspect its current mapping and dry run. A saved-layout load can activate a changed draft
when the requester has **Model release**; that differs from the assistant session, which cannot
activate. Read the shown result and next steps rather than assuming every task ends the same way.

To stop a built-in task, [continue or discard it](/docs/guide/use/continue-an-assistant-task/)
with the unpublished-change consequences visible. To stop an external connection, end its
session or ask the security administrator to [manage agent access](/docs/guide/administer/manage-agent-access/).
The operator can disable future built-in help through [AI settings](/docs/run/ai/).
Disabling help does not undo published records or erase history; task retention and the outside
provider's retention are separate. Manual filters, modelling and file-loading paths remain
available within their own permissions and deployment switches.
guide/src/content/docs/journeys/shape-a-:
---
title: Shape a model
description: Connect model design, workbook loading, releases and workspace migrations.
reader: model-admin
---

These journeys are for model administrators shaping the types, fields, relationships and views
that people use. Applications are declared by the model; they can be changed, replaced or removed.
Start with [Models](/docs/model/models/) for the difference between a draft, an installed release
and the release running in a workspace.

Model authoring, model release and workspace administration permissions serve different purposes.
They do not automatically grant permission to read or change reference data. Each linked task
explains its required access and deployment settings.

## Create and activate an application-model release

A model administrator turns a reviewed design into the definitions a workspace runs.
[Releases](/docs/model/releases/) connects the lifecycle: create or import a draft, validate it,
compare its differences and stored-data compatibility, then install an immutable release.
[Install and activate a release](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/) takes that
release into the intended workspace. Saving, installing and activating are separate outcomes.

An incompatible release does not become active. Resolve its data problems or use the reviewed
[migration](#move-a-workspace-to-another-release) path. If another activation wins first, refresh
the state and review again. Use [Compare releases](/docs/guide/model/compare-releases/)
when checking differences, or [Export a release](/docs/guide/model/export-a-release/) to reuse it
elsewhere. Read-only inspection remains available when model administration is switched off.

## Administer workspaces

A workspace administrator, or an authorised integrator, creates a separate place for data,
gives it a stable key and a label, and chooses the release it runs.
[Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/) leads to
[Create a workspace](/docs/guide/model/create-a-workspace/) and
[Make a workspace the default](/docs/guide/model/make-a-workspace-the-default/).
Changing the default affects requests that omit a workspace; an explicit choice stays explicit.

When a workspace is no longer used, [retire or delete it](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-workspace/).
Retirement preserves reads and refuses changes. The default cannot be retired; deletion also
requires an empty workspace with no publications. A refusal names what still prevents deletion.
Choose another default or retain the workspace for reading as appropriate.

## Define a consumer API in the model

A model author defines the business objects other systems should read without exposing their
storage structure. Start with [Consumer APIs](/docs/model/consumer-apis/), then
[define a consumer API](/docs/guide/model/define-a-consumer-api/) over the chosen types, fields,
related records, lists, lookup rules and events. Validate each reference and review the generated
[schema and message example](/docs/guide/model/see-a-consumer-apis-documents/).

Compare the consumer contract before installing and activating the release. A breaking change
needs a higher contract version; activation refuses it otherwise. An operation is available only
when declared. Coordinate changed contracts with integrators, who can then
[read through the consumer API](/docs/guide/integrate/read-through-a-consumer-api/).

**Example:** the reference model's stops consumer API exposes stops with names and codes drawn
from connected records. Another model can expose entirely different business objects.

## Design a model in the editor

A model administrator [creates a model draft](/docs/guide/model/create-a-model-draft/), then uses
[the model editor](/docs/model/the-model-editor/) to shape applications, types, reusable fields,
relationships, navigation and pages. Each edit has issues and a history; inspect them as the model
grows and [undo or review steps](/docs/guide/model/undo-and-review-the-draft-history/) where needed.
Preview pages before installation, without writing reference data from the preview.

A draft can temporarily be invalid, but an invalid draft cannot be installed. Released keys are
stable; a removal or structural change affecting stored data can require migration. If a colleague
changes the draft first, review their steps before retrying your edit. Finish through
[installation and activation](/docs/guide/model/install-and-activate-a-release/), then work with
records under the changed model to check the result.

## Onboard a workbook

A model administrator turns a workbook into a reviewed model and a repeatable loading profile.
Read [Workbook onboarding](/docs/model/workbook-onboarding/), then
[start a draft from a workbook](/docs/guide/model/start-a-draft-from-a-workbook/).
Inspect sheets, tables and lists; accept, change or reject proposals, or map columns by hand.
[Map a column](/docs/guide/model/map-a-column/) and
[read lists in a sheet](/docs/guide/model/read-lists-in-a-sheet/) explain the choices.
A proposal does not apply itself.

[Check the workbook with a dry run](/docs/guide/model/check-a-workbook-with-a-dry-run/) to inspect
what every row would do without writing records. Resolve missing values and mapping problems,
install and activate the model, then [load into a change set](/docs/guide/model/load-a-workbook-into-a-change-set/).
Review its differences and publish. Installation saves definitions and the loading profile;
it does not make the file's records live.

## Load the next version of a workbook

A steward or model administrator uses the saved profile to repeat the load without rebuilding
the mapping. [Load the next version of a workbook](/docs/guide/use/load-the-next-version-of-a-workbook/)
connects uploading the next file, inspecting differences, accepting column renames or ignoring
new columns, and checking again. Read the report before loading into a new change set.

Missing records are reported and kept unless the profile explicitly deletes them. A deleting
load needs a change set so the removals and their relationships can be reviewed. A changed model
release can invalidate a profile binding; fix the named binding rather than loading around it.
Finish by [reviewing the changes](/docs/guide/use/review-what-a-change-set-changes/) and publishing.

**Example:** a newer workbook of stop names or external codes can correct existing records and
add others. A stop absent from that file is not automatically deleted.

## Run a workspace on a model of its own

A model administrator installs the desired release and
[creates a workspace on it](/docs/guide/model/create-a-workspace/) or
[changes an existing workspace's model](/docs/guide/model/change-a-workspaces-model/)
after its compatibility review. Other workspaces keep their models. Switching workspace changes
the available applications and views as well as the records; shared labels do not imply shared data.

To evolve that workspace's definitions, [edit its model](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-workspaces-model/)
and apply the reviewed draft there. A page built under a replaced release must reload before
saving. If one workspace's model cannot be served, inspect its explanation and recovery options;
other workspaces can remain available. [Releases](/docs/model/releases/) also explains retiring
unused choices and deleting releases that nothing refers to.

## Move a workspace to another release

A model administrator uses [Migrations](/docs/model/migrations/) when the target release needs
conversions or changes the existing data cannot adopt unchanged.
[Migrate a workspace](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) connects the preview, type and field
mapping, inspection of every loss, correction of blockers and explicit confirmation. Cancelling
changes nothing. The data conversion and release switch succeed together or neither does.

An intervening write makes the review stale: preview again instead of confirming an older result.
Open change sets stay on their release; move them separately or review a workspace migration with
publication as one operation. Existing publications keep their model and content. If a workspace
cannot open because its stored model uses an unsupported language version, follow the specific
recovery in [Managing workspaces](/docs/model/managing-workspaces/); an ordinary migration and
raising an unsupported stored release are different operations.

## Move data between workspaces whose models differ

A model administrator or steward needs a mapping between the source and target definitions,
rather than assuming record types mean the same thing. Start with
[Model mappings](/docs/model/model-mappings/), then
[move records to another model](/docs/guide/model/move-records-to-another-model/).
Complete the proposed mapping, choose the records, and inspect the dry run's created, updated and
refused items. Confirm a copy or move into the target's change set, then review and publish it.

A move also prepares reviewed deletion in the source; publish the target copy before that deletion.
Relationships whose other end stays behind are carried only when the counterpart can be found
in the target, otherwise they are dropped and reported. Matching and remembered counterparts let
later transfers update records rather than duplicate them. A changed mapping or release needs a
fresh review. Nothing rejected in the dry run should be treated as successfully moved.

## An account of a model change

A model administrator with **Model release** and **Use AI proposals** in the workspace can ask
for an explanation before activating a release or applying a draft. A configured AI provider
is required; enabling only the built-in assistant does not offer this account. Follow
[Explain a model change](/docs/guide/model/explain-a-model-change/).

Open the activation dialog or **Apply to this workspace** and read the compatibility checks.
Under **What this change does**, choose **Explain this change**. Nothing is sent before that
request. The provider receives the model's differences, rule failures, consumer-contract effects
and record counts, without record values or names. Requests can incur charges; the same facts
are reused for up to an hour. Call records remain; request text is kept only if enabled.
Read [AI and your data](/docs/use/ai-and-your-data/) for full access, disclosure, cost and retention rules.

Review the account and follow each numbered citation to the facts refiroo computed. These include
blocked activation and the counts of affected records, not a promise that the change is safe.
The explanation is English only, is not attached permanently to the release and takes no
follow-up question. It appears in activation and Apply, rather than installation or migration.
[Accounts of model changes](/docs/model/model-change-accounts/) explains its rules and limits.

![An account beside the model checks, with numbered citations and facts](/docs/screens/model-account-facts.png)

*Above: the Apply dialog for a change to the Graubünden reference model. The account cites the facts below it.*

If the provider fails, read the facts alone or choose **Try again**. Fix an invalid or newer draft
before asking again. Asking does not apply or activate anything, and an explanation cannot remove
a compatibility refusal. Continue through the normal activation review, or use
[the migration path](/docs/guide/model/migrate-a-workspace/) when the existing data needs conversion.

## Add types, fields and relationships

With **Model authoring**, [add a record type and fields](/docs/guide/model/add-a-record-type-and-fields/),
[reuse and change attributes](/docs/guide/model/reuse-and-change-attributes/) and
[add a relationship](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relationship/). A shared attribute change affects
all its attachments. Review required values, allowed parents and relationship candidates, then
[fix issues before installing](/docs/guide/model/fix-issues-before-installing/).
[Turn an attribute into a list](/docs/guide/model/turn-an-attribute-into-a-list/) when values
should become maintained records. Released values can need migration; a saved draft does not
populate that list or convert Live.

## Arrange navigation, views and record pages

[Find your way around the editor](/docs/guide/model/find-your-way-around-the-editor/), then
[arrange applications and views](/docs/guide/model/arrange-applications-and-views/) and
[group collections in navigation](/docs/guide/model/group-collections-in-navigation/).
[Add a view](/docs/guide/model/add-a-view/) for another way to read a collection, or
[add a relation matrix](/docs/guide/model/add-a-relation-matrix/) when its structure supports one.
Removing a navigation group keeps its collections; hiding a page panel keeps its stored values.

[Edit a record page](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-record-page/) to arrange fields and panels, and
[choose table columns, filters and sort](/docs/guide/model/choose-table-columns-filters-and-sort/)
for a view's defaults. [Preview a type](/docs/guide/model/preview-a-type/) against populated and
empty records before installation. Preview cannot write records. An invalid draft needs its
issues repaired first. [The specialist workbench](/docs/model/json-view/) owns supported
settings without visual forms; ask a specialist to
[edit that draft](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-draft-as-json/) where needed.

## Refine a draft without losing identity or colleagues' work

[Rename or re-key an element](/docs/guide/model/rename-or-re-key-an-element/) distinguishes a
label change from a stable identity: released keys are fixed even without records.
[Split, merge and move types](/docs/guide/model/split-merge-and-move-types/) reshapes definitions;
[remove an element](/docs/guide/model/remove-an-element/) first reviews affected uses and data.
Neither changes Live simply by saving the draft. Plan a migration when released data blocks a change.

[Work on a draft with others](/docs/guide/model/work-on-a-draft-with-others/) explains reviewing
a colleague's newer steps before retrying an edit. Use
[Undo and draft history](/docs/guide/model/undo-and-review-the-draft-history/) for an unwanted
saved step. [Delete a draft](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-draft/) only after preserving needed
work: its history and attached workbook go with it; installed releases stay.

## Recheck a workbook design or a saved mapping

[Propose again with a newer workbook](/docs/guide/model/propose-again-with-a-newer-workbook/)
keeps the distinction between design proposals, accepted draft edits and a fresh dry run.
Inspect changed columns and skipped sheets, then return to the normal loading and review path.

For transfers, [edit a mapping row](/docs/guide/model/edit-a-mapping-row/) and
[choose what moves](/docs/guide/model/choose-what-moves/) before reviewing a fresh complete dry
run. [Delete a model mapping](/docs/guide/model/delete-a-model-mapping/) only when future
transfers no longer need it; deletion does not undo earlier copies or moves.

## Maintain released contracts and definitions

[Raise a contract version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-contract-version/) before activating a
breaking consumer change, and coordinate it with callers. This does not raise the model language:
[Raise a model language version](/docs/guide/model/raise-a-model-language-version/) is the
separate review for a stored model outside the supported window. Keep retained publications and
their definitions in the recovery plan.

[Retire or delete a release](/docs/guide/model/retire-or-delete-a-release/) hides unused choices
or permanently removes an unreferenced release. Existing references can prevent deletion.
Retirement does not stop workspaces already using a release. Review current use rather than
treating an older version as automatically disposable.
